`app/src/covers.rs`:

```rs
//! Cover art: Steam's own cache first, then art rigcheck downloaded from
//! Steam's image CDN into `~/.cache/rigcheck/images/` (ROADMAP Phase 5).

use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::{Duration, SystemTime};

use iced::Task;
use iced::futures::channel::oneshot;
use rigcheck_net::{Allowlist, Client, RateLimiter, Retry};

use crate::Message;

pub struct Covers {
    /// Where Steam installs are looked for.
    home: PathBuf,
    /// `~/.cache/rigcheck/images`
    dir: PathBuf,
    /// Asked for in this session, found or not.
    asked: HashSet<u32>,
    /// One client for every download, so its rate limiter sees them all.
    cdn: Arc<Mutex<Option<Client>>>,
}

impl Covers {
    pub fn new(home: PathBuf, dir: PathBuf) -> Covers {
        Covers {
            home,
            dir,
            asked: HashSet::new(),
            cdn: Arc::default(),
        }
    }

    /// The cover for `app_id`, if Steam or rigcheck has one on disk.
    /// Showing a downloaded cover marks it used, for [`Covers::evict`].
    pub fn path(&self, app_id: u32) -> Option<PathBuf> {
        rigcheck_steam::cover_art(&self.home, app_id).or_else(|| {
            let downloaded = self.file(app_id);
            let file = std::fs::File::options()
                .write(true)
                .open(&downloaded)
                .ok()?;
            let _ = file.set_modified(SystemTime::now());
            Some(downloaded)
        })
    }

    /// Bytes the downloaded covers take.
    pub fn size(&self) -> u64 {
        self.downloaded().iter().map(|(_, bytes, _)| bytes).sum()
    }

    /// Deletes the least recently used downloaded covers until they take at
    /// most `limit` bytes (ROADMAP §7.1). Steam's own cache isn't touched.
    pub fn evict(&self, limit: u64) {
        let mut covers = self.downloaded();
        covers.sort_by_key(|(_, _, used)| *used);
        let mut size: u64 = covers.iter().map(|(_, bytes, _)| bytes).sum();
        for (path, bytes, _) in covers {
            if size <= limit {
                break;
            }
            if std::fs::remove_file(&path).is_ok() {
                size -= bytes;
            }
        }
    }

    /// Deletes every downloaded cover.
    pub fn clear(&self) {
        self.evict(0);
    }

    /// Each downloaded cover: its path, size and when it was last used.
    fn downloaded(&self) -> Vec<(PathBuf, u64, SystemTime)> {
        let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(&self.dir) else {
            return Vec::new();
        };
        entries
            .flatten()
            .filter(|entry| entry.path().extension().is_some_and(|ext| ext == "jpg"))
            .filter_map(|entry| {
                let meta = entry.metadata().ok()?;
                Some((entry.path(), meta.len(), meta.modified().ok()?))
            })
            .collect()
    }

    /// Keeps a downloaded cover. Written to a temp file and renamed, so a
    /// half-written image is never shown.
    pub fn save(&self, app_id: u32, jpeg: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<PathBuf> {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&self.dir)?;
        let file = self.file(app_id);
        let part = file.with_extension("jpg.part");
        std::fs::write(&part, jpeg)?;
        std::fs::rename(&part, &file)?;
        Ok(file)
    }

    /// Downloads the cover for `app_id` unless it's on disk or was already
    /// asked for in this session (a game without art isn't asked again).
    /// The answer comes back as [`Message::CoverFetched`]; nothing is sent
    /// until iced runs the task.
    pub fn fetch(&mut self, app_id: u32) -> Task<Message> {
        if self.path(app_id).is_some() || !self.asked.insert(app_id) {
            return Task::none();
        }
        let cdn = self.cdn.clone();
        Task::perform(
            async move {
                let (sender, receiver) = oneshot::channel();
                std::thread::spawn(move || {
                    let _ = sender.send(download(&cdn, app_id));
                });
                receiver
                    .await
                    .unwrap_or_else(|_| Err("the download stopped".to_owned()))
            },
            move |result| Message::CoverFetched(app_id, result),
        )
    }

    fn file(&self, app_id: u32) -> PathBuf {
        self.dir.join(format!("{app_id}.jpg"))
    }
}

/// Steam's 600×900 library art for `app_id`, the same image Steam caches.
fn download(cdn: &Mutex<Option<Client>>, app_id: u32) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let mut client = cdn.lock().map_err(|_| "the client broke".to_owned())?;
    if client.is_none() {
        // A CDN, so faster than the store API; still paced, since a big
        // library asks for hundreds at once.
        let limiter = RateLimiter::new(10, Duration::from_secs(1));
        let retry = Retry::new(1, Duration::from_secs(2));
        *client = Some(Client::new(Allowlist::app(), limiter, retry).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?);
    }
    let client = client.as_mut().expect("just built");
    let url = format!(
        "https://shared.akamai.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/{app_id}/library_600x900.jpg"
    );
    let mut jpeg = Vec::new();
    client
        .download(&url, &mut jpeg, |_| {})
        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    Ok(jpeg)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use tempfile::TempDir;

    const BG3: u32 = 1086940;

    fn covers(dir: &TempDir) -> Covers {
        Covers::new(dir.path().join("home"), dir.path().join("cache/images"))
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_downloaded_cover_is_found_again_after_a_restart() {
        let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(covers(&dir).path(BG3), None);

        covers(&dir).save(BG3, b"jpeg").unwrap();

        let found = covers(&dir).path(BG3).expect("saved");
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(found).unwrap(), b"jpeg");
    }

    #[test]
    fn steams_own_cover_comes_first() {
        let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
        let steams = dir
            .path()
            .join("home/.local/share/Steam/appcache/librarycache/1086940/library_600x900.jpg");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(steams.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(&steams, b"steam's").unwrap();
        covers(&dir).save(BG3, b"ours").unwrap();

        assert_eq!(covers(&dir).path(BG3), Some(steams));
    }

    #[test]
    fn each_cover_is_asked_for_once() {
        let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
        let mut covers = covers(&dir);

        assert_eq!(covers.fetch(BG3).units(), 1);
        assert_eq!(covers.fetch(BG3).units(), 0);

        covers.save(620, b"jpeg").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(covers.fetch(620).units(), 0, "already on disk");
    }

    /// Saves a 10-byte cover for each app, oldest use first: `n` seconds ago.
    fn used_at(covers: &Covers, uses: &[(u32, u64)]) {
        let now = std::time::SystemTime::now();
        for &(app_id, seconds_ago) in uses {
            let path = covers.save(app_id, b"0123456789").unwrap();
            std::fs::File::options()
                .write(true)
                .open(path)
                .unwrap()
                .set_modified(now - std::time::Duration::from_secs(seconds_ago))
                .unwrap();
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn eviction_removes_the_least_recently_used_covers_first() {
        let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
        let covers = covers(&dir);
        used_at(&covers, &[(1, 300), (2, 100), (3, 200)]);

        covers.evict(20);

        assert_eq!(covers.size(), 20);
        assert!(covers.path(1).is_none(), "used longest ago");
        assert!(covers.path(2).is_some() && covers.path(3).is_some());
    }

    #[test]
    fn showing_a_cover_counts_as_using_it() {
        let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
        let covers = covers(&dir);
        used_at(&covers, &[(1, 300), (2, 100)]);

        assert!(covers.path(1).is_some()); // shown just now
        covers.evict(10);

        assert!(covers.path(1).is_some());
        assert!(covers.path(2).is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn clearing_removes_every_downloaded_cover() {
        let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
        let covers = covers(&dir);
        used_at(&covers, &[(1, 0), (2, 0)]);

        covers.clear();

        assert_eq!(covers.size(), 0);
        assert!(covers.path(1).is_none());
    }
}
```

`app/src/download.rs`:

```rs
//! Downloading games.db when there isn't one yet (ROADMAP §7.3): read the
//! published manifest, stream `games.db.zst` to a temp file, then let
//! `rigcheck_gamedb::install` verify it and swap it in.

use std::fs::{self, File};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::Duration;

use iced::futures::{SinkExt, Stream, executor::block_on};
use iced::widget::{button, column, container, progress_bar, row, space, text};
use iced::{Element, Fill};
use rigcheck_gamedb::{Manifest, install};
use rigcheck_net::{Allowlist, Client, Error, RateLimiter, Retry};

use crate::Message;
use crate::i18n::I18n;
use crate::style::{BOLD, Colors};

const MANIFEST_URL: &str =
    "https://github.com/Glory42/RigCheck/releases/download/db-latest/manifest.json";

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Event {
    /// Bytes of `games.db.zst` downloaded so far, out of `total`.
    Progress {
        done: u64,
        total: u64,
    },
    Finished(Result<Fetched, Failure>),
}

/// How a download ended well.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Fetched {
    /// A new games.db is in place.
    Installed,
    /// The published games.db is the one already installed.
    UpToDate,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Failure {
    /// The published games.db uses a schema this build can't read.
    NeedsNewerApp,
    /// Offline, GitHub unreachable or a bad download. The text is for the log.
    Failed(String),
}

/// Where the download is, for the banner under the top bar.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Status {
    /// games.db is there; nothing to show.
    Done,
    /// The first download: there's no games.db yet.
    Running {
        done: u64,
        total: u64,
    },
    /// A newer games.db is downloading; the current one stays in use.
    Updating {
        done: u64,
        total: u64,
    },
    Failed(Failure),
}

/// Downloads games.db to `dest`, unless `installed` (its `db_version`) is
/// already the published one. The requests block, so they run on their own
/// thread and send their progress back through the stream.
pub fn games_db(dest: PathBuf, installed: Option<String>) -> impl Stream<Item = Event> {
    iced::stream::channel(8, async move |events| {
        std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let mut events = events;
            let result = fetch(&dest, installed.as_deref(), |done, total| {
                let _ = block_on(events.send(Event::Progress { done, total }));
            });
            let _ = block_on(events.send(Event::Finished(result)));
        });
    })
}

fn fetch(
    dest: &Path,
    installed: Option<&str>,
    mut progress: impl FnMut(u64, u64),
) -> Result<Fetched, Failure> {
    let failed = |error: Error| Failure::Failed(error.to_string());
    // Two requests in all, so pacing barely matters; retries cover a
    // GitHub hiccup.
    let limiter = RateLimiter::new(10, Duration::from_secs(1));
    let retry = Retry::new(2, Duration::from_secs(2));
    let mut client = Client::new(Allowlist::app(), limiter, retry).map_err(failed)?;
    let manifest =
        Manifest::from_json(&client.get_text(MANIFEST_URL).map_err(failed)?).map_err(failed)?;
    if manifest.needs_newer_app() {
        return Err(Failure::NeedsNewerApp);
    }
    if !manifest.is_update_for(installed) {
        return Ok(Fetched::UpToDate);
    }
    let part = dest.with_extension("db.zst.part");
    let result = (|| {
        if let Some(dir) = dest.parent() {
            fs::create_dir_all(dir)?;
        }
        let mut file = File::create(&part)?;
        client.download(&manifest.url, &mut file, |done| {
            progress(done, manifest.size_bytes)
        })?;
        install(&part, &manifest, dest)
    })();
    let _ = fs::remove_file(&part);
    result.map(|_| Fetched::Installed).map_err(failed)
}

/// The banner shown while games.db is missing, or `None` once it's there.
pub fn view(status: &Status, i18n: &I18n, colors: Colors) -> Option<Element<'static, Message>> {
    let content = match *status {
        Status::Done => return None,
        Status::Running { done, total } | Status::Updating { done, total } => column![
            text(i18n.t(if matches!(status, Status::Running { .. }) {
                "download-title"
            } else {
                "download-updating"
            }))
            .font(BOLD),
            progress_bar(0.0..=total.max(1) as f32, done as f32).girth(10),
            text(i18n.t_with(
                "download-progress",
                &[("done", &megabytes(done)), ("total", &megabytes(total))],
            ))
            .size(13),
        ],
        Status::Failed(Failure::Failed(_)) => column![
            row![
                text(i18n.t("download-failed")).font(BOLD),
                space::horizontal(),
                button(text(i18n.t("download-retry")).font(BOLD).size(13))
                    .padding([7, 12])
                    .style(colors.button(false))
                    .on_press(Message::RetryDownload),
            ]
            .align_y(iced::Center)
        ],
        Status::Failed(Failure::NeedsNewerApp) => {
            column![text(i18n.t("download-needs-newer-app")).font(BOLD)]
        }
    };
    Some(
        container(content.spacing(8))
            .padding(14)
            .width(Fill)
            .style(move |_| colors.boxed(colors.panel))
            .into(),
    )
}

/// `bytes` in megabytes with one decimal, e.g. "6.4".
fn megabytes(bytes: u64) -> String {
    format!("{:.1}", bytes as f64 / 1_000_000.0)
}
```

```rs
//! The game page: the verdict, why, and the requirements next to your PC.

use std::path::PathBuf;

use iced::widget::image::Handle;
use iced::widget::{Column, button, column, container, image, row, scrollable, text};
use iced::{Center, ContentFit, Element, Fill};
use rigcheck_core::{Blocker, Component, Level};
use rigcheck_gamedb::{Game, Tier};

use crate::i18n::I18n;
use crate::library::{Status, stamp};
use crate::style::{BOLD, Colors, level_color};
use crate::{Message, Page};

/// The user's machine as the page shows it.
pub struct Rig {
    pub cpu: String,
    pub gpu: String,
    pub ram: String,
    pub vram: String,
    pub api: String,
}

/// `back` is the tab the page was opened from.
#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
pub fn view<'a>(
    app_id: u32,
    name: String,
    // About a live lookup on Steam, under the header.
    note: Option<Element<'a, Message>>,
    record: Option<&'a Game>,
    status: &Status,
    rig: &Rig,
    cover: Option<&PathBuf>,
    back: Page,
    // The game picked to compare with, if any: its app ID and name.
    compare: Option<(u32, String)>,
    i18n: &I18n,
    colors: Colors,
) -> Element<'a, Message> {
    let mut compare_buttons = row![
        button(text(i18n.t("compare")).font(BOLD).size(13))
            .padding([7, 12])
            .style(colors.button(compare.as_ref().is_some_and(|(id, _)| *id == app_id)))
            .on_press(Message::PickToCompare(app_id))
    ]
    .spacing(12);
    if let Some((other, other_name)) = compare.filter(|(id, _)| *id != app_id) {
        compare_buttons = compare_buttons.push(
            button(
                text(i18n.t_with("compare-with", &[("name", &other_name)]))
                    .font(BOLD)
                    .size(13),
            )
            .padding([7, 12])
            .style(colors.button(false))
            .on_press(Message::Open(Page::Compare(other, app_id))),
        );
    }
    let (label, color) = stamp(status, i18n);
    let stamp = container(text(label).font(BOLD).size(18))
        .padding([4, 10])
        .style(move |_| container::Style {
            text_color: Some(colors.line),
            ..container::Style::default().background(color)
        });
    let back_label = match back {
        Page::Catalog => i18n.t("game-back-catalog"),
        _ => i18n.t("game-back"),
    };
    let back = button(text(back_label).font(BOLD).size(13))
        .padding([7, 12])
        .style(colors.button(false))
        .on_press(Message::Open(back));
    let mut header = row![].spacing(18).align_y(Center);
    if let Some(cover) = cover {
        header = header.push(
            image(Handle::from_path(cover))
                .width(110)
                .height(165)
                .content_fit(ContentFit::Cover),
        );
    }
    header = header.push(
        column![
            text(name).font(BOLD).size(24),
            row![
                stamp,
                button(text(i18n.t("game-store")).font(BOLD).size(13))
                    .padding([7, 12])
                    .style(colors.button(false))
                    .on_press(Message::OpenUrl(format!(
                        "https://store.steampowered.com/app/{app_id}/"
                    ))),
                compare_buttons,
            ]
            .spacing(12)
            .align_y(Center),
            text(reason(status, record, i18n)),
        ]
        .spacing(10),
    );

    let mut page = column![back, header].spacing(18);
    if let Some(note) = note {
        page = page.push(note);
    }
    if let Some(record) = record {
        page = page.push(requirements(record, status, rig, i18n, colors));
        page = page.push(linux(record, i18n, colors));
        if let Some(text) = steam_text(record, i18n, colors) {
            page = page.push(text);
        }
    }
    scrollable(page.padding([0, 6])).into()
}

/// One sentence on why the game got its stamp.
fn reason(status: &Status, record: Option<&Game>, i18n: &I18n) -> String {
    let verdict = match status {
        Status::Verdict(verdict) => verdict,
        Status::NoData => return i18n.t("why-no-data"),
        Status::NotChecked => return i18n.t("why-not-checked"),
        Status::Checking => return i18n.t("detecting-hardware"),
    };
    let part = |component| i18n.t(part_id(component));
    match (verdict.overall, verdict.bottleneck, verdict.blocker) {
        (Level::Blocked, _, Some(Blocker::Proton)) => i18n.t("why-blocked-proton"),
        (Level::Blocked, _, _) => {
            let name = record
                .and_then(|game| game.anticheat_name.clone())
                .unwrap_or_else(|| "Anti-cheat".to_owned());
            i18n.t_with("why-blocked-anticheat", &[("name", &name)])
        }
        (Level::Below, Some(component), _) => {
            i18n.t_with("why-below", &[("part", &part(component))])
        }
        (Level::Minimum, Some(component), _) => {
            i18n.t_with("why-minimum", &[("part", &part(component))])
        }
        (Level::Recommended, _, _) => i18n.t("why-recommended"),
        _ => i18n.t("why-unknown"),
    }
}

/// A size as Steam writes it: "256 MB", "8 GB", "1.5 GB".
fn size(mb: u32) -> String {
    match mb {
        mb if mb < 1024 => format!("{mb} MB"),
        mb if mb % 1024 == 0 => format!("{} GB", mb / 1024),
        mb => format!("{:.1} GB", f64::from(mb) / 1024.0),
    }
}

/// The requirement rows, in order.
pub const ROWS: [Component; 5] = [
    Component::Cpu,
    Component::Gpu,
    Component::Ram,
    Component::Vram,
    Component::GraphicsApi,
];

/// What `tier` asks of `component`, as Steam writes it; "—" if nothing.
pub fn requirement(tier: Option<&Tier>, component: Component) -> String {
    let text = tier.and_then(|tier| match component {
        Component::Cpu => tier.cpu_text.clone(),
        Component::Gpu => tier.gpu_text.clone(),
        Component::Ram => tier.ram_mb.map(size),
        Component::Vram => tier.vram_mb.map(size),
        Component::Storage => tier.storage_mb.map(size),
        Component::GraphicsApi => tier.directx.map(|dx| format!("DirectX {dx}")),
    });
    text.unwrap_or_else(|| "—".to_owned())
}

/// How this PC did on one row; "—" until there's a verdict.
pub fn result(status: &Status, component: Component, i18n: &I18n) -> String {
    let Status::Verdict(verdict) = status else {
        return "—".to_owned();
    };
    let level = verdict
        .components
        .iter()
        .find(|(compared, _)| *compared == component)
        .map(|(_, level)| *level);
    i18n.t(match level {
        Some(Level::Recommended) => "row-meets-recommended",
        Some(Level::Minimum) => "row-meets-minimum",
        Some(Level::Below) => "row-below-minimum",
        _ => "row-not-compared",
    })
}

/// ProtonDB, anti-cheat and Steam Deck: label and value.
pub fn linux_facts(game: &Game, i18n: &I18n) -> [(String, String); 3] {
    let proton = if game.linux.native {
        i18n.t("game-native-linux")
    } else {
        game.linux
            .protondb
            .map(|tier| format!("{tier:?}").to_uppercase())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "—".to_owned())
    };
    let anticheat = match (&game.anticheat_name, game.linux.anticheat) {
        (Some(name), Some(status)) => format!("{name}: {}", format!("{status:?}").to_uppercase()),
        _ => i18n.t("game-none"),
    };
    let deck = game
        .deck
        .clone()
        .map(|deck| deck.to_uppercase())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| "—".to_owned());
    [
        (i18n.t("game-protondb"), proton),
        (i18n.t("game-anticheat"), anticheat),
        (i18n.t("game-deck"), deck),
    ]
}

/// Your PC next to each tier, with the bottleneck row highlighted.
fn requirements<'a>(
    game: &'a Game,
    status: &Status,
    rig: &Rig,
    i18n: &I18n,
    colors: Colors,
) -> Element<'a, Message> {
    let verdict = match status {
        Status::Verdict(verdict) => Some(verdict),
        _ => None,
    };
    let bottleneck = verdict.and_then(|verdict| verdict.bottleneck);
    let (minimum, recommended) = (game.minimum.as_ref(), game.recommended.as_ref());
    let rows = ROWS.map(|component| {
        let yours = match component {
            Component::Cpu => rig.cpu.clone(),
            Component::Gpu => rig.gpu.clone(),
            Component::Ram => rig.ram.clone(),
            Component::Vram => rig.vram.clone(),
            _ => rig.api.clone(),
        };
        (component, yours)
    });

    let cell = |content: String, bold: bool, width: f32| {
        let label = text(content).size(13);
        container(if bold { label.font(BOLD) } else { label })
            .padding([8, 10])
            .width(iced::Length::FillPortion(width as u16))
    };
    let mut table = Column::new().push(
        row![
            cell(String::new(), true, 2.0),
            cell(i18n.t("game-your-pc"), true, 3.0),
            cell(i18n.t("game-minimum"), true, 4.0),
            cell(i18n.t("game-recommended"), true, 4.0),
            cell(i18n.t("game-result"), true, 3.0),
        ]
        .width(Fill),
    );
    for (component, yours) in rows {
        let highlight = bottleneck == Some(component);
        // The bottleneck in its level's color (red below the minimum), not
        // the accent, which is green in some themes and reads as "fine".
        let level = verdict
            .and_then(|verdict| verdict.components.iter().find(|(c, _)| *c == component))
            .map_or(Level::Below, |(_, level)| *level);
        let line = row![
            cell(i18n.t(row_id(component)), true, 2.0),
            cell(yours, highlight, 3.0),
            cell(requirement(minimum, component), false, 4.0),
            cell(requirement(recommended, component), false, 4.0),
            cell(result(status, component, i18n), true, 3.0),
        ]
        .width(Fill);
        table = table.push(container(line).style(move |_| {
            let background = if highlight {
                level_color(level)
            } else {
                colors.panel
            };
            container::Style {
                text_color: Some(if highlight { colors.line } else { colors.text }),
                ..container::Style::default().background(background)
            }
        }));
    }
    container(table)
        .padding(3)
        .width(Fill)
        .style(move |_| colors.boxed(colors.panel))
        .into()
}

/// The requirements as Steam's store page words them, next to each other,
/// so anything the parser missed is still there to read (ROADMAP §1.5).
/// `None` if the store page lists none.
fn steam_text<'a>(game: &'a Game, i18n: &I18n, colors: Colors) -> Option<Element<'a, Message>> {
    let tiers: Vec<&str> = [&game.minimum, &game.recommended]
        .into_iter()
        .filter_map(|tier| tier.as_ref()?.text.as_deref())
        .collect();
    if tiers.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    let columns = tiers.into_iter().map(|tier| {
        Column::with_children(tier.lines().map(|line| text(line).size(13).into()))
            .spacing(4)
            .width(Fill)
            .into()
    });
    Some(
        container(
            column![
                text(i18n.t("game-steam-text")).size(11).font(BOLD),
                row(columns).spacing(18),
            ]
            .spacing(10),
        )
        .padding(12)
        .width(Fill)
        .style(move |_| colors.boxed(colors.panel))
        .into(),
    )
}

/// ProtonDB, anti-cheat and Steam Deck boxes.
fn linux<'a>(game: &'a Game, i18n: &I18n, colors: Colors) -> Element<'a, Message> {
    let [proton, anticheat, deck] = linux_facts(game, i18n);
    let tile = |label: String, value: String| {
        container(column![text(label).size(11).font(BOLD), text(value).font(BOLD)].spacing(4))
            .padding(12)
            .width(Fill)
            .style(move |_| colors.boxed(colors.panel))
    };
    row![
        tile(proton.0, proton.1),
        tile(anticheat.0, anticheat.1),
        tile(deck.0, deck.1),
    ]
    .spacing(16)
    .into()
}

fn part_id(component: Component) -> &'static str {
    match component {
        Component::Cpu => "part-cpu",
        Component::Gpu => "part-gpu",
        Component::Ram => "part-ram",
        Component::Vram => "part-vram",
        Component::Storage => "part-storage",
        Component::GraphicsApi => "part-api",
    }
}

pub fn row_id(component: Component) -> &'static str {
    match component {
        Component::Cpu => "row-cpu",
        Component::Gpu => "row-gpu",
        Component::Ram => "row-ram",
        Component::Vram => "row-vram",
        Component::Storage => "row-storage",
        Component::GraphicsApi => "row-api",
    }
}
```

```rs
//! UI translations with Fluent (https://projectfluent.org). One `.ftl` file per
//! language in `app/i18n/`, built into the binary.

use fluent_bundle::{FluentArgs, FluentBundle, FluentResource};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use unic_langid::LanguageIdentifier;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Language {
    #[serde(rename = "en")]
    English,
    #[serde(rename = "tr")]
    Turkish,
    #[serde(rename = "de")]
    German,
}

impl Language {
    pub const ALL: [Language; 3] = [Language::English, Language::Turkish, Language::German];

    /// The language's name in that language, for the picker.
    pub fn native_name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Language::English => "ENGLISH",
            Language::Turkish => "TÜRKÇE",
            Language::German => "DEUTSCH",
        }
    }

    /// The IDs of every message in this language's file.
    #[cfg(test)]
    fn message_ids(self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &'static str> {
        self.ftl().lines().filter_map(|line| {
            let (id, _) = line.split_once(" =")?;
            let is_id = !id.is_empty() && !id.starts_with(['#', ' ', '\t']);
            is_id.then_some(id)
        })
    }

    fn ftl(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Language::English => include_str!("../i18n/en.ftl"),
            Language::Turkish => include_str!("../i18n/tr.ftl"),
            Language::German => include_str!("../i18n/de.ftl"),
        }
    }

    fn id(self) -> LanguageIdentifier {
        let tag = match self {
            Language::English => "en",
            Language::Turkish => "tr",
            Language::German => "de",
        };
        tag.parse().expect("valid language tag")
    }

    /// The language for a POSIX locale like `tr_TR.UTF-8`, as found in
    /// `$LC_ALL` / `$LC_MESSAGES` / `$LANG`. English if it's not one we have.
    pub fn from_locale(locale: Option<&str>) -> Language {
        match locale.and_then(|locale| locale.get(..2)) {
            Some("tr") => Language::Turkish,
            Some("de") => Language::German,
            _ => Language::English,
        }
    }
}

/// Looks up UI text in one language.
pub struct I18n {
    bundle: FluentBundle<FluentResource>,
}

impl I18n {
    /// Loads a built-in translation. The files ship inside the binary, so a
    /// broken one is a bug the tests catch, not a runtime error.
    pub fn new(language: Language) -> I18n {
        let resource = FluentResource::try_new(language.ftl().to_owned())
            .unwrap_or_else(|(_, errors)| panic!("{language:?} .ftl has errors: {errors:?}"));
        let mut bundle = FluentBundle::new(vec![language.id()]);
        // Fluent wraps arguments in Unicode isolation marks by default; plain
        // left-to-right text doesn't need them.
        bundle.set_use_isolating(false);
        bundle
            .add_resource(resource)
            .expect("message IDs are unique");
        I18n { bundle }
    }

    #[cfg(test)]
    fn has(&self, id: &str) -> bool {
        self.bundle.has_message(id)
    }

    /// The text for `id`.
    pub fn t(&self, id: &str) -> String {
        self.format(id, None)
    }

    /// The text for `id` with `{ $name }` arguments filled in.
    pub fn t_with(&self, id: &str, args: &[(&str, &str)]) -> String {
        let mut fluent_args = FluentArgs::new();
        for (name, value) in args {
            fluent_args.set(*name, *value);
        }
        self.format(id, Some(&fluent_args))
    }

    fn format(&self, id: &str, args: Option<&FluentArgs>) -> String {
        let Some(pattern) = self.bundle.get_message(id).and_then(|m| m.value()) else {
            return id.to_owned();
        };
        let mut errors = Vec::new();
        self.bundle
            .format_pattern(pattern, args, &mut errors)
            .into_owned()
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn every_language_has_every_english_message() {
        for language in Language::ALL {
            let i18n = I18n::new(language);
            for id in Language::English.message_ids() {
                assert!(i18n.has(id), "{language:?} is missing `{id}`");
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_system_locale_picks_the_language() {
        let cases = [
            (Some("tr_TR.UTF-8"), Language::Turkish),
            (Some("de_AT.UTF-8"), Language::German),
            (Some("en_US.UTF-8"), Language::English),
            (Some("fr_FR.UTF-8"), Language::English),
            (Some("C"), Language::English),
            (None, Language::English),
        ];
        for (locale, expected) in cases {
            assert_eq!(Language::from_locale(locale), expected, "{locale:?}");
        }
    }
}
```

`app/src/keys.rs`:

```rs
//! Keyboard shortcuts (ROADMAP Phase 8). iced's buttons can't take focus,
//! so keys stand in: tabs, the search box, going back, and moving through
//! the Catalog.

use iced::keyboard::{Key, Modifiers, key::Named};

/// What a key press asks for.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Shortcut {
    /// Ctrl+1…5: Library, Catalog, My Rig, Settings, About.
    Tab(u8),
    /// Ctrl+F: the page's search box.
    Search,
    /// Escape: back from a game page or a comparison.
    Back,
    /// Arrows and Page Up/Down: move the Catalog's highlighted row.
    Move(i32),
    /// Enter: open the highlighted row.
    Open,
}

/// The shortcut for a key no widget used, if it's one.
pub fn shortcut(key: &Key, modifiers: Modifiers) -> Option<Shortcut> {
    match key {
        Key::Named(Named::Escape) => Some(Shortcut::Back),
        Key::Named(Named::ArrowDown) => Some(Shortcut::Move(1)),
        Key::Named(Named::ArrowUp) => Some(Shortcut::Move(-1)),
        Key::Named(Named::PageDown) => Some(Shortcut::Move(PAGE)),
        Key::Named(Named::PageUp) => Some(Shortcut::Move(-PAGE)),
        Key::Named(Named::Enter) => Some(Shortcut::Open),
        Key::Character(c) if modifiers.command() => match c.as_str() {
            "f" => Some(Shortcut::Search),
            tab @ ("1" | "2" | "3" | "4" | "5") => tab.parse().ok().map(Shortcut::Tab),
            _ => None,
        },
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Rows Page Up/Down move.
const PAGE: i32 = 10;

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn character(c: &str) -> Key {
        Key::Character(c.into())
    }

    #[test]
    fn ctrl_and_a_number_switch_tabs() {
        assert_eq!(
            shortcut(&character("1"), Modifiers::CTRL),
            Some(Shortcut::Tab(1))
        );
        assert_eq!(
            shortcut(&character("5"), Modifiers::CTRL),
            Some(Shortcut::Tab(5))
        );
        assert_eq!(shortcut(&character("6"), Modifiers::CTRL), None);
        // A plain number is just a number.
        assert_eq!(shortcut(&character("2"), Modifiers::empty()), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn ctrl_f_searches_and_escape_goes_back() {
        assert_eq!(
            shortcut(&character("f"), Modifiers::CTRL),
            Some(Shortcut::Search)
        );
        assert_eq!(shortcut(&character("f"), Modifiers::empty()), None);
        assert_eq!(
            shortcut(&Key::Named(Named::Escape), Modifiers::empty()),
            Some(Shortcut::Back)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn arrows_and_pages_move_and_enter_opens() {
        let named = |key| shortcut(&Key::Named(key), Modifiers::empty());
        assert_eq!(named(Named::ArrowDown), Some(Shortcut::Move(1)));
        assert_eq!(named(Named::ArrowUp), Some(Shortcut::Move(-1)));
        assert_eq!(named(Named::PageDown), Some(Shortcut::Move(10)));
        assert_eq!(named(Named::PageUp), Some(Shortcut::Move(-10)));
        assert_eq!(named(Named::Enter), Some(Shortcut::Open));
    }
}
```

`app/src/library.rs`:

```rs
//! The Library page: installed games as cover tiles with verdict stamps.

use std::path::PathBuf;

use iced::widget::grid::Sizing;
use iced::widget::image::Handle;
use iced::widget::{
    Space, button, center, column, container, grid, image, row, scrollable, space, text, text_input,
};
use iced::{ContentFit, Element, Fill};
use rigcheck_core::{Level, Specs, Verdict};
use rigcheck_gamedb::Game;
use rigcheck_steam::InstalledGame;

use crate::i18n::I18n;
use crate::style::{BOLD, Colors, level_color};
use crate::{Message, Page};

/// Steam's library art is 600×900; tiles show it at this size.
const COVER_WIDTH: f32 = 164.0;
const COVER_HEIGHT: f32 = 246.0;

/// The search box's widget ID.
pub const SEARCH: &str = "library-search";

/// What the app knows about an installed game's chances.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Status {
    /// Waiting for hardware detection.
    Checking,
    /// Not in games.db.
    NoData,
    /// In games.db by name only: its store page hasn't been read yet.
    NotChecked,
    Verdict(Verdict),
}

/// The status of `game` (its games.db record, if any) on a PC with `specs`
/// (`None` until hardware detection finishes).
pub fn status(game: Option<&Game>, specs: Option<&Specs>) -> Status {
    match (game, specs) {
        (None, _) => Status::NoData,
        (Some(game), _) if !game.crawled => Status::NotChecked,
        (Some(_), None) => Status::Checking,
        (Some(game), Some(specs)) => Status::Verdict(game.verdict(specs)),
    }
}

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct Entry<'a> {
    pub game: &'a InstalledGame,
    pub status: Status,
    pub cover: Option<&'a PathBuf>,
}

/// `games` is `None` while Steam is being scanned.
/// How the Library lists games.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Order {
    #[default]
    Name,
    /// Grouped under each verdict, best first.
    Verdict,
}

/// `games` is `None` while Steam is being scanned.
pub fn view<'a>(
    games: Option<Vec<Entry<'a>>>,
    search: &str,
    order: Order,
    i18n: &I18n,
    colors: Colors,
) -> Element<'a, Message> {
    let Some(mut games) = games else {
        return center(text(i18n.t("library-scanning"))).into();
    };
    let search_box = text_input(&i18n.t("library-search"), search)
        .id(SEARCH)
        .on_input(Message::Search)
        // Enter opens the first game listed.
        .on_submit(Message::LibraryOpenFirst)
        .padding(10)
        .font(BOLD);
    let order_button = |id: &str, this: Order| {
        button(text(i18n.t(id)).font(BOLD).size(12))
            .padding([6, 10])
            .style(colors.button(order == this))
            .on_press(Message::LibraryOrder(this))
    };
    let mut header = row![
        order_button("library-by-name", Order::Name),
        order_button("library-by-verdict", Order::Verdict),
    ]
    .spacing(8)
    .align_y(iced::Center);
    if let Some(summary) = summary(&games, i18n) {
        header = header
            .push(space::horizontal())
            .push(text(summary).font(BOLD));
    }

    let query = search.to_lowercase();
    games.retain(|entry| entry.game.name.to_lowercase().contains(&query));
    games.sort_by_key(|entry| entry.game.name.to_lowercase());
    let content: Element<'a, Message> = match order {
        Order::Name => tiles(games, i18n, colors),
        Order::Verdict => {
            games.sort_by_key(|entry| rank(&entry.status));
            let mut groups = column![].spacing(18);
            for group in games.chunk_by(|a, b| rank(&a.status) == rank(&b.status)) {
                let (label, _) = stamp(&group[0].status, i18n);
                groups = groups.push(
                    text(format!("{label} · {}", group.len()))
                        .font(BOLD)
                        .size(16),
                );
                let group: Vec<Entry<'a>> = group.iter().map(Entry::clone).collect();
                groups = groups.push(tiles(group, i18n, colors));
            }
            groups.into()
        }
    };

    column![search_box, header, scrollable(content).height(Fill)]
        .spacing(16)
        .into()
}

/// The tile grid. Shrink: each tile is as tall as its content, not square.
fn tiles<'a>(games: Vec<Entry<'a>>, i18n: &I18n, colors: Colors) -> Element<'a, Message> {
    grid(games.into_iter().map(|entry| tile(entry, i18n, colors)))
        .fluid(COVER_WIDTH + 30.0)
        .height(Sizing::EvenlyDistribute(iced::Length::Shrink))
        .spacing(18)
        .into()
}

/// "38 of 42 installed games meet the recommended specs.", once every
/// game has a verdict or is known to have none.
fn summary(games: &[Entry], i18n: &I18n) -> Option<String> {
    if games.is_empty()
        || games
            .iter()
            .any(|entry| matches!(entry.status, Status::Checking))
    {
        return None;
    }
    let ready = games
        .iter()
        .filter(
            |entry| matches!(&entry.status, Status::Verdict(v) if v.overall == Level::Recommended),
        )
        .count();
    Some(i18n.t_with(
        "library-summary",
        &[
            ("ready", &ready.to_string()),
            ("total", &games.len().to_string()),
        ],
    ))
}

/// Best first: the order verdict groups are listed in.
fn rank(status: &Status) -> u8 {
    match status {
        Status::Verdict(verdict) => match verdict.overall {
            Level::Recommended => 0,
            Level::Minimum => 1,
            Level::Below => 2,
            Level::Blocked => 3,
            Level::Unknown => 4,
        },
        Status::NotChecked => 5,
        Status::NoData => 6,
        Status::Checking => 7,
    }
}

fn tile<'a>(entry: Entry<'a>, i18n: &I18n, colors: Colors) -> Element<'a, Message> {
    let cover: Element<'a, Message> = match entry.cover {
        // Exactly the art's 2:3 shape, so filling the box never spills over.
        Some(path) => image(Handle::from_path(path))
            .width(COVER_WIDTH)
            .height(COVER_HEIGHT)
            .content_fit(ContentFit::Cover)
            .into(),
        None => container(Space::new())
            .width(COVER_WIDTH)
            .height(COVER_HEIGHT)
            .style(move |_| container::Style::default().background(colors.panel2))
            .into(),
    };
    let (label, color) = stamp(&entry.status, i18n);
    // Fixed heights: the grid sizes cells to fit, and would squash the stamp.
    let stamp = container(text(label).font(BOLD).size(12))
        .padding([3, 6])
        .width(Fill)
        .height(24)
        .style(move |_| container::Style {
            text_color: Some(colors.line),
            ..container::Style::default().background(color)
        });
    let name = container(text(entry.game.name.clone()).font(BOLD).size(12))
        .padding([6, 6])
        .height(50);

    let tile = button(column![cover, stamp, name].width(COVER_WIDTH))
        .width(COVER_WIDTH + 6.0) // + the padding inside the outline
        .padding(3)
        .style(move |_, _| {
            let boxed = colors.boxed(colors.panel);
            button::Style {
                background: boxed.background,
                text_color: colors.text,
                border: boxed.border,
                shadow: boxed.shadow,
                snap: true,
            }
        })
        .on_press(Message::Open(Page::Game(entry.game.app_id)));
    // The grid stretches cells to its column width; the container takes that,
    // so the tile keeps the cover's width.
    container(tile).width(Fill).into()
}

/// The stamp's text and color.
pub fn stamp(status: &Status, i18n: &I18n) -> (String, iced::Color) {
    let level = match status {
        Status::Checking => return (i18n.t("stamp-checking"), level_color(Level::Unknown)),
        Status::NoData => return (i18n.t("stamp-no-data"), level_color(Level::Unknown)),
        Status::NotChecked => {
            return (i18n.t("stamp-not-checked"), level_color(Level::Unknown));
        }
        Status::Verdict(verdict) => verdict.overall,
    };
    let id = match level {
        Level::Recommended => "stamp-recommended",
        Level::Minimum => "stamp-minimum",
        Level::Below => "stamp-below",
        Level::Blocked => "stamp-blocked",
        Level::Unknown => "stamp-unknown",
    };
    (i18n.t(id), level_color(level))
}
```

`app/src/lookup.rs`:

```rs
//! Asking Steam about a game games.db hasn't checked yet (ROADMAP §6, §7.1):
//! one `appdetails` request for the app ID whose page was opened. The answer
//! is kept in fetched.db by the caller.

use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::Duration;

use iced::futures::channel::oneshot;
use iced::widget::{button, row, space, text};
use iced::{Element, Task};
use rigcheck_net::{Allowlist, Client, RateLimiter, Retry};

use crate::Message;
use crate::i18n::I18n;
use crate::style::{BOLD, Colors};

/// Where a lookup is, for the game page.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum State {
    Idle,
    Checking(u32),
    /// Offline, or Steam didn't answer.
    Failed(u32),
    /// Steam has no store page with requirements for it (DLC, delisted…).
    NoRequirements(u32),
}

/// One client for every lookup, so its rate limiter sees them all. Built on
/// first use.
#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub struct Steam(Arc<Mutex<Option<Client>>>);

impl Steam {
    /// Asks Steam about `app_id` on a background thread; the answer comes
    /// back as [`Message::SteamLookup`]. Nothing is sent until iced runs
    /// the task (tests drop it unrun, so they never reach the network).
    pub fn ask(&self, app_id: u32) -> Task<Message> {
        let steam = self.clone();
        Task::perform(
            async move {
                let (sender, receiver) = oneshot::channel();
                std::thread::spawn(move || {
                    let _ = sender.send(steam.get(app_id));
                });
                receiver
                    .await
                    .unwrap_or_else(|_| Err("the lookup stopped".to_owned()))
            },
            move |result| Message::SteamLookup(app_id, result),
        )
    }

    /// The `appdetails` JSON for `app_id`. Blocks, waiting its turn under
    /// the rate limit.
    fn get(&self, app_id: u32) -> Result<String, String> {
        let mut client = self.0.lock().map_err(|_| "the client broke".to_owned())?;
        if client.is_none() {
            // Well under Steam's ~200 requests per 5 minutes, even for
            // someone opening game after game.
            let limiter = RateLimiter::new(20, Duration::from_secs(60));
            let retry = Retry::new(1, Duration::from_secs(5));
            *client = Some(
                Client::new(Allowlist::app(), limiter, retry).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?,
            );
        }
        let client = client.as_mut().expect("just built");
        let url = format!(
            "https://store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails?appids={app_id}&l=english&cc=us"
        );
        client.get_text(&url).map_err(|error| error.to_string())
    }
}

/// A line for the page of `app_id` about its lookup, if there's one to show.
pub fn note(
    state: State,
    app_id: u32,
    i18n: &I18n,
    colors: Colors,
) -> Option<Element<'static, Message>> {
    let line = |id: &str| text(i18n.t(id)).font(BOLD);
    match state {
        State::Checking(id) if id == app_id => Some(line("lookup-checking").into()),
        State::NoRequirements(id) if id == app_id => Some(line("lookup-no-requirements").into()),
        State::Failed(id) if id == app_id => Some(
            row![
                line("lookup-failed"),
                space::horizontal(),
                button(text(i18n.t("download-retry")).font(BOLD).size(13))
                    .padding([7, 12])
                    .style(colors.button(false))
                    .on_press(Message::RetryLookup(app_id)),
            ]
            .align_y(iced::Center)
            .into(),
        ),
        _ => None,
    }
}
```

```rs
//! The rigcheck desktop app: an iced UI on top of the workspace crates.

mod about;
mod catalog;
mod compare;
mod covers;
mod download;
mod game_page;
mod i18n;
mod keys;
mod library;
mod lookup;
mod my_hardware;
mod overrides;
#[cfg(test)]
mod perf;
mod release;
#[cfg(test)]
mod screenshots;
mod settings;
mod settings_page;
mod style;
#[cfg(test)]
mod test_support;
mod whatif;

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use i18n::{I18n, Language};
use iced::widget::image::{FilterMethod, Handle};
use iced::widget::{
    button, center, column, combo_box, container, image, row, scrollable, space, text,
};
use iced::{Element, Fill, Size, Task, Theme, clipboard, window};
use rigcheck_core::{Catalog, Specs};
use rigcheck_gamedb::ingest::{Ingested, ingest};
use rigcheck_gamedb::{Game, GameDb};
use rigcheck_hardware::Hardware;
use rigcheck_steam::InstalledGame;
use settings::{Appearance, Settings};
```
