/// Reverse-DNS app ID. Wayland uses it to match the window with its .desktop file
/// (and so its icon); Flatpak uses it as the app ID.
const APP_ID: &str = "dev.gorkemkaryol.rigcheck";
const ICON_PNG: &[u8] = include_bytes!("../../assets/brand/icon-256.png");

fn main() -> iced::Result {
    let paths = Paths::from_xdg();
    let system_language = Language::from_locale(system_locale().as_deref());
    iced::application(
        move || App::new(paths.clone(), system_language),
        App::update,
        App::view,
    )
    .title("rigcheck")
    .theme(App::theme)
    .subscription(App::subscription)
    .window(window_settings())
    .run()
}

/// Where the app reads and writes. Tests point these at temp dirs.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
struct Paths {
    /// `settings.json`: ~/.config/rigcheck
    config: PathBuf,
    /// `games.db`: ~/.local/share/rigcheck
    data: PathBuf,
    /// `fetched.db`, live lookups: ~/.cache/rigcheck
    cache: PathBuf,
    /// Where Steam installs are looked for.
    home: PathBuf,
}

impl Paths {
    /// The XDG directories (ROADMAP §7.1), honoring `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` etc.
    fn from_xdg() -> Paths {
        let project = directories::ProjectDirs::from("dev", "gorkemkaryol", "rigcheck")
            .expect("a home directory");
        let base = directories::BaseDirs::new().expect("a home directory");
        Paths {
            config: project.config_dir().to_owned(),
            data: project.data_dir().to_owned(),
            cache: project.cache_dir().to_owned(),
            home: base.home_dir().to_owned(),
        }
    }

    #[cfg(test)]
    fn under(dir: &Path) -> Paths {
        Paths {
            config: dir.join("config"),
            data: dir.join("data"),
            cache: dir.join("cache"),
            home: dir.join("home"),
        }
    }
}

/// The locale for messages, the way POSIX picks it: `$LC_ALL`, then
/// `$LC_MESSAGES`, then `$LANG`.
fn system_locale() -> Option<String> {
    ["LC_ALL", "LC_MESSAGES", "LANG"]
        .into_iter()
        .filter_map(|name| std::env::var(name).ok())
        .find(|value| !value.is_empty())
}

fn window_settings() -> window::Settings {
    window::Settings {
        size: Size::new(1100.0, 720.0),
        min_size: Some(Size::new(640.0, 480.0)),
        icon: Some(
            window::icon::from_file_data(ICON_PNG, None).expect("bundled icon is a valid PNG"),
        ),
        platform_specific: window::settings::PlatformSpecific {
            application_id: APP_ID.to_owned(),
            ..Default::default()
        },
        ..Default::default()
    }
}

/// All UI state. Iced follows the Elm architecture: `view` draws the state,
/// user input becomes a `Message`, and `update` is the only place state changes.
struct App {
    paths: Paths,
    settings: Settings,
    /// Used when the user leaves Language on "System default".
    system_language: Language,
    /// Light or dark, for the System appearance.
    system_mode: iced::theme::Mode,
    i18n: I18n,
    page: Page,
    /// `None` until detection finishes.
    hardware: Option<Hardware>,
    /// `None` until games.db is downloaded; the Library then shows NO DATA.
    db: Option<GameDb>,
    download: download::Status,
    catalog: Catalog,
    /// `None` until Steam has been scanned.
    games: Option<Vec<InstalledGame>>,
    /// games.db records and cover art for the installed games.
    records: HashMap<u32, Game>,
    covers: HashMap<u32, PathBuf>,
    /// Where covers come from: Steam's cache, or downloads.
    art: covers::Covers,
    /// A newer rigcheck release's version, if one is out.
    newer_release: Option<String>,
    /// Sizes for Settings > Storage, refreshed when they can change.
    storage: settings_page::Storage,
    search: String,
    library_order: library::Order,
    catalog_list: catalog::List,
    /// Live lookups of games games.db hasn't checked; `None` if the cache
    /// directory can't be written.
    fetched: Option<GameDb>,
    steam: lookup::Steam,
    lookup: lookup::State,
    /// The open game page's record, and the tab it was opened from.
    opened: Option<Game>,
    opened_from: Page,
    override_choices: overrides::Choices,
    whatif: whatif::Picks,
    /// The game picked to compare with another.
    compare_pick: Option<u32>,
    whatif_choices: overrides::Choices,
}

/// The tabs in the top bar.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Page {
    Library,
    /// A game, by app ID: installed, or picked in the Catalog.
    Game(u32),
    Catalog,
    MyRig,
    Settings,
    About,
    /// Two games side by side, by app ID.
    Compare(u32, u32),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum Message {
    Open(Page),
    HardwareDetected(Hardware),
    GamesFound(Vec<InstalledGame>),
    Search(String),
    LibraryOrder(library::Order),
    /// Enter in the Library's search: open the first game listed.
    LibraryOpenFirst,
    Shortcut(keys::Shortcut),
    /// A hardware-table name, or `None` to go back to what was detected.
    OverrideGpu(Option<String>),
    OverrideCpu(Option<String>),
    CopyHardwareReport,
    /// My Rig > What if: hypothetical parts (`None` keeps your own).
    WhatIfGpu(Option<String>),
    WhatIfCpu(Option<String>),
    WhatIfRam(Option<u32>),
    /// Settings > Privacy: check for a new games.db only when asked.
    SetManualUpdates(bool),
    /// Settings > Storage: the image cache limit in MB.
    ImageCacheLimit(u32),
    CheckForUpdates,
    Redownload,
    ClearFetched,
    ClearImages,
    AppearanceSelected(Appearance),
    /// `None` picks "System default".
    LanguageSelected(Option<Language>),
    /// The system switched between light and dark (or said which it is).
    SystemTheme(iced::theme::Mode),
    Download(download::Event),
    CatalogSearch(String),
    CatalogFilter(catalog::Chip),
    /// Only games ProtonDB rates this or better; `None` for all.
    CatalogProtonDb(Option<rigcheck_core::ProtonTier>),
    /// The Catalog list's scroll position and height, in pixels.
    CatalogScrolled {
        offset: f32,
        height: f32,
    },
    RetryDownload,
    /// Opens a web page in the user's browser.
    OpenUrl(String),
    /// The latest release's version (`version.txt`), or why there's none.
    LatestRelease(Result<String, String>),
    /// Steam's `appdetails` answer for an app ID, or why there's none.
    SteamLookup(u32, Result<String, String>),
    RetryLookup(u32),
    /// A game page's COMPARE: remember this game (again: forget it).
    PickToCompare(u32),
    /// A cover downloaded from Steam's CDN, or why it couldn't be.
    CoverFetched(u32, Result<Vec<u8>, String>),
}

impl App {
    /// Starting state plus work to run right away. Detection reads files and
    /// runs `vulkaninfo`, so it runs as a `Task` on a background thread
    /// instead of freezing the window.
    fn new(paths: Paths, system_language: Language) -> (Self, Task<Message>) {
        let detect = Task::perform(
            async { rigcheck_hardware::detect(Path::new("/"), &rigcheck_hardware::System) },
            Message::HardwareDetected,
        );
        let home = paths.home.clone();
        let scan = Task::perform(
            async move { rigcheck_steam::installed_games(&home) },
            Message::GamesFound,
        );
        let db_path = paths.data.join("games.db");
        let db = db_path
            .exists()
            .then(|| GameDb::open(&db_path).ok())
            .flatten();
        let settings = Settings::load(&paths.config);
        let fetch = match &db {
            // A background update check (ROADMAP §7.3), unless turned off.
            Some(db) if !settings.manual_updates => {
                download_db(&paths.data, db.meta("db_version").ok().flatten())
            }
            Some(_) => Task::none(),
            None => download_db(&paths.data, None),
        };
        // Same setting: is there a newer rigcheck?
        let release_check = if settings.manual_updates {
            Task::none()
        } else {
            release::check()
        };
        let fetched = open_fetched(&paths.cache);
        let art = covers::Covers::new(paths.home.clone(), paths.cache.join("images"));
        art.evict(settings.image_cache_bytes());
        let mut app = App {
            override_choices: overrides::Choices::default(),
            whatif: whatif::Picks::default(),
            compare_pick: None,
            whatif_choices: overrides::Choices::default(),
            i18n: I18n::new(settings.language.unwrap_or(system_language)),
            settings,
            system_language,
            system_mode: iced::theme::Mode::None,
            paths,
            page: Page::Library,
            hardware: None,
            db: None,
            download: download::Status::Running { done: 0, total: 0 },
            catalog: Catalog::default(),
            games: None,
            records: HashMap::new(),
            covers: HashMap::new(),
            art,
            storage: settings_page::Storage::default(),
            newer_release: None,
            search: String::new(),
            library_order: library::Order::default(),
            catalog_list: catalog::List::default(),
            fetched,
            steam: lookup::Steam::default(),
            lookup: lookup::State::Idle,
            opened: None,
            opened_from: Page::Library,
        };
        if let Some(db) = db {
            app.use_db(db);
        }
        let system_mode = iced::system::theme().map(Message::SystemTheme);
        (
            app,
            Task::batch([detect, scan, fetch, release_check, system_mode]),
        )
    }

    /// Switches to `db`: its hardware table, and its records for the
    /// installed games found so far.
    fn use_db(&mut self, db: GameDb) {
        self.catalog = db.catalog().unwrap_or_default();
        let names = |entries: &[rigcheck_core::CatalogEntry]| {
            entries.iter().map(|entry| entry.name.clone()).collect()
        };
        self.override_choices = overrides::Choices {
            gpus: combo_box::State::new(names(self.catalog.gpus())),
            cpus: combo_box::State::new(names(self.catalog.cpus())),
        };
        self.whatif_choices = overrides::Choices {
            gpus: combo_box::State::new(names(self.catalog.gpus())),
            cpus: combo_box::State::new(names(self.catalog.cpus())),
        };
        self.catalog_list.refresh(&db);
        self.db = Some(db);
        self.download = download::Status::Done;
        self.load_records();
    }

    /// Looks up each installed game in games.db.
    fn load_records(&mut self) {
        let (Some(db), Some(games)) = (&self.db, &self.games) else {
            return;
        };
        self.records = games
            .iter()
            .filter_map(|game| Some((game.app_id, db.game(game.app_id).ok()??)))
            .collect();
    }

    /// What verdicts compare against: detected hardware scored with the
    /// hardware table. `None` until detection finishes.
    fn specs(&self) -> Option<Specs> {
        let mut specs = rigcheck_gamedb::specs(&self.catalog, self.hardware.as_ref()?);
        if let Some(gpu) = self.override_gpu() {
            specs.gpu = Some(gpu.to_ref());
            specs.vram_mb = gpu.vram_mb;
        }
        if let Some(cpu) = self.override_cpu() {
            specs.cpu = Some(cpu.to_ref());
        }
        Some(specs)
    }

    fn override_gpu(&self) -> Option<&rigcheck_core::CatalogEntry> {
        let name = self.settings.gpu_override.as_ref()?;
        self.catalog.gpus().iter().find(|entry| &entry.name == name)
    }

    fn override_cpu(&self) -> Option<&rigcheck_core::CatalogEntry> {
        let name = self.settings.cpu_override.as_ref()?;
        self.catalog.cpus().iter().find(|entry| &entry.name == name)
    }

    /// [`App::specs`] with the What if picks in place of your parts.
    fn what_if_specs(&self) -> Option<Specs> {
        let mut specs = self.specs()?;
        let find = |entries: &[rigcheck_core::CatalogEntry], name: &Option<String>| {
            let name = name.as_ref()?;
            entries.iter().find(|entry| &entry.name == name).cloned()
        };
        if let Some(gpu) = find(self.catalog.gpus(), &self.whatif.gpu) {
            specs.gpu = Some(gpu.to_ref());
            specs.vram_mb = gpu.vram_mb;
        }
        if let Some(cpu) = find(self.catalog.cpus(), &self.whatif.cpu) {
            specs.cpu = Some(cpu.to_ref());
        }
        if let Some(gb) = self.whatif.ram_gb {
            specs.ram_mb = Some(gb * 1024);
        }
        Some(specs)
    }

    /// "Cyberpunk 2077: TOO WEAK → LOW" for each installed game the What
    /// if picks would move to another stamp, by name.
    fn what_if_changes(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        let (now, then) = (self.specs(), self.what_if_specs());
        let mut games: Vec<&InstalledGame> = self.games.iter().flatten().collect();
        games.sort_by_key(|game| game.name.to_lowercase());
        games
            .into_iter()
            .filter_map(|game| {
                let record = self.records.get(&game.app_id);
                let (before, _) =
                    library::stamp(&library::status(record, now.as_ref()), &self.i18n);
                let (after, _) =
                    library::stamp(&library::status(record, then.as_ref()), &self.i18n);
                (before != after).then(|| format!("{}: {before} → {after}", game.name))
            })
            .collect()
    }

    /// Your PC as the game page shows it, named by the hardware table when possible.
    fn rig(&self) -> game_page::Rig {
        let unknown = || self.i18n.t("unknown");
        let Some(hardware) = &self.hardware else {
            return game_page::Rig {
                cpu: unknown(),
                gpu: unknown(),
                ram: unknown(),
                vram: unknown(),
                api: unknown(),
            };
        };
        let gpu = hardware.gaming_gpu();
        let vulkan = gpu.and_then(|gpu| gpu.vulkan.as_ref());
        let cpu = hardware.cpu.as_deref().map(|model| {
            self.catalog
                .match_cpus(model)
                .first()
                .map_or_else(|| model.to_owned(), |entry| entry.name.clone())
        });
        let gpu_name = gpu.and_then(|gpu| {
            self.catalog
                .gpu_by_pci(gpu.vendor_id, gpu.device_id)
                .map(|entry| entry.name.clone())
                .or_else(|| vulkan.map(|vulkan| vulkan.name.clone()))
        });
        let cpu = self.override_cpu().map(|entry| entry.name.clone()).or(cpu);
        let gpu_name = self
            .override_gpu()
            .map(|entry| entry.name.clone())
            .or(gpu_name);
        game_page::Rig {
            cpu: cpu.unwrap_or_else(unknown),
            gpu: gpu_name.unwrap_or_else(unknown),
            ram: hardware
                .ram_bytes
                .map(rigcheck_hardware::gib)
                .unwrap_or_else(unknown),
            vram: match gpu.map(|gpu| gpu.vram) {
                Some(rigcheck_hardware::Vram::Shared) => self.i18n.t("vram-shared"),
                Some(rigcheck_hardware::Vram::Dedicated(bytes)) => rigcheck_hardware::gib(bytes),
                _ => self.i18n.t("vram-unknown"),
            },
            api: vulkan.map_or_else(unknown, |vulkan| format!("Vulkan {}", vulkan.api_version)),
        }
    }

    fn status(&self, app_id: u32) -> library::Status {
        library::status(self.records.get(&app_id), self.specs().as_ref())
    }

    /// The appearance to draw with: the picked one, or the system's.
    fn appearance(&self) -> Appearance {
        self.settings.appearance.resolve(self.system_mode)
    }

    /// Follows the system switching between light and dark, and listens for
    /// shortcuts (keys no widget used).
    fn subscription(&self) -> iced::Subscription<Message> {
        iced::Subscription::batch([
            iced::system::theme_changes().map(Message::SystemTheme),
            iced::keyboard::listen().filter_map(key_shortcut),
        ])
    }

    fn shortcut(&mut self, shortcut: keys::Shortcut) -> Task<Message> {
        use keys::Shortcut;
        match (shortcut, self.page) {
            (Shortcut::Tab(n), _) => {
                let tabs = [
                    Page::Library,
                    Page::Catalog,
                    Page::MyRig,
                    Page::Settings,
                    Page::About,
                ];
                match tabs.get(usize::from(n).saturating_sub(1)) {
                    Some(&page) => self.update(Message::Open(page)),
                    None => Task::none(),
                }
            }
            (Shortcut::Search, Page::Library) => iced::widget::operation::focus(library::SEARCH),
            (Shortcut::Search, Page::Catalog) => iced::widget::operation::focus(catalog::SEARCH),
            (Shortcut::Back, Page::Game(_)) => self.update(Message::Open(self.opened_from)),
            (Shortcut::Back, Page::Compare(_, b)) => self.update(Message::Open(Page::Game(b))),
            (Shortcut::Move(by), Page::Catalog) => match &self.db {
                Some(db) => {
                    let offset = self.catalog_list.move_selection(by, db);
                    iced::widget::operation::scroll_to(
                        catalog::LIST,
                        iced::widget::operation::AbsoluteOffset {
                            x: None,
                            y: Some(offset),
                        },
                    )
                }
                None => Task::none(),
            },
            (Shortcut::Open, Page::Catalog) => {
                match self
                    .db
                    .as_ref()
                    .and_then(|db| self.catalog_list.selected_game(db))
                {
                    Some(app_id) => self.update(Message::Open(Page::Game(app_id))),
                    None => Task::none(),
                }
            }
            _ => Task::none(),
        }
    }

    fn theme(&self) -> Theme {
        self.appearance().theme()
    }

    fn update(&mut self, message: Message) -> Task<Message> {
        match message {
            Message::Open(Page::Settings) => {
                self.page = Page::Settings;
                self.refresh_storage();
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::SetManualUpdates(manual) => {
                self.settings.manual_updates = manual;
                self.save_settings();
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::ImageCacheLimit(mb) => {
                self.settings.image_cache_mb = Some(mb);
                self.save_settings();
                self.art.evict(self.settings.image_cache_bytes());
                self.refresh_storage();
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::CheckForUpdates | Message::Redownload => {
                let installed = match message {
                    Message::CheckForUpdates => self
                        .db
                        .as_ref()
                        .and_then(|db| db.meta("db_version").ok().flatten()),
                    _ => None,
                };
                self.download = match self.db {
                    Some(_) => download::Status::Updating { done: 0, total: 0 },
                    None => download::Status::Running { done: 0, total: 0 },
                };
                download_db(&self.paths.data, installed)
            }
            Message::ClearFetched => {
                // Closed first: the file is replaced by an empty one.
                self.fetched = None;
                let path = self.paths.cache.join("fetched.db");
                let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&path);
                self.fetched = open_fetched(&self.paths.cache);
                self.lookup = lookup::State::Idle;
                self.refresh_storage();
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::ClearImages => {
                self.art.clear();
                let images = self.paths.cache.join("images");
                self.covers.retain(|_, path| !path.starts_with(&images));
                self.refresh_storage();
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::Open(page) => {
                if let Page::Game(app_id) = page {
                    if !matches!(self.page, Page::Game(_)) {
                        self.opened_from = self.page;
                    }
                    self.page = page;
                    return self.open_game(app_id);
                }
                self.page = page;
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::LatestRelease(answer) => {
                // Offline, or no release yet: nothing to say.
                self.newer_release = answer
                    .ok()
                    .filter(|latest| release::is_newer(latest, env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")))
                    .map(|latest| latest.trim().to_owned());
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::SteamLookup(app_id, answer) => {
                self.looked_up(app_id, answer);
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::CoverFetched(app_id, jpeg) => {
                // A game without art is normal; only a failed save is worth a line.
                if let Ok(jpeg) = jpeg {
                    match self.art.save(app_id, &jpeg) {
                        Ok(path) => {
                            self.covers.insert(app_id, path);
                            self.art.evict(self.settings.image_cache_bytes());
                        }
                        Err(error) => eprintln!("couldn't keep the cover of {app_id}: {error}"),
                    }
                }
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::PickToCompare(app_id) => {
                self.compare_pick = (self.compare_pick != Some(app_id)).then_some(app_id);
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::RetryLookup(app_id) => {
                self.lookup = lookup::State::Checking(app_id);
                self.steam.ask(app_id)
            }
            Message::SystemTheme(mode) => {
                self.system_mode = mode;
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::AppearanceSelected(appearance) => {
                self.settings.appearance = appearance;
                self.save_settings();
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::LanguageSelected(language) => {
                self.settings.language = language;
                self.i18n = I18n::new(language.unwrap_or(self.system_language));
                self.save_settings();
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::HardwareDetected(hardware) => {
                self.hardware = Some(hardware);
                self.specs_changed();
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::GamesFound(games) => {
                let downloads: Vec<_> = games.iter().map(|game| self.cover(game.app_id)).collect();
                self.games = Some(games);
                self.load_records();
                Task::batch(downloads)
            }
            Message::LibraryOpenFirst => {
                let query = self.search.to_lowercase();
                let first = self
                    .games
                    .iter()
                    .flatten()
                    .filter(|game| game.name.to_lowercase().contains(&query))
                    .min_by_key(|game| game.name.to_lowercase());
                match first {
                    Some(game) => self.update(Message::Open(Page::Game(game.app_id))),
                    None => Task::none(),
                }
            }
            Message::Shortcut(shortcut) => self.shortcut(shortcut),
            Message::LibraryOrder(order) => {
                self.library_order = order;
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::Search(query) => {
                self.search = query;
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::OverrideGpu(name) => {
                self.settings.gpu_override = name;
                self.save_settings();
                self.specs_changed();
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::OverrideCpu(name) => {
                self.settings.cpu_override = name;
                self.save_settings();
                self.specs_changed();
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::Download(download::Event::Progress { done, total }) => {
                self.download = match self.db {
                    Some(_) => download::Status::Updating { done, total },
                    None => download::Status::Running { done, total },
                };
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::Download(download::Event::Finished(result)) => {
                let opened = result.and_then(|fetched| match fetched {
                    download::Fetched::UpToDate => Ok(None),
                    download::Fetched::Installed => GameDb::open(&self.paths.data.join("games.db"))
                        .map(Some)
                        .map_err(|error| download::Failure::Failed(error.to_string())),
                });
                self.download = download::Status::Done;
                match opened {
                    Ok(Some(db)) => self.use_db(db),
                    Ok(None) => {}
                    Err(failure) => {
                        eprintln!("couldn't download games.db: {failure:?}");
                        // A failed update keeps the current games.db in use;
                        // only say so if there's none, or the app is too old.
                        if self.db.is_none() || failure == download::Failure::NeedsNewerApp {
                            self.download = download::Status::Failed(failure);
                        }
                    }
                }
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::CatalogSearch(query) => match &self.db {
                Some(db) => {
                    self.catalog_list.search(query, db);
                    catalog_to_top()
                }
                None => Task::none(),
            },
            Message::CatalogProtonDb(lowest) => match &self.db {
                Some(db) => {
                    self.catalog_list.protondb(lowest, db);
                    catalog_to_top()
                }
                None => Task::none(),
            },
            Message::CatalogFilter(chip) => match &self.db {
                Some(db) => {
                    self.catalog_list.toggle(chip, self.specs(), db);
                    catalog_to_top()
                }
                None => Task::none(),
            },
            Message::CatalogScrolled { offset, height } => {
                if let Some(db) = &self.db {
                    self.catalog_list.scrolled(offset, height, db);
                }
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::OpenUrl(url) => {
                // The desktop's own "open this link": the app sends nothing.
                std::thread::spawn(move || {
                    if let Err(error) = std::process::Command::new("xdg-open").arg(&url).status() {
                        eprintln!("couldn't open {url}: {error}");
                    }
                });
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::RetryDownload => {
                self.download = download::Status::Running { done: 0, total: 0 };
                download_db(&self.paths.data, None)
            }
            Message::WhatIfGpu(name) => {
                self.whatif.gpu = name;
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::WhatIfCpu(name) => {
                self.whatif.cpu = name;
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::WhatIfRam(gb) => {
                self.whatif.ram_gb = gb;
                Task::none()
            }
            Message::CopyHardwareReport => match &self.hardware {
                Some(hardware) => clipboard::write(hardware.report()),
                None => Task::none(),
            },
        }
    }

    /// Opens a game's page: its cover and its record.
    fn open_game(&mut self, app_id: u32) -> Task<Message> {
        let cover = self.cover(app_id);
        Task::batch([cover, self.look_up(app_id)])
    }

    /// Shows `app_id`'s cover if one is on disk, else downloads it.
    fn cover(&mut self, app_id: u32) -> Task<Message> {
        if self.covers.contains_key(&app_id) {
            return Task::none();
        }
        match self.art.path(app_id) {
            Some(path) => {
                self.covers.insert(app_id, path);
                Task::none()
            }
            None => self.art.fetch(app_id),
        }
    }

    /// The record for the game page: games.db, then a recent lookup in
    /// fetched.db, else asks Steam (ROADMAP §7.1).
    fn look_up(&mut self, app_id: u32) -> Task<Message> {
        self.opened = self.db.as_ref().and_then(|db| db.game(app_id).ok()?);
        if self.opened.as_ref().is_some_and(|game| game.crawled) {
            return Task::none();
        }
        let (Some(_), Some(fetched)) = (&self.db, &self.fetched) else {
            return Task::none();
        };
        if let Some(game) = fetched.lookup(app_id, now()).ok().flatten() {
            self.opened = Some(game);
            return Task::none();
        }
        self.lookup = lookup::State::Checking(app_id);
        self.steam.ask(app_id)
    }

    /// Keeps Steam's answer about `app_id` in fetched.db and shows it.
    fn looked_up(&mut self, app_id: u32, answer: Result<String, String>) {
        let (Some(db), Some(fetched)) = (&self.db, &self.fetched) else {
            return;
        };
        let stored = answer.and_then(|json| {
            match ingest(app_id, &json).map_err(|error| error.to_string())? {
                Ingested::Game(record) => fetched
                    .store_lookup(*record, db, now())
                    .map(|()| true)
                    .map_err(|error| error.to_string()),
                Ingested::NotAGame { .. } | Ingested::Unavailable => Ok(false),
            }
        });
        self.lookup = match stored {
            Ok(true) => lookup::State::Idle,
            Ok(false) => lookup::State::NoRequirements(app_id),
            Err(error) => {
                eprintln!("couldn't look up {app_id} on Steam: {error}");
                lookup::State::Failed(app_id)
            }
        };
        if self.page == Page::Game(app_id) && self.lookup == lookup::State::Idle {
            self.opened = fetched.lookup(app_id, now()).ok().flatten();
        }
    }

    /// A game's record by the lookup order of its page (ROADMAP §7.1):
    /// games.db if checked, else a recent live lookup, else games.db's name.
    fn record(&self, app_id: u32) -> Option<Game> {
        let from_db = self.db.as_ref().and_then(|db| db.game(app_id).ok()?);
        if from_db.as_ref().is_some_and(|game| game.crawled) {
            return from_db;
        }
        self.fetched
            .as_ref()
            .and_then(|fetched| fetched.lookup(app_id, now()).ok()?)
            .or(from_db)
    }

    /// A game's name: its record's, else Steam's for an installed game.
    fn game_name(&self, app_id: u32) -> String {
        self.record(app_id)
            .map(|game| game.name)
            .or_else(|| {
                let installed = self
                    .games
                    .iter()
                    .flatten()
                    .find(|game| game.app_id == app_id);
                installed.map(|game| game.name.clone())
            })
            .unwrap_or_else(|| app_id.to_string())
    }

    /// Measures what Settings > Storage shows.
    fn refresh_storage(&mut self) {
        let size = |path: PathBuf| std::fs::metadata(path).map_or(0, |meta| meta.len());
        self.storage = settings_page::Storage {
            games_db: size(self.paths.data.join("games.db")),
            fetched_db: size(self.paths.cache.join("fetched.db")),
            images: self.art.size(),
        };
    }

    /// Lets the Catalog's CAN RUN use the current specs.
    fn specs_changed(&mut self) {
        let specs = self.specs();
        if let Some(db) = &self.db {
            self.catalog_list.use_specs(specs, db);
        }
    }

    fn save_settings(&self) {
        if let Err(error) = self.settings.save(&self.paths.config) {
            eprintln!("couldn't save settings: {error}");
        }
    }

    fn view(&self) -> Element<'_, Message> {
        let colors = self.appearance().colors();
        let i18n = &self.i18n;
        let page = match self.page {
            Page::Library => {
                let entries = self.games.as_ref().map(|games| {
                    games
                        .iter()
                        .map(|game| library::Entry {
                            game,
                            status: self.status(game.app_id),
                            cover: self.covers.get(&game.app_id),
                        })
                        .collect()
                });
                library::view(entries, &self.search, self.library_order, i18n, colors)
            }
            Page::Game(app_id) => {
                // Installed games that aren't in games.db have only Steam's name.
                let installed = self
                    .games
                    .iter()
                    .flatten()
                    .find(|game| game.app_id == app_id);
                let name = self
                    .opened
                    .as_ref()
                    .map(|game| game.name.clone())
                    .or_else(|| installed.map(|game| game.name.clone()));
                match name {
                    Some(name) => game_page::view(
                        app_id,
                        name,
                        lookup::note(self.lookup, app_id, i18n, colors),
                        self.opened.as_ref(),
                        &library::status(self.opened.as_ref(), self.specs().as_ref()),
                        &self.rig(),
                        self.covers.get(&app_id),
                        self.opened_from,
                        self.compare_pick
                            .map(|other| (other, self.game_name(other))),
                        i18n,
                        colors,
                    ),
                    None => coming_soon(i18n.t("tab-library"), i18n, colors),
                }
            }
            Page::Catalog => catalog::view(&self.catalog_list, self.specs().as_ref(), i18n, colors),
            Page::MyRig => match &self.hardware {
                Some(hardware) => {
                    let rig = self.rig();
                    let picked = overrides::Picked {
                        gpu: self.settings.gpu_override.as_ref(),
                        cpu: self.settings.cpu_override.as_ref(),
                        gpu_in_use: rig.gpu.clone(),
                        cpu_in_use: rig.cpu.clone(),
                    };
                    // Room on the right and bottom so hard shadows aren't clipped.
                    scrollable(
                        column![
                            my_hardware::view(hardware, i18n, colors),
                            overrides::view(&self.override_choices, picked, i18n, colors),
                            whatif::view(
                                &self.whatif_choices,
                                &self.whatif,
                                (rig.gpu, rig.cpu),
                                self.what_if_changes(),
                                i18n,
                                colors,
                            ),
                        ]
                        .spacing(18)
                        .padding([0, 6]),
                    )
                    .into()
                }
                None => center(text(i18n.t("detecting-hardware"))).into(),
            },
            Page::About => about::view(i18n, colors),
            Page::Compare(a, b) => {
                let side = |app_id| {
                    let record = self.record(app_id);
                    compare::Side {
                        app_id,
                        name: self.game_name(app_id),
                        status: library::status(record.as_ref(), self.specs().as_ref()),
                        record,
                    }
                };
                compare::view(side(a), side(b), i18n, colors)
            }
            Page::Settings => settings_page::view(&self.settings, self.storage, i18n, colors),
        };
        let mut body = column![].spacing(18);
        if let Some(banner) = download::view(&self.download, i18n, colors) {
            body = body.push(banner);
        }
        if let Some(version) = &self.newer_release {
            body = body.push(release::notice(version, i18n, colors));
        }
        column![
            self.top_bar(colors),
            container(body.push(page))
                .padding(18)
                .width(Fill)
                .height(Fill),
        ]
        .into()
    }

    /// Design D's top bar: pixel logo on the left, tabs on the right.
    fn top_bar(&self, colors: Colors) -> Element<'_, Message> {
        let tab = |id: &str, page: Page| {
            button(text(self.i18n.t(id)).font(BOLD).size(13))
                .padding([7, 12])
                .style(colors.button(
                    self.page == page
                        || (page == self.opened_from && matches!(self.page, Page::Game(_))),
                ))
                .on_press(Message::Open(page))
        };
        // One handle for the app's life: `from_bytes` gives every handle a
        // new ID, so a fresh one each redraw is a new image to decode.
        static LOGO: std::sync::LazyLock<Handle> =
            std::sync::LazyLock::new(|| Handle::from_bytes(ICON_PNG));
        let logo = image(LOGO.clone())
            .width(36)
            .height(36)
            .filter_method(FilterMethod::Nearest); // keep the pixel art crisp
        let bar = row![
            logo,
            text("RIGCHECK").font(BOLD).size(18),
            space::horizontal(),
            tab("tab-library", Page::Library),
            tab("tab-catalog", Page::Catalog),
            tab("tab-my-rig", Page::MyRig),
            tab("tab-settings", Page::Settings),
            tab("tab-about", Page::About),
        ]
        .spacing(10)
        .align_y(iced::Center);
        let bar = container(bar)
            .padding([12, 18])
            .width(Fill)
            .style(move |_| container::Style {
                text_color: Some(colors.text),
                ..container::Style::default().background(colors.hud)
            });
        let rule = container(space::vertical())
            .width(Fill)
            .height(4)
            .style(move |_| container::Style::default().background(colors.rule));
        column![bar, rule].into()
    }
}

/// fetched.db in `dir`, created on first use.
fn open_fetched(dir: &Path) -> Option<GameDb> {
    let path = dir.join("fetched.db");
    let opened = if path.exists() {
        GameDb::open(&path)
    } else {
        std::fs::create_dir_all(dir)
            .map_err(Into::into)
            .and_then(|()| GameDb::create(&path))
    };
    opened
        .inspect_err(|error| eprintln!("couldn't open fetched.db: {error}"))
        .ok()
}

/// Seconds since 1970, the way games.db and fetched.db store times.
fn now() -> i64 {
    std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map_or(0, |elapsed| elapsed.as_secs() as i64)
}

/// A key press no widget used, as a shortcut message.
fn key_shortcut(event: iced::keyboard::Event) -> Option<Message> {
    match event {
        iced::keyboard::Event::KeyPressed { key, modifiers, .. } => {
            keys::shortcut(&key, modifiers).map(Message::Shortcut)
        }
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Scrolls the Catalog list back to its first row.
fn catalog_to_top() -> Task<Message> {
    iced::widget::operation::snap_to(
        catalog::LIST,
        iced::widget::operation::RelativeOffset::START,
    )
}

/// Downloads games.db into `data`, reporting progress as messages.
/// Downloads games.db into `data` unless `installed` is the published
/// build, reporting progress as messages.
fn download_db(data: &Path, installed: Option<String>) -> Task<Message> {
    Task::run(
        download::games_db(data.join("games.db"), installed),
        Message::Download,
    )
}

/// Placeholder for pages that later phases build.
fn coming_soon(title: String, i18n: &I18n, colors: Colors) -> Element<'static, Message> {
    center(
        container(column![text(title).font(BOLD).size(20), text(i18n.t("coming-soon"))].spacing(6))
            .padding(18)
            .style(move |_| colors.boxed(colors.panel)),
    )
    .into()
}

    }

    fn shows(app: &App, text: &str) -> bool {
        iced_test::simulator(app.view()).find(text).is_ok()
    }

    /// Clicks the widget showing `label` and runs the messages it produces.
    fn click(app: &mut App, label: &str) {
        let mut ui = iced_test::simulator(app.view());
        if let Err(error) = ui.click(label) {
            panic!("couldn't click {label:?}: {error}");
        }
        for message in ui.into_messages() {
            let _ = app.update(message);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn says_it_is_detecting_hardware_at_startup() {
        let config = TempDir::new().unwrap();
        let (mut app, _) = App::new(Paths::under(config.path()), Language::English);

        click(&mut app, "MY RIG");

        assert!(shows(&app, "Detecting your hardware…"));
    }

    /// An app on the AMD laptop with Cyberpunk 2077 and OMORI installed.
    fn library_app(dir: &TempDir) -> App {
        let paths = Paths::under(dir.path());
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&paths.data).unwrap();
        GameDb::create_seed(&paths.data.join("games.db")).unwrap();
        let (mut app, _) = App::new(Paths::under(dir.path()), Language::English);
        let _ = app.update(Message::HardwareDetected(test_support::amd_laptop()));
        let _ = app.update(Message::GamesFound(vec![
            test_support::installed(1091500, "Cyberpunk 2077"),
            test_support::installed(1150690, "OMORI"),
        ]));
        app
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_library_shows_each_installed_game_with_its_verdict() {
        let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
        let app = library_app(&dir);

        for text in ["Cyberpunk 2077", "TOO WEAK", "OMORI", "READY"] {
            assert!(shows(&app, text), "{text} not shown");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn clicking_a_game_opens_its_page() {
        let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
        let mut app = library_app(&dir);

        click(&mut app, "Cyberpunk 2077");

        for text in [
            "Your GPU is below the minimum.",
            "GeForce GTX 1060 6GB or Radeon RX 580 8GB or Arc A380",
            "Radeon Vega 7 (Ryzen 5000/7000U)",
            "PLATINUM",
        ] {
            assert!(shows(&app, text), "{text} not shown");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn overriding_the_gpu_is_saved_shown_and_used_for_verdicts() {
        let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
        let mut app = library_app(&dir);
        assert!(shows(&app, "TOO WEAK")); // Cyberpunk on the iGPU

        click(&mut app, "MY RIG");
        let mut ui = iced_test::simulator(app.view());
        ui.click(iced::widget::Id::new(overrides::GPU)).unwrap();
        ui.typewrite("RTX 3060");
        // Enter picks the highlighted match, as it does for keyboard users.
        ui.tap_key(iced::keyboard::key::Named::Enter);
        for message in ui.into_messages() {
            let _ = app.update(message);
        }

        let saved = Settings::load(&Paths::under(dir.path()).config);
        assert_eq!(saved.gpu_override.as_deref(), Some("GeForce RTX 3060"));
        assert!(shows(&app, "GeForce RTX 3060"));
        click(&mut app, "LIBRARY");
        assert!(!shows(&app, "TOO WEAK"));
    }

        let mut ui = iced_test::simulator(app.view());
        ui.click(iced::widget::Id::new(library::SEARCH)).unwrap();

    /// The seed with popularities (Cyberpunk 2077 most popular, then OMORI),
    /// plus a game the pipeline only knows the name of.
    fn catalog_app(dir: &TempDir) -> App {
        let paths = Paths::under(dir.path());
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&paths.data).unwrap();
        let db = GameDb::create_seed(&paths.data.join("games.db")).unwrap();
        db.store_names(&[(30, "Day of Defeat")]).unwrap();
        db.set_protondb(&[
            (1091500, None, 3000),
            (1150690, None, 2000),
            (30, None, 1000),
        ])
        .unwrap();
        db.rebuild_search().unwrap();
        let (mut app, _) = App::new(paths, Language::English);
        let _ = app.update(Message::HardwareDetected(test_support::amd_laptop()));
        click(&mut app, "CATALOG");
        app
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_game_page_shows_steams_requirement_text() {
        let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
        let mut app = library_app(&dir);

        click(&mut app, "OMORI");

        // From OMORI's store page in the requirement corpus.
        for line in [
            "Memory: 4 GB RAM",
            "Memory: 8 GB RAM",
            "Additional Notes: 1280x720 display is recommended at x2 resolution but is not required",

    const BG3: u32 = 1086940;

    /// A games.db that knows Baldur's Gate 3 only by name, on the AMD laptop.
    fn lookup_app(dir: &TempDir) -> App {
        let paths = Paths::under(dir.path());
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&paths.data).unwrap();
        let db = GameDb::create(&paths.data.join("games.db")).unwrap();
        let table = include_str!("../../data/hardware.toml");
        db.store_catalog(&Catalog::from_toml(table).unwrap())
            .unwrap();
        db.store_names(&[
            (BG3, "Baldur's Gate 3"),
            (2138330, "Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty"),
        ])
        .unwrap();
        let (mut app, _) = App::new(paths, Language::English);
        let _ = app.update(Message::HardwareDetected(test_support::amd_laptop()));
        app
    }

    /// Steam's saved `appdetails` response for `app_id`.
    fn steam_says(app_id: u32) -> Message {
        let path = format!("../data/fixtures/appdetails/{app_id}.json");
        Message::SteamLookup(app_id, Ok(std::fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap()))
    }

    #[test]

        assert!(shows(&app, "Checking Steam…"));

        let _ = app.update(steam_says(BG3));

        // Radeon Vega 7 (32) against the RX 480 (95) in data/hardware.toml.

        assert!(!shows(&app, "Downloading the game database…"));

        new.set_protondb(&[(1150690, Some(rigcheck_core::ProtonTier::Borked), 10)])
            .unwrap();
        let _ = app.update(Message::Download(download::Event::Finished(Ok(

        assert!(!shows(&app, "Updating the game database…"));

            None

        click(&mut app, "LIBRARY");

`app/src/my_hardware.rs`:

```rs
//! The My Rig page: what rigcheck detected about this machine, drawn as
//! design D's "character sheet".

use iced::widget::{Column, button, column, container, row, space, text};
use iced::{Center, Element, Fill};
use rigcheck_hardware::{Hardware, Vram, gib};

use crate::Message;
use crate::i18n::I18n;
use crate::style::{BOLD, Colors};

pub fn view<'a>(hardware: &'a Hardware, i18n: &I18n, colors: Colors) -> Element<'a, Message> {
    let unknown = || i18n.t("unknown");
    let mut rows = vec![
        (
            "CPU".to_owned(),
            hardware.cpu.clone().unwrap_or_else(unknown),
        ),
        (
            "RAM".to_owned(),
            hardware.ram_bytes.map(gib).unwrap_or_else(unknown),
        ),
    ];
    let mut notes = Vec::new();
    for gpu in &hardware.gpus {
        let name = gpu.vulkan.as_ref().map_or_else(
            || {
                let name = i18n.t("unknown-gpu");
                format!("{name} [{:04x}:{:04x}]", gpu.vendor_id, gpu.device_id)
            },
            |vulkan| vulkan.name.clone(),
        );
        let memory = match gpu.vram {
            Vram::Shared => i18n.t("vram-shared"),
            Vram::Dedicated(bytes) => i18n.t_with("vram-dedicated", &[("size", &gib(bytes))]),
            Vram::Unknown => i18n.t("vram-unknown"),
        };
        rows.push(("GPU".to_owned(), name));
        rows.push((i18n.t("label-video-memory"), memory));
        if let Some(vulkan) = &gpu.vulkan {
            rows.push((
                i18n.t("label-vulkan"),
                format!("Vulkan {}, {}", vulkan.api_version, vulkan.driver),
            ));
        }
        if gpu.kernel_driver.as_deref() == Some("nouveau") {
            notes.push(i18n.t("note-nouveau"));
        }
    }
    if hardware.gpus.iter().any(|gpu| gpu.vulkan.is_none()) {
        notes.push(i18n.t("note-no-vulkan"));
    }
    rows.push((
        i18n.t("label-distro"),
        hardware.distro.clone().unwrap_or_else(unknown),
    ));
    rows.push((
        i18n.t("label-kernel"),
        hardware.kernel.clone().unwrap_or_else(unknown),
    ));

    let header = row![
        text(i18n.t("my-rig-title")).font(BOLD).size(20),
        space::horizontal(),
        button(text(i18n.t("copy-as-text")).font(BOLD).size(13))
            .padding([7, 12])
            .style(colors.button(true))
            .on_press(Message::CopyHardwareReport),
    ]
    .align_y(Center);
    let sheet = container(Column::with_children(
        rows.into_iter()
            .map(|(label, value)| sheet_row(label, value, colors)),
    ))
    .padding(3) // the outline's width, so cells don't paint over it
    .style(move |_| colors.boxed(colors.panel));

    let mut page = column![header, sheet].spacing(18);
    for note in notes {
        page = page.push(
            container(text(note))
                .padding(12)
                .width(Fill)
                .style(move |_| colors.boxed(colors.panel2)),
        );
    }
    page.into()
}

/// One line of the sheet: a bold label cell and its value.
fn sheet_row(label: String, value: String, colors: Colors) -> Element<'static, Message> {
    row![
        container(text(label).font(BOLD))
            .width(170)
            .padding([10, 14])
            .style(move |_| container::Style::default().background(colors.panel2)),
        container(text(value)).padding([10, 14]).width(Fill),
    ]
    .into()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use rigcheck_hardware::{Gpu, Hardware, Vram, VulkanDevice};

    fn laptop() -> Hardware {
        Hardware {
            cpu: Some("AMD Ryzen 5 7530U with Radeon Graphics".to_owned()),
            ram_bytes: Some(15_746_968 * 1024),
            gpus: vec![Gpu {
                vendor_id: 0x1002,
                device_id: 0x15e7,
                kernel_driver: Some("amdgpu".to_owned()),
                vram: Vram::Shared,
                vulkan: Some(VulkanDevice {
                    name: "AMD Radeon Graphics (RADV RENOIR)".to_owned(),
                    api_version: "1.4.354".to_owned(),
                    driver: "Mesa 26.2.6-arch1.1".to_owned(),
                    integrated: true,
                }),
            }],
            distro: Some("Arch Linux".to_owned()),
            kernel: Some("7.2.11-arch1-1".to_owned()),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn shows_the_detected_hardware() {
        let hardware = laptop();
        let mut ui = iced_test::simulator(super::view(
            &hardware,
            &crate::i18n::I18n::new(crate::i18n::Language::English),
            crate::settings::Appearance::Paper.colors(),
        ));

        for value in [
            "AMD Ryzen 5 7530U with Radeon Graphics",
            "15.0 GiB",
            "AMD Radeon Graphics (RADV RENOIR)",
            "Arch Linux",
            "7.2.11-arch1-1",
        ] {
            assert!(ui.find(value).is_ok(), "{value} not shown");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn hints_at_vulkan_tools_when_vulkan_is_missing() {
        let mut hardware = laptop();
        hardware.gpus[0].vulkan = None;
        hardware.gpus[0].vram = Vram::Unknown;
        let mut ui = iced_test::simulator(super::view(
            &hardware,
            &crate::i18n::I18n::new(crate::i18n::Language::English),
            crate::settings::Appearance::Paper.colors(),
        ));

        for value in [
            "Unknown GPU [1002:15e7]",
            "VRAM unknown",
            "Vulkan wasn't detected. Install vulkan-tools (it provides vulkaninfo) and restart rigcheck.",
        ] {
            assert!(ui.find(value).is_ok(), "{value} not shown");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn warns_about_the_nouveau_driver() {
        let mut hardware = laptop();
        hardware.gpus[0].kernel_driver = Some("nouveau".to_owned());
        let mut ui = iced_test::simulator(super::view(
            &hardware,
            &crate::i18n::I18n::new(crate::i18n::Language::English),
            crate::settings::Appearance::Paper.colors(),
        ));

        assert!(ui.find(NOUVEAU_WARNING).is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn no_nouveau_warning_with_other_drivers() {
        let hardware = laptop();
        let mut ui = iced_test::simulator(super::view(
            &hardware,
            &crate::i18n::I18n::new(crate::i18n::Language::English),
            crate::settings::Appearance::Paper.colors(),
        ));

        assert!(ui.find(NOUVEAU_WARNING).is_err());
    }

    const NOUVEAU_WARNING: &str = "This GPU uses the open-source nouveau driver, which runs most 3D games poorly. Install NVIDIA's driver to play.";
}

//! The override picker on My Rig: "my GPU is actually X" or "what if I had X?".

use iced::widget::{Row, button, column, combo_box, container, row, text};
use iced::{Center, Element, Fill};

use crate::Message;
use crate::i18n::I18n;
use crate::style::{BOLD, Colors};

/// Widget IDs for the pickers.
pub const GPU: &str = "override-gpu";
pub const CPU: &str = "override-cpu";

/// The hardware-table names to pick from.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Choices {
    pub gpus: combo_box::State<String>,
    pub cpus: combo_box::State<String>,
}

pub struct Picked<'a> {
    pub gpu: Option<&'a String>,
    pub cpu: Option<&'a String>,
    /// What verdicts use now: the pick, or the detected hardware's name.
    pub gpu_in_use: String,
    pub cpu_in_use: String,
}

pub fn view<'a>(
    choices: &'a Choices,
    picked: Picked<'a>,
    i18n: &I18n,
    colors: Colors,
) -> Element<'a, Message> {
    let gpu = Picker {
        label: "GPU",
        in_use: picked.gpu_in_use,
        id: GPU,
        state: &choices.gpus,
        selection: picked.gpu,
        on_pick: Message::OverrideGpu,
    };
    let cpu = Picker {
        label: "CPU",
        in_use: picked.cpu_in_use,
        id: CPU,
        state: &choices.cpus,
        selection: picked.cpu,
        on_pick: Message::OverrideCpu,
    };
    container(
        column![
            text(i18n.t("override-title")).font(BOLD).size(16),
            text(i18n.t("override-description")).color(colors.muted),
            gpu.view(i18n, colors),
            cpu.view(i18n, colors),
        ]
        .spacing(10),
    )
    .padding(14)
    .width(Fill)
    .style(move |_| colors.boxed(colors.panel))
    .into()
}

/// One row: what's in use, a searchable list of the table, and a reset
/// button. Also used by "What if I upgrade?".
pub struct Picker<'a> {
    pub label: &'static str,
    pub in_use: String,
    pub id: &'static str,
    pub state: &'a combo_box::State<String>,
    pub selection: Option<&'a String>,
    pub on_pick: fn(Option<String>) -> Message,
}

impl<'a> Picker<'a> {
    pub fn view(self, i18n: &I18n, colors: Colors) -> Row<'a, Message> {
        let on_pick = self.on_pick;
        let input = combo_box(
            self.state,
            &i18n.t("override-placeholder"),
            self.selection,
            move |name| on_pick(Some(name)),
        )
        .padding(8)
        .font(BOLD);
        let reset = button(text(i18n.t("override-reset")).font(BOLD).size(12))
            .padding([6, 10])
            .style(colors.button(false))
            .on_press_maybe(self.selection.map(|_| on_pick(None)));
        row![
            text(self.label).font(BOLD).width(60),
            text(self.in_use).font(BOLD).width(Fill),
            container(input).id(self.id).width(Fill),
            reset,
        ]
        .spacing(12)
        .align_y(Center)
    }
}

`app/src/perf.rs`:

```rs
//! The Phase 8 performance targets, checked on a real games.db: the app's
//! start-up work under 1 s, and Catalog searches under 50 ms on ~200k games.
//! Timing depends on the machine, so it's run by hand, in release mode:
//!
//! ```sh
//! RIGCHECK_PERF_DB=~/.local/share/rigcheck/games.db \
//!     cargo test --release -p rigcheck perf -- --ignored --nocapture
//! ```
//!
//! A games.db installed by the app has the prefix-indexed name search the
//! search target needs; one straight from the pipeline doesn't.

use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use crate::{App, Language, Message, Paths};

#[test]
#[ignore = "timing; needs RIGCHECK_PERF_DB and a release build"]
fn perf() {
    let db = std::env::var("RIGCHECK_PERF_DB").expect("RIGCHECK_PERF_DB");
    let dir = tempfile::TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let mut paths = Paths::under(dir.path());
    paths.home = std::env::var("HOME").unwrap().into();
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&paths.data).unwrap();
    std::fs::copy(db, paths.data.join("games.db")).unwrap();

    // What runs before the first frame, plus the two background jobs.
    let start = Instant::now();
    let (mut app, _) = App::new(paths.clone(), Language::English);
    let new = start.elapsed();
    let hardware = rigcheck_hardware::detect(std::path::Path::new("/"), &rigcheck_hardware::System);
    let games = rigcheck_steam::installed_games(&paths.home);
    let _ = app.update(Message::HardwareDetected(hardware));
    let _ = app.update(Message::GamesFound(games));
    let _ = app.view();
    let ready = start.elapsed();
    println!("App::new {new:?}; with hardware, Steam scan and first view {ready:?}");
    assert!(ready < Duration::from_secs(1), "cold start {ready:?}");

    // Broad queries are the slow ones: "s" matches ~50k names.
    for query in ["s", "a", "the", "co", "portal", "elden ri"] {
        let start = Instant::now();
        let _ = app.update(Message::CatalogSearch(query.to_owned()));
        let took = start.elapsed();
        println!("search {query:?}: {took:?}");
        assert!(
            took < Duration::from_millis(50),
            "search {query:?} took {took:?}"
        );
    }
}

`app/src/release.rs`:

```rs
//! "A newer rigcheck is out": the version of the latest GitHub Release,
//! compared with the running one (ROADMAP Phase 7). The app never replaces
//! itself; Flathub and AUR users update through their package manager.

use std::time::Duration;

use iced::futures::channel::oneshot;
use iced::widget::{button, container, row, space, text};
use iced::{Element, Fill, Task};
use rigcheck_net::{Allowlist, Client, RateLimiter, Retry};

use crate::Message;
use crate::i18n::I18n;
use crate::style::{BOLD, Colors};

/// Uploaded with every release (packaging/package.sh). `latest` skips
/// prereleases, so the daily `db-latest` games.db release never counts.
/// github.com redirects to its asset host, both in ROADMAP §6.
const VERSION_URL: &str =
    "https://github.com/Glory42/rigcheck/releases/latest/download/version.txt";
/// Where the notice links to.
pub const PAGE: &str = "https://github.com/Glory42/rigcheck/releases/latest";

/// Asks GitHub for the latest release's version; the answer comes back as
/// [`Message::LatestRelease`]. Nothing is sent until iced runs the task.
pub fn check() -> Task<Message> {
    Task::perform(
        async {
            let (sender, receiver) = oneshot::channel();
            std::thread::spawn(move || {
                let _ = sender.send(fetch());
            });
            receiver
                .await
                .unwrap_or_else(|_| Err("the check stopped".to_owned()))
        },
        Message::LatestRelease,
    )
}

fn fetch() -> Result<String, String> {
    let limiter = RateLimiter::new(5, Duration::from_secs(1));
    let mut client = Client::new(
        Allowlist::app(),
        limiter,
        Retry::new(1, Duration::from_secs(2)),
    )
    .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
    client
        .get_text(VERSION_URL)
        .map_err(|error| error.to_string())
}

/// The notice for a newer `version`, under the top bar.
pub fn notice(version: &str, i18n: &I18n, colors: Colors) -> Element<'static, Message> {
    container(
        row![
            text(i18n.t_with("release-out", &[("version", version)])).font(BOLD),
            space::horizontal(),
            button(text(i18n.t("release-get")).font(BOLD).size(13))
                .padding([7, 12])
                .style(colors.button(false))
                .on_press(Message::OpenUrl(PAGE.to_owned())),
        ]
        .align_y(iced::Center),
    )
    .padding(14)
    .width(Fill)
    .style(move |_| colors.boxed(colors.panel))
    .into()
}

/// Whether `latest` (e.g. "0.8.0") is a newer version than `running`.
/// Anything that isn't `major.minor.patch` counts as not newer.
pub fn is_newer(latest: &str, running: &str) -> bool {
    match (parse(latest), parse(running)) {
        (Some(latest), Some(running)) => latest > running,
        _ => false,
    }
}

/// "0.10.2" → (0, 10, 2). Tuples compare number by number.
fn parse(version: &str) -> Option<(u32, u32, u32)> {
    let mut numbers = version.trim().split('.').map(|part| part.parse().ok());
    let version = (numbers.next()??, numbers.next()??, numbers.next()??);
    numbers.next().is_none().then_some(version)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn compares_versions_number_by_number() {
        assert!(is_newer("0.8.0", "0.7.0"));
        assert!(is_newer("0.10.0", "0.9.3")); // not as text: "0.10" < "0.9"
        assert!(is_newer("1.0.0", "0.99.99"));
        assert!(!is_newer("0.7.0", "0.7.0"));
        assert!(!is_newer("0.6.9", "0.7.0"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_version_file_with_a_newline_or_junk_is_read_carefully() {
        assert!(is_newer("0.8.0\n", "0.7.0"));
        assert!(!is_newer("<html>Not Found</html>", "0.7.0"));
        assert!(!is_newer("", "0.7.0"));
    }
}

```rs
//! The README's screenshots, rendered offscreen by iced's test renderer:
//! the real app on a real games.db, with the dev machine's hardware.
//!
//! ```sh
//! RIGCHECK_SCREENSHOT_DB=~/.local/share/rigcheck/games.db \
//!     cargo test -p rigcheck screenshots -- --ignored
//! ```
//!
//! PNGs land in target/screenshots/; convert the ones to keep to WebP in
//! assets/screenshots/ (`magick x.png -quality 90 x.webp`).

use std::path::PathBuf;

use crate::{App, Language, Message, Page, Paths, catalog, test_support};

const SIZE: (f32, f32) = (1100.0, 720.0);

#[test]
#[ignore = "writes target/screenshots/; needs RIGCHECK_SCREENSHOT_DB"]
fn screenshots() {
    let db = std::env::var("RIGCHECK_SCREENSHOT_DB").expect("RIGCHECK_SCREENSHOT_DB");
    let dir = tempfile::TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let mut paths = Paths::under(dir.path());
    // The real home: installed games and Steam's cover art.
    paths.home = std::env::var("HOME").unwrap().into();
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&paths.data).unwrap();
    std::fs::copy(&db, paths.data.join("games.db")).unwrap();
    let out = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../target/screenshots");
    // The renderer adds its name to each file (`game-wgpu.png`): start clean.
    let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&out);
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&out).unwrap();

    let (mut app, _) = App::new(paths.clone(), Language::English);
    let _ = app.update(Message::HardwareDetected(test_support::amd_laptop()));
    let installed = rigcheck_steam::installed_games(&paths.home);
    let _ = app.update(Message::GamesFound(installed));

    shoot(&mut app, &out, "library");
    let _ = app.update(Message::Open(Page::Catalog));
    let rows = SIZE.1;
    let _ = app.update(Message::CatalogScrolled {
        offset: 0.0,
        height: rows,
    });
    shoot(&mut app, &out, "catalog");
    let _ = app.update(Message::CatalogFilter(catalog::Chip::CanRun));
    let _ = app.update(Message::CatalogScrolled {
        offset: 0.0,
        height: rows,
    });
    shoot(&mut app, &out, "catalog-can-run");
    let _ = app.update(Message::Open(Page::Game(1086940))); // Baldur's Gate 3
    shoot(&mut app, &out, "game");
    let _ = app.update(Message::PickToCompare(1086940));
    let _ = app.update(Message::Open(Page::Compare(1086940, 1091500))); // vs Cyberpunk 2077
    shoot(&mut app, &out, "compare");
    let _ = app.update(Message::Open(Page::Settings));
    shoot(&mut app, &out, "settings");
    let _ = app.update(Message::Open(Page::About));
    shoot(&mut app, &out, "about");
}

/// Saves the app as it looks now to `out/<name>.png`, replacing any old one.
fn shoot(app: &mut App, out: &std::path::Path, name: &str) {
    let path = out.join(format!("{name}.png"));
    let mut ui =
        iced_test::Simulator::with_size(iced_test::core::Settings::default(), SIZE, app.view());
    // Images load in the background over the first frames this renderer
    // draws: draw a few, then the one to keep.
    for _ in 0..4 {
        let _ = ui.snapshot(&app.theme());
        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(100));
    }
    let snapshot = ui.snapshot(&app.theme()).unwrap();
    assert!(snapshot.matches_image(&path).unwrap());
    println!("{}", path.display());
}

`app/src/settings.rs`:

```rs
//! User settings, saved as `settings.json` in the config dir (ROADMAP §7.1).

use std::path::Path;
use std::{fs, io};

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use crate::i18n::Language;

const FILE: &str = "settings.json";

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Settings {
    pub appearance: Appearance,
    /// `None` follows the system language. Files saved before languages
    /// existed lack this field, which serde reads as `None`.
    pub language: Option<Language>,
    /// Hardware-table names the user picked instead of what was detected.
    pub gpu_override: Option<String>,
    pub cpu_override: Option<String>,
    /// Only check for a new games.db when asked, not at every start.
    /// `default`: files saved before this existed would otherwise fail to
    /// load, and every setting would reset.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub manual_updates: bool,
    /// The most space downloaded covers may take; `None` for the default.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub image_cache_mb: Option<u32>,
}

/// The app's color theme, picked under Settings > Appearance.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Appearance {
    /// Paper when the system is light, Ink when it's dark.
    #[default]
    System,
    Ink,
    Midnight,
    Plum,
    Forest,
    Paper,
}

impl Appearance {
    /// The appearance to draw with, given the system's light or dark mode.
    pub fn resolve(self, system: iced::theme::Mode) -> Appearance {
        match (self, system) {
            (Appearance::System, iced::theme::Mode::Dark) => Appearance::Ink,
            (Appearance::System, _) => Appearance::Paper,
            (picked, _) => picked,
        }
    }

    /// In the order Settings shows them.
    pub const ALL: [Appearance; 6] = [
        Appearance::System,
        Appearance::Paper,
        Appearance::Ink,
        Appearance::Midnight,
        Appearance::Plum,
        Appearance::Forest,
    ];
}

impl Settings {
    /// The image cache limit in bytes: 500 MB unless set (ROADMAP §7.1).
    pub fn image_cache_bytes(&self) -> u64 {
        u64::from(self.image_cache_mb.unwrap_or(500)) * 1_000_000
    }

    /// Reads the settings in `dir`.
    pub fn load(dir: &Path) -> Settings {
        let Ok(json) = fs::read_to_string(dir.join(FILE)) else {
            return Settings::default();
        };
        serde_json::from_str(&json).unwrap_or_default()
    }

    /// Writes the settings to `dir`, creating it if needed.
    pub fn save(&self, dir: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
        fs::create_dir_all(dir)?;
        let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(self).map_err(io::Error::other)?;
        fs::write(dir.join(FILE), json + "\n")
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use tempfile::TempDir;

    #[test]
    fn a_fresh_install_follows_the_system() {
        let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();

        let settings = Settings::load(dir.path());

        assert_eq!(settings.appearance, Appearance::System);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_saved_appearance_comes_back() {
        let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
        let settings = Settings {
            appearance: Appearance::Ink,
            ..Settings::default()
        };

        settings.save(dir.path()).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(Settings::load(dir.path()).appearance, Appearance::Ink);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_broken_file_falls_back_to_the_defaults() {
        let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
        for broken in ["{not json", r#"{"appearance": "neon"}"#] {
            fs::write(dir.path().join("settings.json"), broken).unwrap();

            assert_eq!(
                Settings::load(dir.path()).appearance,
                Appearance::System,
                "{broken}"
            );
        }
    }

    /// Written by v0.5, before `manual_updates` existed.
    #[test]
    fn settings_from_an_older_version_keep_their_choices() {
        let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
        let old = r#"{"appearance": "ink", "language": "tr", "gpu_override": "GeForce RTX 3060", "cpu_override": null}"#;
        fs::write(dir.path().join("settings.json"), old).unwrap();

        let settings = Settings::load(dir.path());

        assert_eq!(settings.appearance, Appearance::Ink);
        assert_eq!(settings.gpu_override.as_deref(), Some("GeForce RTX 3060"));
        assert!(!settings.manual_updates);
    }
}

`app/src/settings_page.rs`:

```rs
//! The Settings page: Appearance, Language, Storage and Privacy.

use iced::border::Border;
use iced::widget::{Space, button, column, container, row, scrollable, space, text};
use iced::{Color, Element, Fill};

use crate::Message;
use crate::i18n::{I18n, Language};
use crate::settings::{Appearance, Settings};
use crate::style::{BOLD, Colors};

/// What the app keeps on disk, in bytes (ROADMAP §7.1).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
pub struct Storage {
    pub games_db: u64,
    pub fetched_db: u64,
    pub images: u64,
}

/// The image cache limits to pick from, in MB.
const IMAGE_LIMITS: [u32; 4] = [100, 250, 500, 1000];

pub fn view(
    settings: &Settings,
    storage: Storage,
    i18n: &I18n,
    colors: Colors,
) -> Element<'static, Message> {
    let appearances = Appearance::ALL.map(|appearance| {
        appearance_option(appearance, appearance == settings.appearance, i18n, colors)
    });
    let languages = [None]
        .into_iter()
        .chain(Language::ALL.map(Some))
        .map(|language| language_option(language, settings.language == language, i18n, colors));

    let page = column![
        section(
            i18n.t("appearance-title"),
            i18n.t("appearance-description"),
            colors
        ),
        // Wraps in a narrow window instead of running off the side.
        row(appearances).spacing(18).wrap(),
        section(
            i18n.t("language-title"),
            i18n.t("language-description"),
            colors
        ),
        row(languages).spacing(18).wrap(),
        section(
            i18n.t("storage-title"),
            i18n.t("storage-description"),
            colors
        ),
        storage_rows(settings, storage, i18n, colors),
        section(
            i18n.t("privacy-title"),
            i18n.t("privacy-description"),
            colors
        ),
        privacy(settings, i18n, colors),
    ]
    .spacing(12);
    // Room on the right and bottom so hard shadows aren't clipped.
    scrollable(page.padding([0, 6])).width(Fill).into()
}

/// Sizes and what can be done about them.
fn storage_rows(
    settings: &Settings,
    storage: Storage,
    i18n: &I18n,
    colors: Colors,
) -> Element<'static, Message> {
    let action = |id: &str, message: Message| {
        button(text(i18n.t(id)).font(BOLD).size(12))
            .padding([6, 10])
            .style(colors.button(false))
            .on_press(message)
    };
    let line = |id: &str, bytes: u64, actions: Vec<Element<'static, Message>>| {
        row![
            text(i18n.t(id)).font(BOLD).width(180),
            text(megabytes(bytes)).width(90),
            row(actions).spacing(8),
        ]
        .spacing(12)
        .align_y(iced::Center)
    };
    let limits = IMAGE_LIMITS.map(|mb| {
        let label = if mb >= 1000 {
            format!("{} GB", mb / 1000)
        } else {
            format!("{mb} MB")
        };
        let on = settings.image_cache_bytes() == u64::from(mb) * 1_000_000;
        button(text(label).font(BOLD).size(12))
            .padding([6, 10])
            .style(colors.button(on))
            .on_press(Message::ImageCacheLimit(mb))
            .into()
    });
    column![
        line(
            "storage-games-db",
            storage.games_db,
            vec![
                action("storage-check", Message::CheckForUpdates).into(),
                action("storage-redownload", Message::Redownload).into(),
            ],
        ),
        line(
            "storage-fetched",
            storage.fetched_db,
            vec![action("storage-clear-fetched", Message::ClearFetched).into()],
        ),
        line(
            "storage-images",
            storage.images,
            vec![action("storage-clear-images", Message::ClearImages).into()],
        ),
        row![
            text(i18n.t("storage-image-limit")).font(BOLD).width(180),
            space::horizontal().width(90),
            row(limits).spacing(8),
        ]
        .spacing(12)
        .align_y(iced::Center),
    ]
    .spacing(10)
    .into()
}

/// The update choice and every place the app sends requests (ROADMAP §6).
fn privacy(settings: &Settings, i18n: &I18n, colors: Colors) -> Element<'static, Message> {
    let choice = |id: &str, manual: bool| {
        button(
            column![
                text(i18n.t(id)).font(BOLD),
                status(settings.manual_updates == manual, i18n)
            ]
            .spacing(8)
            .padding(6),
        )
        .style(colors.button(settings.manual_updates == manual))
        .on_press(Message::SetManualUpdates(manual))
    };
    let destinations = ["privacy-github", "privacy-steam-store", "privacy-steam-cdn"]
        .map(|id| text(i18n.t(id)).into());
    column![
        text(i18n.t("privacy-updates")).font(BOLD),
        row![
            choice("privacy-automatic", false),
            choice("privacy-manual", true)
        ]
        .spacing(18),
        text(i18n.t("privacy-destinations")).font(BOLD),
        column(destinations).spacing(4),
    ]
    .spacing(12)
    .into()
}

/// `bytes` in megabytes with one decimal, e.g. "18.3 MB".
fn megabytes(bytes: u64) -> String {
    format!("{:.1} MB", bytes as f64 / 1_000_000.0)
}

fn section(title: String, description: String, colors: Colors) -> Element<'static, Message> {
    column![
        text(title).font(BOLD).size(20),
        text(description).color(colors.muted),
    ]
    .spacing(6)
    .padding([10, 0])
    .into()
}

/// A button showing an appearance's name and its main colors.
fn appearance_option(
    appearance: Appearance,
    selected: bool,
    i18n: &I18n,
    colors: Colors,
) -> Element<'static, Message> {
    let own = appearance.colors();
    let swatch = |color: Color| {
        container(Space::new().width(22).height(22)).style(move |_| container::Style {
            background: Some(color.into()),
            border: Border {
                color: own.line,
                width: 2.0,
                radius: 0.0.into(),
            },
            ..container::Style::default()
        })
    };
    // System: two of Paper's colors and two of Ink's, light and dark.
    let (light, dark) = (Appearance::Paper.colors(), Appearance::Ink.colors());
    let shown = match appearance {
        Appearance::System => [light.bg, light.hud, dark.bg, dark.accent],
        _ => [own.bg, own.hud, own.panel, own.accent],
    };
    let preview = row![
        swatch(shown[0]),
        swatch(shown[1]),
        swatch(shown[2]),
        swatch(shown[3])
    ]
    .spacing(4);
    let name = i18n.t(&format!("theme-{}", appearance.name().to_lowercase()));

    button(
        column![preview, text(name).font(BOLD), status(selected, i18n)]
            .spacing(8)
            .padding(6),
    )
    .style(colors.button(selected))
    .on_press(Message::AppearanceSelected(appearance))
    .into()
}

/// A button for one language, or for following the system (`None`).
fn language_option(
    language: Option<Language>,
    selected: bool,
    i18n: &I18n,
    colors: Colors,
) -> Element<'static, Message> {
    let name = match language {
        Some(language) => language.native_name().to_owned(),
        None => i18n.t("language-system"),
    };
    button(
        column![text(name).font(BOLD), status(selected, i18n)]
            .spacing(8)
            .padding(6),
    )
    .style(colors.button(selected))
    .on_press(Message::LanguageSelected(language))
    .into()
}

fn status(selected: bool, i18n: &I18n) -> Element<'static, Message> {
    let label = if selected {
        i18n.t("selected")
    } else {
        " ".to_owned()
    };
    text(label).size(11).font(BOLD).into()
}

//! Colors for each appearance, from the round 2 prototype
//! (branch `prototype/ui-variants`).

use iced::border::Border;
use iced::font::{Font, Weight};
use iced::theme::Palette;
use iced::widget::{button, container};
use iced::{Color, Shadow, Theme, Vector};

use crate::settings::Appearance;

/// The colors design D draws with.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Colors {
    pub bg: Color,
    /// The top bar.
    pub hud: Color,
    pub panel: Color,
    /// Alternate rows and labels.
    pub panel2: Color,
    /// Outlines and hard shadows.
    pub line: Color,
    /// The thick line under the top bar.
    pub rule: Color,
    pub text: Color,
    pub muted: Color,
    pub accent: Color,

    pub on_accent: Color,
}

const fn rgb(hex: u32) -> Color {
    Color::from_rgb8((hex >> 16) as u8, (hex >> 8) as u8, hex as u8)
}

impl Appearance {

            Appearance::Paper | Appearance::System => Colors {

                hud: rgb(0xf58a1f),
                panel: rgb(0xfffaf0),
                panel2: rgb(0xf7ecd6),

        Theme::custom(
