/// Design D's lettering: bold monospace.
pub const BOLD: Font = Font {
    weight: Weight::Bold,
    ..Font::MONOSPACE
};

impl Colors {
    /// A chunky box: thick outline and a hard shadow with no blur.
    pub fn boxed(self, background: Color) -> container::Style {
        container::Style {
            text_color: Some(self.text),
            background: Some(background.into()),
            border: Border {
                color: self.line,
                width: 3.0,
                radius: 0.0.into(),
            },
            shadow: self.hard_shadow(4.0),
            snap: true,
        }
    }

    /// A tab or button; `on` paints it in the accent color.
    pub fn button(self, on: bool) -> impl Fn(&Theme, button::Status) -> button::Style {
        move |_, status| {
            let (background, text_color) = if on {
                (self.accent, self.on_accent)
            } else {
                (self.panel, self.text)
            };
            let pressed = status == button::Status::Pressed;
            button::Style {
                background: Some(background.into()),
                text_color,
                border: Border {
                    color: self.line,
                    width: 3.0,
                    radius: 0.0.into(),
                },
                // Pressing flattens the shadow, like pushing a physical key.
                shadow: self.hard_shadow(if pressed { 0.0 } else { 3.0 }),
                snap: true,
            }
        }
    }

    fn hard_shadow(self, offset: f32) -> Shadow {
        Shadow {
            color: self.line,
            offset: Vector::new(offset, offset),
            blur_radius: 0.0,
        }
    }
}

/// The stamp color for a verdict level.
pub fn level_color(level: rigcheck_core::Level) -> Color {
    use rigcheck_core::Level;
    match level {
        Level::Recommended => rgb(0x2ea043),
        Level::Minimum => rgb(0xd29922),
        Level::Below => rgb(0xe5534b),
        Level::Blocked => rgb(0xa371f7),
        Level::Unknown => rgb(0x8b949e),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::settings::Appearance;
    use rigcheck_core::Level;

    /// WCAG 2's contrast ratio: (lighter + 0.05) / (darker + 0.05), from
    /// each color's relative luminance.
    fn contrast(a: Color, b: Color) -> f32 {
        let channel = |c: f32| {
            if c <= 0.03928 {
                c / 12.92
            } else {
                ((c + 0.055) / 1.055).powf(2.4)
            }
        };
        let luminance =
            |c: Color| 0.2126 * channel(c.r) + 0.7152 * channel(c.g) + 0.0722 * channel(c.b);
        let (l1, l2) = (luminance(a), luminance(b));
        (l1.max(l2) + 0.05) / (l1.min(l2) + 0.05)
    }

    /// WCAG AA for normal text: 4.5:1, in every appearance.
    #[test]
    fn every_appearance_has_readable_text() {
        for appearance in Appearance::ALL {
            let c = appearance.colors();
            let pairs = [
                ("text on background", c.text, c.bg),
                ("text on panels", c.text, c.panel),
                ("top bar text", c.text, c.hud),
                ("muted text on background", c.muted, c.bg),
                ("muted text on panels", c.muted, c.panel),
                ("selected buttons", c.on_accent, c.accent),
            ];
            let stamps = [
                Level::Recommended,
                Level::Minimum,
                Level::Below,
                Level::Blocked,
                Level::Unknown,
            ]
            .map(|level| ("a stamp", c.line, level_color(level)));
            for (what, fg, bg) in pairs.into_iter().chain(stamps) {
                let ratio = contrast(fg, bg);
                assert!(ratio >= 4.5, "{appearance:?}: {what} is {ratio:.1}:1");
            }
        }
    }
}

`app/src/whatif.rs`:

```rs
//! "What if I upgrade?" on My Rig: pick a GPU, CPU or amount of RAM and see
//! which installed games would change verdict. Nothing is saved, and the
//! rest of the app keeps using your PC (with its overrides).

use iced::widget::{button, column, container, row, text};
use iced::{Element, Fill};

use crate::Message;
use crate::i18n::I18n;
use crate::overrides::{Choices, Picker};
use crate::style::{BOLD, Colors};

/// Widget IDs for the pickers.
pub const GPU: &str = "whatif-gpu";
pub const CPU: &str = "whatif-cpu";

/// The RAM amounts to pick from, in GB.
const RAM_GB: [u32; 4] = [8, 16, 32, 64];

/// The hypothetical parts; `None` keeps your own.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct Picks {
    pub gpu: Option<String>,
    pub cpu: Option<String>,
    pub ram_gb: Option<u32>,
}

impl Picks {
    fn any(&self) -> bool {
        self.gpu.is_some() || self.cpu.is_some() || self.ram_gb.is_some()
    }
}

/// `changes`: one line per installed game whose verdict would change, e.g.
/// "Cyberpunk 2077: TOO WEAK → LOW".
pub fn view<'a>(
    choices: &'a Choices,
    picks: &'a Picks,
    in_use: (String, String),
    changes: Vec<String>,
    i18n: &I18n,
    colors: Colors,
) -> Element<'a, Message> {
    let (gpu_in_use, cpu_in_use) = in_use;
    let gpu = Picker {
        label: "GPU",
        in_use: gpu_in_use,
        id: GPU,
        state: &choices.gpus,
        selection: picks.gpu.as_ref(),
        on_pick: Message::WhatIfGpu,
    };
    let cpu = Picker {
        label: "CPU",
        in_use: cpu_in_use,
        id: CPU,
        state: &choices.cpus,
        selection: picks.cpu.as_ref(),
        on_pick: Message::WhatIfCpu,
    };
    let ram = RAM_GB.map(|gb| {
        let on = picks.ram_gb == Some(gb);
        button(text(format!("{gb} GB")).font(BOLD).size(12))
            .padding([6, 10])
            .style(colors.button(on))
            .on_press(Message::WhatIfRam((!on).then_some(gb)))
            .into()
    });
    let result: Element<'a, Message> = if !picks.any() {
        text(i18n.t("whatif-hint")).color(colors.muted).into()
    } else if changes.is_empty() {
        text(i18n.t("whatif-no-change")).font(BOLD).into()
    } else {
        column(changes.into_iter().map(|line| text(line).font(BOLD).into()))
            .spacing(4)
            .into()
    };
    container(
        column![
            text(i18n.t("whatif-title")).font(BOLD).size(16),
            text(i18n.t("whatif-description")).color(colors.muted),
            gpu.view(i18n, colors),
            cpu.view(i18n, colors),
            row![text("RAM").font(BOLD).width(60), row(ram).spacing(8)]
                .spacing(12)
                .align_y(iced::Center),
            result,
        ]
        .spacing(10),
    )
    .padding(14)
    .width(Fill)
    .style(move |_| colors.boxed(colors.panel))
    .into()
}

`assets/brand/README.md`:

```md
# Brand assets

The rigcheck icon: a pixel-art oil derrick (the "rig") with a check badge. Original artwork made for this project and covered by the repository's MIT license.

| File | Source |
|---|---|
| `src/draw_icon_32.py` | Draws the 32×32 master icon |
| `src/draw_icon_16.py` | Hand-drawn 16×16 version for favicons, stored as a text pixel map: edit the characters to change pixels |
| `icon-16.png`, `icon-32.png` | Output of the scripts above |
| `icon-64.png` … `icon-1024.png` | `icon-32.png` scaled up with nearest-neighbor, so the pixels stay sharp |

Regenerate everything after editing a script:

```sh
./build.sh
```

Requires `python3` (standard library only) and ImageMagick 7.

## Palette

| Name | Hex | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Steel dark | `#333D47` | Outlines, crown block, platform |
| Steel | `#5B6B7A` | Bracing, platform edge |
| Steel light | `#8A9BAB` | Leg highlights |
| Orange | `#F58A1F` / `#C25E0A` | Pennant |
| Green | `#2EA043` / `#1A6B2A` | Check badge |
| White | `#FFFFFF` | Badge ring and check |

```

`assets/brand/build.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regenerate every icon PNG from the drawing scripts in src/.
# Needs python3 and ImageMagick 7 (`magick`).
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

python3 -I src/draw_icon_16.py icon-16.png
python3 -I src/draw_icon_32.py icon-32.png

# The art sits on a 32x32 grid, so whole-number nearest-neighbor scaling keeps it sharp.
for s in 64 128 256 512 1024; do
  magick icon-32.png -filter point -resize "${s}x${s}" "PNG32:icon-$s.png"
done

```

`assets/brand/src/draw_icon_16.py`:

```py
"""Hand-drawn 16x16 rigcheck icon (simplified for favicons). Usage: python3 draw_icon_16.py OUT.png"""

import struct
import sys
import zlib

PALETTE = {
    ".": (0, 0, 0, 0),
    "D": (0x33, 0x3D, 0x47, 255),
    "S": (0x5B, 0x6B, 0x7A, 255),
    "L": (0x8A, 0x9B, 0xAB, 255),
    "O": (0xF5, 0x8A, 0x1F, 255),
    "o": (0xC2, 0x5E, 0x0A, 255),
    "G": (0x2E, 0xA0, 0x43, 255),
    "g": (0x1A, 0x6B, 0x2A, 255),
    "W": (0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 255),
}

ART = """
.......DOOO.....
.......Doo......
......DDDD......
......DLLD......
.....DLSSLD.....
.....DS..SD.....
....DLDDDDLD....
....DS.S..WWWW..
...DLS...WGGGGW.
...DS...WGGGGGGW
..DLDDDDWGGGGWGW
..DS....WGWGWGGW
.DLS....WGGWGGGW
DDDDDDDD.WggggW.
.SSSSSSS..WWWW..
................
"""

rows = [line for line in ART.strip("\n").split("\n")]
assert len(rows) == 16 and all(len(r) == 16 for r in rows), [len(r) for r in rows]
raw = b"".join(b"\x00" + b"".join(bytes(PALETTE[c]) for c in row) for row in rows)


def chunk(tag, data):
    c = struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + tag + data
    return c + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(tag + data) & 0xFFFFFFFF)


with open(sys.argv[1], "wb") as f:
    f.write(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n")
    f.write(chunk(b"IHDR", struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", 16, 16, 8, 6, 0, 0, 0)))
    f.write(chunk(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(raw, 9)))
    f.write(chunk(b"IEND", b""))

```

`assets/brand/src/draw_icon_32.py`:

```py
"""Draw the rigcheck icon: a pixel-art oil derrick with a check badge.

Pure stdlib. Usage: python3 draw_icon_32.py OUT.png
"""

import struct
import sys
import zlib

N = 32

T = (0, 0, 0, 0)
STEEL = (0x5B, 0x6B, 0x7A, 255)
STEEL_LIGHT = (0x8A, 0x9B, 0xAB, 255)
STEEL_DARK = (0x33, 0x3D, 0x47, 255)
ORANGE = (0xF5, 0x8A, 0x1F, 255)
ORANGE_DARK = (0xC2, 0x5E, 0x0A, 255)
GREEN = (0x2E, 0xA0, 0x43, 255)
GREEN_DARK = (0x1A, 0x6B, 0x2A, 255)
WHITE = (0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 255)

img = [[T] * N for _ in range(N)]


def px(x, y, c):
    if 0 <= x < N and 0 <= y < N:
        img[y][x] = c


def line(x0, y0, x1, y1, c):
    dx, dy = abs(x1 - x0), -abs(y1 - y0)
    sx = 1 if x0 < x1 else -1
    sy = 1 if y0 < y1 else -1
    err = dx + dy
    while True:
        px(x0, y0, c)
        if x0 == x1 and y0 == y1:
            return
        e2 = 2 * err
        if e2 >= dy:
            err += dy
            x0 += sx
        if e2 <= dx:
            err += dx
            y0 += sy


def rect(x0, y0, x1, y1, c):
    for y in range(y0, y1 + 1):
        for x in range(x0, x1 + 1):
            px(x, y, c)


def leg_x(y, left):
    """x of the left/right tower leg at row y (top y=5, base y=27)."""
    t = (y - 5) / (27 - 5)
    return round(13 - t * 9) if left else round(18 + t * 9)


# Pennant on top
line(15, 0, 15, 4, STEEL_DARK)
rect(16, 0, 19, 1, ORANGE)
px(20, 0, ORANGE)
px(16, 2, ORANGE_DARK)
px(17, 2, ORANGE_DARK)

# Crown block
rect(12, 4, 19, 5, STEEL_DARK)

# Girders and alternating V / inverted-V (Warren truss) bracing
girders = [11, 19, 27]
prev = 5
for i, g in enumerate(girders):
    l0, r0 = leg_x(prev, True), leg_x(prev, False)
    l1, r1 = leg_x(g, True), leg_x(g, False)
    if i % 2 == 0:  # V: top corners down to the middle
        line(l0 + 1, prev + 1, 15, g - 1, STEEL)
        line(r0 - 1, prev + 1, 16, g - 1, STEEL)
    else:  # inverted V: middle top down to the bottom corners
        line(15, prev + 1, l1 + 1, g - 1, STEEL)
        line(16, prev + 1, r1 - 1, g - 1, STEEL)
    line(l1, g, r1, g, STEEL_DARK)
    prev = g

# Legs: two pixels thick, dark outer edge + lighter inner edge
for y in range(5, 28):
    lx, rx = leg_x(y, True), leg_x(y, False)
    px(lx, y, STEEL_DARK)
    px(lx + 1, y, STEEL_LIGHT)
    px(rx, y, STEEL_DARK)
    px(rx - 1, y, STEEL_LIGHT)

# Ground platform
rect(1, 28, 30, 29, STEEL_DARK)
rect(2, 30, 29, 30, STEEL)

# Check badge, bottom right, with a white ring to separate it from the tower
cx, cy, r = 25.0, 24.5, 6.5
for y in range(N):
    for x in range(N):
        d = ((x + 0.5 - cx) ** 2 + (y + 0.5 - cy) ** 2) ** 0.5
        if d <= r - 1.2:
            px(x, y, GREEN_DARK if (r - 2.2 < d and y >= cy + 2) else GREEN)
        elif d <= r:
            px(x, y, WHITE)
for x, y in [(22, 24), (23, 25)]:
    px(x, y, WHITE)
    px(x, y + 1, WHITE)
for x, y in [(24, 25), (25, 24), (26, 23), (27, 22)]:
    px(x, y, WHITE)
    px(x, y + 1, WHITE)


def write_png(path, rows):
    raw = b"".join(b"\x00" + b"".join(bytes(p) for p in row) for row in rows)

    def chunk(tag, data):
        c = struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + tag + data
        return c + struct.pack(">I", zlib.crc32(tag + data) & 0xFFFFFFFF)

    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n")
        f.write(chunk(b"IHDR", struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", N, N, 8, 6, 0, 0, 0)))
        f.write(chunk(b"IDAT", zlib.compress(raw, 9)))
        f.write(chunk(b"IEND", b""))


write_png(sys.argv[1], img)

`crates/core/src/catalog.rs`:

```rs
//! The hardware table: known CPUs and GPUs with scores, and matching the
//! names requirements and /proc use to entries (ROADMAP §8.2 steps 2–5).

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::sync::LazyLock;

use regex::Regex;
use serde::Deserialize;

use crate::matcher::{HardwareRef, Vendor};

/// A known CPU or GPU.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize)]
pub struct CatalogEntry {
    /// Display name, e.g. "GeForce GTX 1060 6GB".
    pub name: String,
    pub vendor: Vendor,
    pub score: u32,
    /// GPUs with their own memory.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub vram_mb: Option<u32>,
    /// Extra spellings to match, besides the name.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub aliases: Vec<String>,
    /// PCI IDs as "vendor:device" hex, e.g. "10de:1c03". GPUs only.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub pci: Vec<String>,
}

impl CatalogEntry {
    /// What the matcher compares.
    pub fn to_ref(&self) -> HardwareRef {
        HardwareRef {
            vendor: self.vendor,
            score: self.score,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct Catalog {
    cpus: Vec<CatalogEntry>,
    cpu_keys: HashMap<String, usize>,
    gpus: Vec<CatalogEntry>,
    gpu_keys: HashMap<String, usize>,
}

impl Catalog {
    pub fn new(cpus: Vec<CatalogEntry>, gpus: Vec<CatalogEntry>) -> Catalog {
        Catalog {
            cpu_keys: keys(&cpus),
            cpus,
            gpu_keys: keys(&gpus),
            gpus,
        }
    }

    /// Reads the format of `data/hardware.toml`.
    pub fn from_toml(text: &str) -> Result<Catalog, toml::de::Error> {
        #[derive(Deserialize)]
        struct File {
            #[serde(default)]
            cpu: Vec<CatalogEntry>,
            #[serde(default)]
            gpu: Vec<CatalogEntry>,
        }
        let file: File = toml::from_str(text)?;
        Ok(Catalog::new(file.cpu, file.gpu))
    }

    pub fn cpus(&self) -> &[CatalogEntry] {
        &self.cpus
    }

    pub fn gpus(&self) -> &[CatalogEntry] {
        &self.gpus
    }

    /// Every CPU the text names that the table knows, in order. Also finds
    /// /proc/cpuinfo names like "Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-8400 CPU @ 2.80GHz".
    pub fn match_cpus(&self, text: &str) -> Vec<&CatalogEntry> {
        matches(text, &self.cpus, &self.cpu_keys)
    }

    /// CPU names in `text` the table doesn't know, as written.
    pub fn unmatched_cpus(&self, text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
        unmatched(text, &self.cpu_keys)
    }

    /// GPU names in `text` the table doesn't know, as written.
    pub fn unmatched_gpus(&self, text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
        unmatched(text, &self.gpu_keys)
    }

    /// The GPU with this PCI ID, the exact way to identify a detected GPU.
    pub fn gpu_by_pci(&self, vendor_id: u16, device_id: u16) -> Option<&CatalogEntry> {
        let id = format!("{vendor_id:04x}:{device_id:04x}");
        self.gpus.iter().find(|gpu| gpu.pci.contains(&id))
    }

    /// Every GPU the text names that the table knows, in order.
    pub fn match_gpus(&self, text: &str) -> Vec<&CatalogEntry> {
        matches(text, &self.gpus, &self.gpu_keys)
    }
}

/// Lookup keys for each entry: its name and aliases, normalized.
fn keys(entries: &[CatalogEntry]) -> HashMap<String, usize> {
    let mut keys = HashMap::new();
    for (index, entry) in entries.iter().enumerate() {
        for name in std::iter::once(&entry.name).chain(&entry.aliases) {
            keys.insert(normalize(name, false), index);
        }
    }
    keys
}

fn matches<'a>(
    text: &str,
    entries: &'a [CatalogEntry],
    keys: &HashMap<String, usize>,
) -> Vec<&'a CatalogEntry> {
    let mut found: Vec<&CatalogEntry> = Vec::new();
    for token in alternatives(text) {
        if let Some(entry) = lookup(&token, keys).map(|index| &entries[index])
            && !found.contains(&entry)
        {
            found.push(entry);
        }
    }
    found
}

/// The alternatives in `text` that name hardware but match no entry.
fn unmatched(text: &str, keys: &HashMap<String, usize>) -> Vec<String> {
    alternatives(text)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|token| !normalize(token, false).is_empty() && lookup(token, keys).is_none())
        .collect()
}

/// "GTX 970 / RX 480 or Arc A380 (4GB)" → ["GTX 970", "RX 480", "Arc A380"].
/// A bare model number reuses the previous name's series: "GTX 970 / 1060"
/// → ["GTX 970", "GTX 1060"].
fn alternatives(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    static ALTERNATIVES: LazyLock<Regex> =
        LazyLock::new(|| Regex::new(r"(?i)\s*(?:/|,|;|\||\bor\b)\s*").unwrap());
    let mut tokens: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for token in ALTERNATIVES.split(&strip_parentheses(text)) {
        let token = token.trim();
        if token.is_empty() {
            continue;
        }
        let series = tokens.last().and_then(|previous: &String| {
            let digits = previous.find(|c: char| c.is_ascii_digit())?;
            Some(previous[..digits].to_owned())
        });
        match series {
            Some(series) if token.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_digit()) => {
                tokens.push(format!("{series}{token}"));
            }
            _ => tokens.push(token.to_owned()),
        }
    }
    tokens
}

fn lookup(token: &str, keys: &HashMap<String, usize>) -> Option<usize> {
    keys.get(&normalize(token, false))
        .or_else(|| keys.get(&normalize(token, true)))
        .copied()
}

/// Words that don't tell models apart.
const NOISE: &[&str] = &[
    "nvidia",
    "geforce",
    "amd",
    "ati",
    "radeon",
    "intel",
    "core",
    "processor",
    "cpu",
    "graphics",
    "card",
    "better",
    "equivalent",
    "higher",
    "series",
    "with",
    "and",
    "similar",
];

/// A comparable key: "Intel I5 4690" and "Core i5-4690" both become "i54690".
/// `drop_sizes` also drops memory sizes, so "RX 580 8GB" finds "RX 580".
fn normalize(text: &str, drop_sizes: bool) -> String {
    static SIZE: LazyLock<Regex> = LazyLock::new(|| Regex::new(r"^\d+(gb|mb)$").unwrap());
    static SPACED_SIZE: LazyLock<Regex> =
        LazyLock::new(|| Regex::new(r"(\d)\s+(gb|mb)\b").unwrap());
    let text = strip_parentheses(&text.to_lowercase());
    let text = SPACED_SIZE.replace_all(&text, "$1$2"); // "4 gb" → "4gb"
    let text = text.split('@').next().unwrap_or_default(); // "i5-2500K@3.3GHz"
    text.split(|c: char| !c.is_alphanumeric())
        .filter(|word| !word.is_empty() && !NOISE.contains(word))
        .filter(|word| !(drop_sizes && SIZE.is_match(word)))
        .collect()
}

/// Drops "(...)" asides like "(4GB+ of VRAM)" or "(R)".
fn strip_parentheses(text: &str) -> String {
    static ASIDE: LazyLock<Regex> = LazyLock::new(|| Regex::new(r"\([^)]*\)").unwrap());
    ASIDE.replace_all(text, " ").into_owned()
}

//! Compares a game's requirements with the user's specs (ROADMAP §8.3).

/// What a game asks for. Either tier can be missing from the store page.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct GameRequirements {
    pub minimum: Option<Requirement>,
    pub recommended: Option<Requirement>,
}

/// One tier of requirements. `None` means the store page doesn't say.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Requirement {
    pub ram_mb: Option<u32>,
    pub vram_mb: Option<u32>,
    pub storage_mb: Option<u32>,
    /// DirectX version, e.g. 11 or 12.
    pub directx: Option<u8>,
    /// Alternatives, as in "i5-4460 or FX-6300". Empty if none matched.
    pub cpus: Vec<HardwareRef>,
    /// Alternatives, as in "GTX 1060 or RX 580". Empty if none matched.
    pub gpus: Vec<HardwareRef>,
}

/// A CPU or GPU found in the hardware table.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct HardwareRef {
    pub vendor: Vendor,
    /// Performance score; higher is faster. Comparable within CPUs or GPUs.
    pub score: u32,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Vendor {
    Amd,
    Intel,
    Nvidia,
}

/// The user's machine, already resolved to numbers the matcher compares.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Specs {
    pub ram_mb: Option<u32>,
    /// `None` for GPUs that share system RAM, or when unknown.
    pub vram_mb: Option<u32>,
    /// Free space on the Steam library with the most room.
    pub free_storage_mb: Option<u32>,
    /// Highest Vulkan version the gaming GPU supports, as (major, minor).
    pub vulkan: Option<(u32, u32)>,
    /// The gaming GPU runs on the open-source `nouveau` driver.
    pub nouveau: bool,
    pub cpu: Option<HardwareRef>,
    pub gpu: Option<HardwareRef>,
}

/// Linux-specific facts about a game.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct LinuxInfo {
    /// `None` if the game has no anti-cheat.
    pub anticheat: Option<AntiCheat>,
    /// `None` if ProtonDB has too few reports.
    pub protondb: Option<ProtonTier>,
    /// Has a Linux build, so Proton isn't needed.
    pub native: bool,
}

/// ProtonDB's rating for running the Windows version through Proton.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum ProtonTier {
    Platinum,
    Gold,
    Silver,
    Bronze,
    Borked,
}

/// AreWeAntiCheatYet's status for a game's anti-cheat on Linux.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum AntiCheat {
    Supported,
    Running,
    Planned,
    Broken,
    Denied,
}

/// Something worth telling the user that doesn't change the level.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Warning {
    /// `nouveau` runs most 3D games poorly.
    Nouveau,
}

/// Why a game can't run on Linux whatever the hardware.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Blocker {
    AntiCheat,
    /// ProtonDB rates the game "Borked".
    Proton,
}

/// How well a game should run. Variants go from best to worst, so the
/// derived `Ord` makes `max()` the worst level.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub enum Level {
    Recommended,
    Minimum,
    Below,
    /// Not enough data to say.
    Unknown,
    /// Can't run on Linux whatever the hardware. See [`Verdict::blocker`].
    Blocked,
}

/// How much of the verdict rests on data rather than gaps.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Confidence {
    /// Every component was compared.
    High,
    /// Some components were compared.
    Partial,
    /// Nothing could be compared.
    Low,
}

/// A part of the machine that requirements talk about.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Component {
    /// DirectX through Proton, which needs Vulkan.
    GraphicsApi,
    Cpu,
    Gpu,
    Ram,
    Storage,
    Vram,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Verdict {
    /// The worst component's level.
    pub overall: Level,
    /// The component holding the verdict down, if any.
    pub bottleneck: Option<Component>,
    /// Each component that could be compared, with its level, in the order
    /// the game page lists them.
    pub components: Vec<(Component, Level)>,
    pub confidence: Confidence,
    pub blocker: Option<Blocker>,
    pub warnings: Vec<Warning>,
}

pub fn evaluate(game: &GameRequirements, specs: &Specs, linux: &LinuxInfo) -> Verdict {
    let tiers = |need: &dyn Fn(&Requirement) -> Option<u32>| {
        (
            game.minimum.as_ref().and_then(need),
            game.recommended.as_ref().and_then(need),
        )
    };

    // Usable RAM is below installed RAM: the kernel and an iGPU keep some.
    let (min, rec) = tiers(&|r| r.ram_mb);
    let ram = compare(specs.ram_mb.map(|mb| mb + mb / 10), min, rec);

    let (min, rec) = tiers(&|r| r.storage_mb);
    let storage = compare(specs.free_storage_mb, min, rec);

    let (min, rec) = tiers(&|r| r.vram_mb);
    let vram = compare(specs.vram_mb, min, rec);

    let (min, rec) = tiers(&|r| needed_score(&r.cpus, specs.cpu));
    let cpu = compare(specs.cpu.map(|cpu| cpu.score), min, rec);

    let (min, rec) = tiers(&|r| needed_score(&r.gpus, specs.gpu));
    let gpu = compare(specs.gpu.map(|gpu| gpu.score), min, rec);

    // Native games don't go through Proton; their DirectX line is for Windows.
    let api = if linux.native {
        None
    } else {
        graphics_api(game, specs)
    };

    let components = [
        (Component::GraphicsApi, api),
        (Component::Cpu, cpu),
        (Component::Gpu, gpu),
        (Component::Ram, ram),
        (Component::Vram, vram),
        (Component::Storage, storage),
    ];
    let known: Vec<(Component, Level)> = components
        .into_iter()
        .filter_map(|(component, level)| Some((component, level?)))
        .collect();
    // Confidence rests on the core three; VRAM doesn't apply to iGPUs.
    let core = [Component::Cpu, Component::Gpu, Component::Ram];
    let compared = known.iter().filter(|(c, _)| core.contains(c)).count();
    let confidence = match compared {
        0 => Confidence::Low,
        3 => Confidence::High,
        _ => Confidence::Partial,
    };
    let worst = known.iter().copied().max_by_key(|(_, level)| *level);
    let blocker = if matches!(linux.anticheat, Some(AntiCheat::Denied | AntiCheat::Broken)) {
        Some(Blocker::AntiCheat)
    } else if !linux.native && linux.protondb == Some(ProtonTier::Borked) {
        Some(Blocker::Proton)
    } else {
        None
    };
    Verdict {
        overall: match blocker {
            Some(_) => Level::Blocked,
            None => worst.map_or(Level::Unknown, |(_, level)| level),
        },
        bottleneck: worst
            .filter(|(_, level)| *level != Level::Recommended)
            .map(|(component, _)| component),
        components: known,
        confidence,
        blocker,
        warnings: specs
            .nouveau
            .then_some(Warning::Nouveau)
            .into_iter()
            .collect(),
    }
}

/// Proton runs DirectX on Vulkan: DXVK (DX9–11) and VKD3D-Proton (DX12) both
/// need Vulkan 1.3.
fn graphics_api(game: &GameRequirements, specs: &Specs) -> Option<Level> {
    let tiers = [&game.minimum, &game.recommended];
    tiers
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|tier| tier.as_ref()?.directx)
        .next()?;
    let vulkan = specs.vulkan?;
    Some(if vulkan >= (1, 3) {
        Level::Recommended
    } else {
        Level::Below
    })
}

/// The score to beat among alternatives: the one from the user's vendor if
/// listed, since publishers pair cards they consider equal; else the lowest.
fn needed_score(alternatives: &[HardwareRef], have: Option<HardwareRef>) -> Option<u32> {
    let same_vendor = have.and_then(|have| alternatives.iter().find(|a| a.vendor == have.vendor));
    same_vendor
        .or_else(|| alternatives.iter().min_by_key(|a| a.score))
        .map(|a| a.score)
}

/// Where `have` falls against the tiers the game lists. `None` if either
/// side is unknown.
fn compare(have: Option<u32>, minimum: Option<u32>, recommended: Option<u32>) -> Option<Level> {
    let have = have?;
    match (minimum, recommended) {
        (None, None) => None,
        (_, Some(recommended)) if have >= recommended => Some(Level::Recommended),
        (Some(minimum), _) if have < minimum => Some(Level::Below),
        // Meets the only tier listed: nothing to fall short of (ROADMAP §2).
        (Some(_), None) => Some(Level::Recommended),
        // Meets minimum, or misses a recommended tier that's the only one listed.
        _ => Some(Level::Minimum),
    }
}

`crates/core/src/parser.rs`:

```rs
//! Reads one tier of Steam's requirement HTML (ROADMAP §8.2).

use std::sync::LazyLock;

use regex::Regex;

/// What a requirement tier says, before hardware names are matched.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ParsedTier {
    /// As written, e.g. "Core i7-6700 or Ryzen 5 1600". Matched to hardware later.
    pub cpu: Option<String>,
    /// As written, e.g. "GeForce GTX 1060 6GB or Radeon RX 580 8GB".
    pub gpu: Option<String>,
    pub ram_mb: Option<u32>,
    /// The smallest video memory the graphics text mentions.
    pub vram_mb: Option<u32>,
    pub storage_mb: Option<u32>,
    /// Major version: "Version 9.0c" → 9.
    pub directx: Option<u8>,
}

pub fn parse(html: &str) -> ParsedTier {
    let fields = fields(html);
    // Steam pages name the same field in several ways.
    let field = |labels: &[&str]| {
        fields
            .iter()
            .find(|(label, _)| labels.contains(&label.as_str()))
            .map(|(_, value)| value.as_str())
    };
    let gpu = field(&["graphics", "video card", "video"]);
    ParsedTier {
        cpu: field(&["processor"]).map(str::to_owned),
        gpu: gpu.map(str::to_owned),
        vram_mb: gpu.and_then(|text| sizes_mb(text).min()),
        ram_mb: field(&["memory"])
            .and_then(size_mb)
            .or_else(|| unlabelled_ram_mb(html)),
        storage_mb: field(&["storage", "hard drive", "hard disk space", "disk space"])
            .and_then(size_mb),
        directx: field(&["directx", "direct x", "directx®"]).and_then(directx_version),
    }
}

/// `("label", "value")` for each `Label: value` line, labels lowercased.
fn fields(html: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)> {
    plain_lines(html)
        .into_iter()
        .filter_map(|line| {
            let (label, value) = line.split_once(':')?;
            Some((label.trim().to_lowercase(), value.trim().to_owned()))
        })
        .collect()
}

/// Steam's requirement HTML as plain text, one line per item, the way the
/// store page reads: what the game page shows next to the parsed values.
pub fn requirement_text(html: &str) -> String {
    plain_lines(html).join("\n")
}

/// The HTML's lines with tags removed and entities decoded, blank ones dropped.
fn plain_lines(html: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    static TAG: LazyLock<Regex> = LazyLock::new(|| Regex::new(r"<[^>]*>").unwrap());
    static BREAK: LazyLock<Regex> =
        LazyLock::new(|| Regex::new(r"(?i)<(br|li|/li|p|/p)\b[^>]*>").unwrap());

    BREAK
        .replace_all(html, "\n")
        .lines()
        .map(|line| {
            decode_entities(&TAG.replace_all(line, ""))
                .trim()
                .to_owned()
        })
        .filter(|line| !line.is_empty())
        .collect()
}

/// The entities Steam's requirement HTML uses. Decoded after tags are
/// stripped, so a decoded `<` can't start a tag.
fn decode_entities(text: &str) -> String {
    text.replace("&quot;", "\"")
        .replace("&reg;", "®")
        .replace("&gt;", ">")
        .replace("&lt;", "<")
        .replace("&nbsp;", " ")
        .replace("&amp;", "&")
}

/// RAM on old pages without labels: "96mb ram", "512MB RAM".
fn unlabelled_ram_mb(html: &str) -> Option<u32> {
    static RAM: LazyLock<Regex> =
        LazyLock::new(|| Regex::new(r"(?i)(\d+(?:\.\d+)?\s*(?:gb|mb))\s+(?:of\s+)?ram\b").unwrap());
    size_mb(&RAM.captures(html)?[1])
}

/// The first version number in a DirectX field: "DirectX® version 9.0c" → 9.
fn directx_version(text: &str) -> Option<u8> {
    static VERSION: LazyLock<Regex> =
        LazyLock::new(|| Regex::new(r"\b(\d{1,2})(?:\.\d)?").unwrap());
    VERSION.captures(text)?[1].parse().ok()
}

/// The first size in `text`, in MB: "8 GB RAM" → 8192, "7.5 GB" → 7680.
fn size_mb(text: &str) -> Option<u32> {
    sizes_mb(text).next()
}

/// Every size in `text`, in MB.
fn sizes_mb(text: &str) -> impl Iterator<Item = u32> {
    static SIZE: LazyLock<Regex> =
        LazyLock::new(|| Regex::new(r"(?i)(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*\+?\s*(gb|mb)").unwrap());
    SIZE.captures_iter(text).filter_map(|caps| {
        let number: f64 = caps[1].parse().ok()?;
        let mb = match caps[2].to_lowercase().as_str() {
            "gb" => number * 1024.0,
            _ => number,
        };
        Some(mb.round() as u32)
    })
}

`crates/core/tests/catalog.rs`:

```rs
//! Tests for the hardware table (`Catalog`): matching the CPU and GPU text
//! from requirements and from /proc to entries in data/hardware.toml.

use rigcheck_core::{Catalog, CatalogEntry};

fn catalog() -> Catalog {
    Catalog::from_toml(include_str!("../../../data/hardware.toml")).expect("valid hardware.toml")
}

fn names(entries: Vec<&CatalogEntry>) -> Vec<&str> {
    entries
        .into_iter()
        .map(|entry| entry.name.as_str())
        .collect()
}

#[test]
fn matches_every_known_gpu_alternative() {
    let catalog = catalog();

    // Baldur's Gate 3, minimum
    let gpus = catalog
        .match_gpus("Nvidia GTX 970 / RX 480 / Intel Arc A380 / Qualcomm Adreno X1 (4GB+ of VRAM)");

    assert_eq!(
        names(gpus),
        ["GeForce GTX 970", "Radeon RX 480", "Arc A380"]
    );
}

#[test]
fn matches_gpus_with_and_without_their_memory_size() {

}

    let cases = [
        // Baldur's Gate 3
        (
            "Intel I5 4690 / AMD FX 8350 / Snapdragon X Elite",
            vec!["Core i5-4690", "FX-8350"],

        // Days Gone
        (

            vec!["Core i5-2500K", "FX-6300"],
        ),
        // Baldur's Gate 3, recommended
        (
            "Intel i7 8700K / AMD r5 3600",
            vec!["Core i7-8700K", "Ryzen 5 3600"],

    for (text, expected) in cases {

    }
}

#[test]
fn finds_cpus_by_their_proc_cpuinfo_name() {
    let catalog = catalog();
    let cases = [
        ("AMD Ryzen 5 7530U with Radeon Graphics", "Ryzen 5 7530U"),
        ("Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-8400 CPU @ 2.80GHz", "Core i5-8400"),
        ("AMD Custom APU 0405", "Custom APU 0405 (Steam Deck)"),
    ];
    for (model, expected) in cases {
        let entry = catalog.match_cpus(model).into_iter().next();
        assert_eq!(entry.map(|e| e.name.as_str()), Some(expected), "{model}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn finds_detected_gpus_by_pci_id() {
    let catalog = catalog();
    let cases = [
        ((0x1002, 0x15e7), Some("Radeon Vega 7 (Ryzen 5000/7000U)")),
        ((0x10de, 0x1c03), Some("GeForce GTX 1060 6GB")),
        ((0x1002, 0x163f), Some("Steam Deck GPU (Van Gogh)")),
        ((0xffff, 0x0001), None),
    ];
    for ((vendor, device), expected) in cases {
        let entry = catalog.gpu_by_pci(vendor, device);
        assert_eq!(
            entry.map(|e| e.name.as_str()),
            expected,
            "{vendor:04x}:{device:04x}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn memory_sizes_written_with_a_space_still_match() {
    let catalog = catalog();

    // ELDEN RING, minimum
    let gpus = catalog.match_gpus("NVIDIA GEFORCE GTX 1060 3 GB or AMD RADEON RX 580 4 GB");

    assert_eq!(names(gpus), ["GeForce GTX 1060 3GB", "Radeon RX 580"]);
}

#[test]
fn a_bare_model_number_reuses_the_previous_names_series() {
    let catalog = catalog();

    // Call of Duty, minimum: "GTX 970 / 1060" means GTX 970 or GTX 1060.
    let gpus = catalog
        .match_gpus("AMD Radeon™ RX 470, NVIDIA® GeForce® GTX 970 / 1060 or Intel® Arc™ A580");

    assert_eq!(
        names(gpus),
        [
            "Radeon RX 470",
            "GeForce GTX 970",
            "GeForce GTX 1060 6GB",
            "Arc A580"
        ]
    );
}

```rs
//! Tests for `evaluate(game, specs, linux)`, which turns requirements and the
//! user's specs into a verdict (ROADMAP §2 "Verdict levels", §8.3).

use rigcheck_core::{
    AntiCheat, Blocker, Component, Confidence, GameRequirements, HardwareRef, Level, LinuxInfo,
    ProtonTier, Requirement, Specs, Vendor, Warning, evaluate,
};

/// A game that only states RAM, in MB.
fn needs_ram(minimum: u32, recommended: u32) -> GameRequirements {
    GameRequirements {
        minimum: Some(Requirement {
            ram_mb: Some(minimum),
            ..Requirement::default()
        }),
        recommended: Some(Requirement {
            ram_mb: Some(recommended),
            ..Requirement::default()
        }),
    }
}

fn with_ram(ram_mb: u32) -> Specs {
    Specs {
        ram_mb: Some(ram_mb),
        ..Specs::default()
    }
}

#[test]
fn meeting_recommended_specs_is_recommended() {
    let verdict = evaluate(
        &needs_ram(8192, 16384),
        &with_ram(32768),
        &LinuxInfo::default(),
    );

    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, Level::Recommended);
}

#[test]
fn meeting_only_minimum_specs_is_minimum() {
    let verdict = evaluate(
        &needs_ram(8192, 16384),
        &with_ram(12288),
        &LinuxInfo::default(),
    );

    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, Level::Minimum);
}

#[test]
fn falling_short_of_minimum_is_below_and_names_the_component() {
    let verdict = evaluate(
        &needs_ram(8192, 16384),
        &with_ram(4096),
        &LinuxInfo::default(),
    );

    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, Level::Below);
    assert_eq!(verdict.bottleneck, Some(Component::Ram));
}

/// The kernel and the iGPU keep part of installed RAM, so a 16 GB laptop
/// reports 15,746,968 kB (15,377 MiB) in /proc/meminfo.
#[test]
fn a_16_gb_laptop_meets_a_16_gb_requirement() {
    let verdict = evaluate(
        &needs_ram(8192, 16384),
        &with_ram(15377),
        &LinuxInfo::default(),
    );

    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, Level::Recommended);
}

#[test]
fn a_14_gb_machine_does_not_meet_16_gb() {
    let verdict = evaluate(
        &needs_ram(8192, 16384),
        &with_ram(14336),
        &LinuxInfo::default(),
    );

    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, Level::Minimum);
}

/// A game whose tiers each list GPU alternatives ("GTX 1060 or RX 580").
fn needs_gpu(minimum: &[HardwareRef], recommended: &[HardwareRef]) -> GameRequirements {
    GameRequirements {
        minimum: Some(Requirement {
            gpus: minimum.to_vec(),
            ..Requirement::default()
        }),
        recommended: Some(Requirement {
            gpus: recommended.to_vec(),
            ..Requirement::default()
        }),
    }
}

fn hw(vendor: Vendor, score: u32) -> HardwareRef {
    HardwareRef { vendor, score }
}

fn with_gpu(gpu: HardwareRef) -> Specs {
    Specs {
        gpu: Some(gpu),
        ..Specs::default()
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_gpu_slower_than_the_minimum_is_the_bottleneck() {
    let game = needs_gpu(&[hw(Vendor::Nvidia, 100)], &[hw(Vendor::Nvidia, 200)]);

    let verdict = evaluate(&game, &with_gpu(hw(Vendor::Amd, 60)), &LinuxInfo::default());

    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, Level::Below);
    assert_eq!(verdict.bottleneck, Some(Component::Gpu));
}

#[test]
fn gpus_are_compared_with_the_same_vendors_alternative() {
    // "GTX 1060 or RX 580", where our scores put the RX 580 higher.
    let game = needs_gpu(
        &[hw(Vendor::Nvidia, 80), hw(Vendor::Amd, 100)],
        &[hw(Vendor::Nvidia, 160), hw(Vendor::Amd, 200)],
    );

    let verdict = evaluate(&game, &with_gpu(hw(Vendor::Amd, 90)), &LinuxInfo::default());

    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, Level::Below);
}

#[test]
fn without_a_same_vendor_alternative_the_lowest_one_counts() {
    let game = needs_gpu(
        &[hw(Vendor::Nvidia, 80), hw(Vendor::Amd, 100)],
        &[hw(Vendor::Nvidia, 160), hw(Vendor::Amd, 200)],
    );

    let verdict = evaluate(
        &game,
        &with_gpu(hw(Vendor::Intel, 90)),
        &LinuxInfo::default(),
    );

    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, Level::Minimum);
}

#[test]
fn a_cpu_slower_than_the_minimum_is_the_bottleneck() {
    let game = GameRequirements {
        minimum: Some(Requirement {
            cpus: vec![hw(Vendor::Intel, 100), hw(Vendor::Amd, 90)],
            ..Requirement::default()
        }),
        recommended: None,
    };
    let specs = Specs {
        cpu: Some(hw(Vendor::Amd, 70)),
        ..Specs::default()
    };

    let verdict = evaluate(&game, &specs, &LinuxInfo::default());

    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, Level::Below);
    assert_eq!(verdict.bottleneck, Some(Component::Cpu));
}

#[test]
fn a_game_without_requirements_is_unknown() {
    let verdict = evaluate(
        &GameRequirements::default(),
        &with_ram(16384),
        &LinuxInfo::default(),
    );

    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, Level::Unknown);
    assert_eq!(verdict.confidence, Confidence::Low);
}

#[test]
fn a_verdict_from_some_components_has_partial_confidence() {
    // The store page lists RAM, but its CPU and GPU weren't recognized.
    let verdict = evaluate(
        &needs_ram(8192, 16384),
        &with_ram(32768),
        &LinuxInfo::default(),
    );

    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, Level::Recommended);
    assert_eq!(verdict.confidence, Confidence::Partial);
}

#[test]
fn anti_cheat_that_denies_linux_blocks_the_game() {
    let linux = LinuxInfo {
        anticheat: Some(AntiCheat::Denied),
        ..LinuxInfo::default()
    };

    let verdict = evaluate(&needs_ram(8192, 16384), &with_ram(32768), &linux);

    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, Level::Blocked);
    assert_eq!(verdict.blocker, Some(Blocker::AntiCheat));
}

#[test]
fn anti_cheat_that_is_broken_on_linux_blocks_the_game() {
    let linux = LinuxInfo {
        anticheat: Some(AntiCheat::Broken),
        ..LinuxInfo::default()
    };

    let verdict = evaluate(&needs_ram(8192, 16384), &with_ram(32768), &linux);

    assert_eq!(verdict.blocker, Some(Blocker::AntiCheat));
}

#[test]
fn a_borked_protondb_rating_blocks_the_game() {
    let linux = LinuxInfo {
        protondb: Some(ProtonTier::Borked),
        ..LinuxInfo::default()
    };

    let verdict = evaluate(&needs_ram(8192, 16384), &with_ram(32768), &linux);

    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, Level::Blocked);
    assert_eq!(verdict.blocker, Some(Blocker::Proton));
}

#[test]
fn a_borked_proton_rating_does_not_block_a_native_linux_game() {
    let linux = LinuxInfo {
        native: true,
        protondb: Some(ProtonTier::Borked),
        ..LinuxInfo::default()
    };

    let verdict = evaluate(&needs_ram(8192, 16384), &with_ram(32768), &linux);

    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, Level::Recommended);
    assert_eq!(verdict.blocker, None);
}

#[test]
fn igpu_users_get_high_confidence_when_cpu_gpu_and_ram_compare() {
    let tier = |cpu, gpu, ram_mb, vram_mb| Requirement {
        cpus: vec![hw(Vendor::Amd, cpu)],
        gpus: vec![hw(Vendor::Amd, gpu)],
        ram_mb: Some(ram_mb),
        vram_mb: Some(vram_mb),
        ..Requirement::default()
    };
    let game = GameRequirements {
        minimum: Some(tier(50, 50, 8192, 2048)),
        recommended: Some(tier(100, 100, 16384, 4096)),
    };
    let specs = Specs {
        cpu: Some(hw(Vendor::Amd, 120)),
        gpu: Some(hw(Vendor::Amd, 120)),
        ram_mb: Some(15377),
        vram_mb: None,
        ..Specs::default()
    };

    let verdict = evaluate(&game, &specs, &LinuxInfo::default());

    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, Level::Recommended);
    assert_eq!(verdict.confidence, Confidence::High);
}

    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, Level::Below);
    assert_eq!(verdict.bottleneck, Some(Component::Storage));
}

        nouveau: true,
        ..Specs::default()
    };

    let verdict = evaluate(&needs_ram(8192, 16384), &specs, &LinuxInfo::default());

    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, Level::Recommended);
    assert_eq!(verdict.warnings, [Warning::Nouveau]);
}

/// ROADMAP §2: Minimum means "at least one falls short of recommended". With no
/// recommended tier there's nothing to fall short of.
#[test]
fn meeting_the_only_tier_listed_is_recommended() {
    let game = GameRequirements {
        minimum: Some(Requirement {
            ram_mb: Some(256),
            ..Requirement::default()
        }),
        recommended: None,
    };

    let verdict = evaluate(&game, &with_ram(15377), &LinuxInfo::default());

    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, Level::Recommended);
}

#[test]
fn the_verdict_lists_each_compared_components_level() {
    let mut game = needs_gpu(&[hw(Vendor::Nvidia, 100)], &[hw(Vendor::Nvidia, 200)]);
    for (tier, ram_mb) in [(&mut game.minimum, 8192), (&mut game.recommended, 16384)] {
        tier.as_mut().unwrap().ram_mb = Some(ram_mb);
    }
    let specs = Specs {
        gpu: Some(hw(Vendor::Nvidia, 60)),
        ram_mb: Some(12288),
        ..Specs::default()
    };

    let verdict = evaluate(&game, &specs, &LinuxInfo::default());

    // CPU, VRAM, storage and the graphics API weren't stated or known.
    assert_eq!(
        verdict.components,
        [
            (Component::Gpu, Level::Below),
            (Component::Ram, Level::Minimum)
        ]
    );
}

`crates/core/tests/parser.rs`:

```rs
//! Tests for `parse(html)`, which reads one tier of a Steam store page's
//! requirements. Inputs are real strings from data/fixtures/requirements/.

use std::sync::LazyLock;

use rigcheck_core::parse;
use serde_json::Value;

static CORPUS: LazyLock<Vec<Value>> = LazyLock::new(|| {
    let path = concat!(
        env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
        "/../../data/fixtures/requirements/corpus.json"
    );
    serde_json::from_str(&std::fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap()).unwrap()
});

/// The raw HTML of a game's tier ("minimum" or "recommended").
fn tier(app_id: u64, tier: &str) -> &'static str {
    CORPUS
        .iter()
        .find(|game| game["app_id"] == app_id)
        .and_then(|game| game[tier].as_str())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{app_id} has no {tier} in the corpus"))
}

const BALDURS_GATE_3: u64 = 1086940;

#[test]
fn reads_memory() {
    // "Memory: 8 GB RAM"
    let parsed = parse(tier(BALDURS_GATE_3, "minimum"));

    assert_eq!(parsed.ram_mb, Some(8 * 1024));
}

#[test]
fn reads_storage_under_any_label() {
    let cases = [
        (
            BALDURS_GATE_3,
            "Storage: 150 GB available space",
            150 * 1024,
        ),
        (500, "Hard Drive: At least 7.5 GB of free space", 7680),
        (
            2280,
            "Disk Space: Minimum 2GB free space on hard drive",
            2048,
        ),
        (3590, "Hard Drive: 65+MB of free hard drive space", 65),
        (22380, "Hard Disk Space: 10GB free space", 10 * 1024),
    ];
    for (app_id, line, mb) in cases {
        assert_eq!(
            parse(tier(app_id, "minimum")).storage_mb,
            Some(mb),
            "{line}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn reads_the_directx_version_under_any_label() {
    let cases = [
        (BALDURS_GATE_3, "minimum", "DirectX: Version 11", 11),
        (2280, "minimum", "Direct X: Version 12", 12),
        (8930, "minimum", "DirectX®: DirectX® version 9.0c", 9),
        (8930, "recommended", "DirectX®: DirectX® version 11", 11),
    ];
    for (app_id, which, line, version) in cases {
        assert_eq!(parse(tier(app_id, which)).directx, Some(version), "{line}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn keeps_the_cpu_and_gpu_text() {
    let parsed = parse(tier(BALDURS_GATE_3, "minimum"));

    assert_eq!(
        parsed.cpu.as_deref(),
        Some("Intel I5 4690 / AMD FX 8350 / Snapdragon X Elite")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        parsed.gpu.as_deref(),
        Some("Nvidia GTX 970 / RX 480 / Intel Arc A380 / Qualcomm Adreno X1 (4GB+ of VRAM)")
    );
}

#[test]
fn reads_the_gpu_under_video_card() {
    // Fallout: New Vegas
    let parsed = parse(tier(22380, "minimum"));

    assert_eq!(
        parsed.gpu.as_deref(),
        Some("NVIDIA GeForce 6 series, ATI 1300XT series")
    );
}

#[test]
fn reads_the_gpu_under_video() {
    // Warframe
    let parsed = parse(tier(230410, "minimum"));

    assert_eq!(
        parsed.gpu.as_deref(),
        Some("DirectX 11+ capable Graphics Card")
    );
}

#[test]
fn decodes_html_entities() {
    // PAYDAY 2: "NVIDIA &amp; AMD (1GB VRAM ..."
    let gpu = parse(tier(218620, "minimum")).gpu.unwrap();

    assert!(gpu.starts_with("NVIDIA & AMD"), "{gpu}");
}

#[test]
fn reads_vram_from_the_graphics_text() {
    let cases = [
        (
            BALDURS_GATE_3,
            "... Qualcomm Adreno X1 (4GB+ of VRAM)",
            Some(4096),
        ),
        // Cyberpunk 2077: the smallest card listed sets the bar.
        (
            1091500,
            "GeForce GTX 1060 6GB or Radeon RX 580 8GB or Arc A380",
            Some(6144),
        ),
        // Skyrim
        (
            72850,
            "Direct X 9.0c compliant video card with 512 MB of RAM",
            Some(512),
        ),
        // Fallout: New Vegas
        (22380, "NVIDIA GeForce 6 series, ATI 1300XT series", None),
    ];
    for (app_id, line, mb) in cases {
        assert_eq!(parse(tier(app_id, "minimum")).vram_mb, mb, "{line}");
    }
}

/// ROADMAP Phase 3: at least 90% of the corpus parses. A tier counts when
/// its CPU, GPU and RAM all come out; the matcher needs those three.
#[test]
fn at_least_90_percent_of_the_corpus_parses() {
    let tiers: Vec<(String, &str)> = CORPUS
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|game| {
            ["minimum", "recommended"]
                .into_iter()
                .filter_map(move |which| {
                    let html = game[which].as_str()?;
                    Some((format!("{} {which}", game["name"]), html))
                })
        })
        .collect();

    let failed: Vec<&String> = tiers
        .iter()
        .filter(|(_, html)| {
            let parsed = parse(html);
            parsed.cpu.is_none() || parsed.gpu.is_none() || parsed.ram_mb.is_none()
        })
        .map(|(name, _)| name)
        .collect();

    let rate = 1.0 - failed.len() as f64 / tiers.len() as f64;
    assert!(
        rate >= 0.9,
        "{:.1}% parsed; failed: {failed:#?}",
        rate * 100.0
    );
}

#[test]
fn finds_ram_in_unlabelled_text() {
    let cases = [
        // Half-Life: "500 mhz processor, 96mb ram, 16mb video card, ..."
        (70, 96),
        // Medieval II: "... 512MB RAM ..." in an unlabelled list
        (4700, 512),
    ];
    for (app_id, mb) in cases {
        assert_eq!(parse(tier(app_id, "minimum")).ram_mb, Some(mb), "{app_id}");
    }
}

/// What the parser makes of every tier in the corpus, reviewed by hand once.
/// A parser change that moves any value shows up as a diff in
/// `snapshots/parser__corpus.snap`; accept it with `cargo insta review`.
#[test]
fn corpus() {
    let parsed: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, _> = CORPUS
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|game| {
            ["minimum", "recommended"]
                .into_iter()
                .filter_map(move |which| {
                    let html = game[which].as_str()?;
                    let app_id = game["app_id"].as_u64()?;
                    let key = format!("{app_id:07} {} ({which})", game["name"].as_str()?);
                    Some((key, parse(html)))
                })
        })
        .collect();

    insta::assert_debug_snapshot!(parsed);
}
