`crates/net/src/client.rs`:

```rs
//! The HTTP client: every request and redirect checked against an
//! [`Allowlist`], paced by a [`RateLimiter`], retried per [`Retry`].

use std::io::{Read, Write};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use crate::{Allowlist, RateLimiter, Retry};

pub type Error = Box<dyn std::error::Error + Send + Sync>;

const USER_AGENT: &str = concat!(
    "rigcheck/",
    env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"),
    " (+https://github.com/Glory42/rigcheck)"
);

/// Long enough for the 50 MB games.db budget on a slow (~0.5 Mbit/s) line.
const DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(15 * 60);

pub struct Client {
    http: reqwest::blocking::Client,
    allowlist: Allowlist,
    limiter: RateLimiter,
    retry: Retry,
    started: Instant,
}

impl Client {
    pub fn new(allowlist: Allowlist, limiter: RateLimiter, retry: Retry) -> Result<Client, Error> {
        let redirects = allowlist.clone();
        let http = reqwest::blocking::Client::builder()
            .user_agent(USER_AGENT)
            // A redirect to a host off the list is refused like any request.
            .redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::custom(move |attempt| {
                if attempt.previous().len() > 5 {
                    attempt.error("too many redirects")
                } else if redirects.allows(attempt.url().as_str()) {
                    attempt.follow()
                } else {
                    attempt.error("redirect to a host that isn't allowed")
                }
            }))
            .build()?;
        Ok(Client {
            http,
            allowlist,
            limiter,
            retry,
            started: Instant::now(),
        })
    }

    /// The body of `url`. Errors never include the URL, which can carry an
    /// API key and end up in CI logs.
    pub fn get_text(&mut self, url: &str) -> Result<String, Error> {
        Ok(self.get(url, None)?.text().map_err(|e| e.without_url())?)
    }

    /// Streams the body of `url` into `to`, calling `progress` with the bytes
    /// written so far after each chunk. Returns the total.
    pub fn download(
        &mut self,
        url: &str,
        to: &mut impl Write,
        mut progress: impl FnMut(u64),
    ) -> Result<u64, Error> {
        let mut response = self.get(url, Some(DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT))?;
        let mut buffer = vec![0; 64 * 1024];
        let mut done = 0;
        loop {
            let read = response.read(&mut buffer)?;
            if read == 0 {
                return Ok(done);
            }
            to.write_all(&buffer[..read])?;
            done += read as u64;
            progress(done);
        }
    }

    /// A successful response for `url`, after any retries. `timeout` covers
    /// the whole request including reading the body (reqwest's blocking
    /// client defaults to 30 seconds).
    fn get(
        &mut self,
        url: &str,
        timeout: Option<Duration>,
    ) -> Result<reqwest::blocking::Response, Error> {
        if !self.allowlist.allows(url) {
            return Err("host isn't on the allowlist".into());
        }
        for attempt in 1.. {
            std::thread::sleep(self.limiter.wait(self.started.elapsed()));
            let mut request = self.http.get(url);
            if let Some(timeout) = timeout {
                request = request.timeout(timeout);
            }
            let response = request.send().map_err(|e| e.without_url())?;
            let status = response.status();
            if status.is_success() {
                return Ok(response);
            }
            match self.retry.after(status.as_u16(), attempt) {
                Some(wait) => std::thread::sleep(wait),
                None => return Err(format!("HTTP {status}").into()),
            }
        }
        unreachable!("the loop only ends by returning")
    }
}

`crates/net/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! The only crate allowed to make network requests. Every request goes to a
//! host on an [`Allowlist`] (ROADMAP §6); `deny.toml` keeps HTTP clients out
//! of other crates.

mod client;
mod limit;

use url::Url;

pub use client::{Client, Error};
pub use limit::{RateLimiter, Retry};

/// The hosts a program may send requests to, over HTTPS only.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Allowlist {
    hosts: &'static [&'static str],
}

impl Allowlist {
    /// The desktop app: GitHub Releases (games.db, served from GitHub's
    /// asset host after a redirect), Steam's store API (live lookups) and
    /// Steam's image CDN. Nothing else, ever (ROADMAP §6).
    pub fn app() -> Allowlist {
        Allowlist {
            hosts: &[
                "github.com",
                "release-assets.githubusercontent.com",
                "store.steampowered.com",
                "shared.akamai.steamstatic.com",
            ],
        }
    }

    /// The data pipeline: the app's hosts plus its data sources (Steam Web
    /// API for the app list, GitHub files for ProtonDB and AreWeAntiCheatYet).
    pub fn pipeline() -> Allowlist {
        Allowlist {
            hosts: &[
                "github.com",
                "release-assets.githubusercontent.com",
                "store.steampowered.com",
                "shared.akamai.steamstatic.com",
                "api.steampowered.com",
                "raw.githubusercontent.com",
            ],
        }
    }

    /// Whether a request to `url` is allowed.
    pub fn allows(&self, url: &str) -> bool {
        let Ok(url) = Url::parse(url) else {
            return false;
        };
        url.scheme() == "https"
            && url
                .host_str()
                .is_some_and(|host| self.hosts.contains(&host))
    }
}

`crates/net/src/limit.rs`:

```rs
//! Staying under a server's request limit.

use std::collections::VecDeque;
use std::time::Duration;

/// At most `max` requests in any `window`. Time is passed in (time since
/// start), so callers own the clock and tests can fake it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct RateLimiter {
    max: usize,
    window: Duration,
    /// When the requests still inside the window were sent.
    sent: VecDeque<Duration>,
}

impl RateLimiter {
    pub fn new(max: usize, window: Duration) -> RateLimiter {
        RateLimiter {
            max,
            window,
            sent: VecDeque::with_capacity(max),
        }
    }

    /// How long to wait before sending a request at `now`. The request is
    /// counted as sent once that wait is over.
    pub fn wait(&mut self, now: Duration) -> Duration {
        let wait = if self.sent.len() < self.max {
            Duration::ZERO
        } else {
            let oldest = self.sent.pop_front().expect("the window is full");
            (oldest + self.window).saturating_sub(now)
        };
        self.sent.push_back(now + wait);
        wait
    }
}

/// When to try a failed request again: rate limits (429) and server errors
/// (5xx) are retried with doubling waits; other failures are final.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Retry {
    max_retries: u32,
    first_wait: Duration,
}

impl Retry {
    pub fn new(max_retries: u32, first_wait: Duration) -> Retry {
        Retry {
            max_retries,
            first_wait,
        }
    }

    /// How long to wait after the `attempt`-th failure with `status`, or
    /// `None` to give up.
    pub fn after(&self, status: u16, attempt: u32) -> Option<Duration> {
        let retryable = status == 429 || (500..600).contains(&status);
        (retryable && attempt <= self.max_retries).then(|| self.first_wait * 2u32.pow(attempt - 1))
    }
}

```

`crates/net/tests/rate_limit.rs`:

```rs
//! Tests for staying under Steam's limits: a sliding-window rate limiter and
//! retry with backoff. Time is passed in, so tests control the clock.

use std::time::Duration;

use rigcheck_net::{RateLimiter, Retry};

const fn secs(s: u64) -> Duration {
    Duration::from_secs(s)
}

#[test]
fn requests_wait_once_the_window_is_full() {
    let mut limiter = RateLimiter::new(3, secs(10));

    assert_eq!(limiter.wait(secs(0)), secs(0));
    assert_eq!(limiter.wait(secs(1)), secs(0));
    assert_eq!(limiter.wait(secs(2)), secs(0));
    // The first request leaves the window at 10 s.
    assert_eq!(limiter.wait(secs(4)), secs(6));
    // That waited request was sent at 10 s; the next slot opens at 11 s.
    assert_eq!(limiter.wait(secs(10)), secs(1));
}

#[test]
fn rate_limits_and_server_errors_are_retried_with_growing_waits() {
    let retry = Retry::new(3, secs(2));

    // `after(status, attempt)`: attempt is how many tries have failed so far.
    assert_eq!(retry.after(429, 1), Some(secs(2)));
    assert_eq!(retry.after(503, 2), Some(secs(4)));
    assert_eq!(retry.after(429, 3), Some(secs(8)));
    assert_eq!(retry.after(429, 4), None, "gives up after 3 retries");
}

#[test]
fn other_errors_are_not_retried() {
    let retry = Retry::new(3, secs(2));

    assert_eq!(retry.after(404, 1), None);
    assert_eq!(retry.after(403, 1), None);
}

`crates/steam/src/lib.rs`:

```rs
//! Steam install and library discovery.
//!
//! `steamlocate` parses Steam's files; this crate decides where to look and
//! what counts as a game.

use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use steamlocate::{Library, SteamDir};

/// A game installed in one of the user's Steam libraries.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct InstalledGame {
    pub app_id: u32,
    pub name: String,
    pub size_on_disk: u64,
    pub install_dir: PathBuf,
}

/// Where Steam installs itself, relative to the home directory.
const INSTALL_DIRS: &[&str] = &[
    ".local/share/Steam",
    ".steam/steam", // older installs and Debian's package
    ".var/app/com.valvesoftware.Steam/.local/share/Steam", // Flatpak
];

/// Lists the games installed by every Steam install under `home`.
pub fn installed_games(home: &Path) -> Vec<InstalledGame> {
    libraries(home).iter().flat_map(games_in).collect()
}

/// Every library of every Steam install under `home`, each listed once.
fn libraries(home: &Path) -> Vec<Library> {
    let mut seen = HashSet::new();
    let mut libraries = Vec::new();
    for dir in INSTALL_DIRS {
        let Ok(steam) = SteamDir::from_dir(&home.join(dir)) else {
            continue;
        };
        let Ok(found) = steam.libraries() else {
            continue;
        };
        for library in found.flatten() {
            // Symlinks and shared drives can make two installs list the same library.
            if let Ok(real_path) = library.path().canonicalize()
                && seen.insert(real_path)
            {
                libraries.push(library);
            }
        }
    }
    libraries
}

fn games_in(library: &Library) -> Vec<InstalledGame> {
    let mut games = Vec::new();
    for app in library.apps().flatten() {
        let name = app.name.clone().unwrap_or_default();
        if is_steam_tool(&name) {
            continue;
        }
        games.push(InstalledGame {
            install_dir: library.resolve_app_dir(&app),
            app_id: app.app_id,
            name,
            size_on_disk: app.size_on_disk.unwrap_or_default(),
        });
    }
    games
}

/// Steam installs these like games, but they're compatibility tools and shared
/// libraries. Matching names catches new Proton versions without an ID list.
fn is_steam_tool(name: &str) -> bool {
    name.starts_with("Proton ")
        || name.starts_with("Steam Linux Runtime")
        || name == "Steamworks Common Redistributables"
}

/// Steam's cached cover art for an app (`appcache/librarycache/<id>/library_600x900.jpg`,
/// sometimes one folder deeper), so covers show without any download.
pub fn cover_art(home: &Path, app_id: u32) -> Option<PathBuf> {
    const FILE: &str = "library_600x900.jpg";
    INSTALL_DIRS.iter().find_map(|install| {
        let dir = home
            .join(install)
            .join("appcache/librarycache")
            .join(app_id.to_string());
        let direct = dir.join(FILE);
        if direct.is_file() {
            return Some(direct);
        }
        std::fs::read_dir(&dir)
            .ok()?
            .flatten()
            .map(|entry| entry.path().join(FILE))
            .find(|path| path.is_file())
    })
}

`crates/steam/tests/installed_games.rs`:

```rs
//! Tests for the crate's public seam, `installed_games(home)`.
//!
//! Each test builds a fake home directory in a temp dir and fills it with real
//! Steam files from `data/fixtures/steam/`.

use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use rigcheck_steam::{InstalledGame, installed_games};
use tempfile::TempDir;

const FIXTURES: &str = concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/../../data/fixtures/steam");

/// Creates a Steam install at `home/relative` whose `libraryfolders.vdf`
/// lists the install itself followed by `extra_libraries`.
fn steam_install(home: &Path, relative: &str, extra_libraries: &[&Path]) -> PathBuf {
    let steam = home.join(relative);
    fs::create_dir_all(steam.join("steamapps")).unwrap();

    let mut vdf = String::from("\"libraryfolders\"\n{\n");
    for (i, library) in [steam.as_path()].iter().chain(extra_libraries).enumerate() {
        vdf += &format!(
            "\t\"{i}\"\n\t{{\n\t\t\"path\"\t\t\"{}\"\n\t}}\n",
            library.display()
        );
    }
    vdf += "}\n";
    fs::write(steam.join("steamapps/libraryfolders.vdf"), vdf).unwrap();

    steam
}

/// Installs the fixture manifest for `app_id` into `library`.
fn install(library: &Path, app_id: u32) {
    let manifest = format!("appmanifest_{app_id}.acf");
    fs::create_dir_all(library.join("steamapps")).unwrap();
    fs::copy(
        Path::new(FIXTURES).join(&manifest),
        library.join("steamapps").join(&manifest),
    )
    .unwrap();
}

#[test]
fn finds_a_game_in_the_default_steam_install() {
    let home = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let steam = steam_install(home.path(), ".local/share/Steam", &[]);
    install(&steam, 1150690);

    let games = installed_games(home.path());

    assert_eq!(
        games,
        [InstalledGame {
            app_id: 1150690,
            name: "OMORI".to_owned(),
            size_on_disk: 2_039_368_158,
            install_dir: steam.join("steamapps/common/OMORI"),
        }]
    );
}

#[test]
fn skips_proton_runtimes_and_redistributables() {
    let home = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let steam = steam_install(home.path(), ".local/share/Steam", &[]);
    for app_id in [1150690, 1493710, 4183110, 228980] {
        install(&steam, app_id);
    }

    let games = installed_games(home.path());

    assert_eq!(app_ids(&games), [1150690]);
}

#[test]
fn finds_games_in_libraries_on_other_drives() {
    let home = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let drive = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let steam = steam_install(home.path(), ".local/share/Steam", &[drive.path()]);
    install(&steam, 1150690);
    install(drive.path(), 21000);

    let games = installed_games(home.path());

    assert_eq!(app_ids(&games), [21000, 1150690]);
}

#[test]
fn finds_games_in_a_flatpak_steam_install() {
    let home = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let steam = steam_install(
        home.path(),
        ".var/app/com.valvesoftware.Steam/.local/share/Steam",
        &[],
    );
    install(&steam, 1150690);

    let games = installed_games(home.path());

    assert_eq!(app_ids(&games), [1150690]);
}

#[test]
fn finds_games_in_a_steam_install_under_dot_steam() {
    let home = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let steam = steam_install(home.path(), ".steam/steam", &[]);
    install(&steam, 1150690);

    let games = installed_games(home.path());

    assert_eq!(app_ids(&games), [1150690]);
}

#[test]
fn lists_each_game_once_when_dot_steam_links_to_the_install() {
    let home = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let steam = steam_install(home.path(), ".local/share/Steam", &[]);
    install(&steam, 1150690);
    fs::create_dir(home.path().join(".steam")).unwrap();
    std::os::unix::fs::symlink(&steam, home.path().join(".steam/steam")).unwrap();

    let games = installed_games(home.path());

    assert_eq!(app_ids(&games), [1150690]);
}

/// The app IDs of `games`, sorted so tests don't depend on directory order.
fn app_ids(games: &[InstalledGame]) -> Vec<u32> {
    let mut ids: Vec<u32> = games.iter().map(|game| game.app_id).collect();
    ids.sort_unstable();
    ids
}

`data/fixtures/hardware/README.md`:

```md
# Hardware fixtures

Fake filesystem roots for `crates/hardware/tests/`. Each directory mirrors the files hardware detection reads (`proc/`, `sys/`, `etc/`), and `commands/<program>.txt` holds what `vulkaninfo --summary` and `nvidia-smi` printed. A missing `commands/` file means the program isn't installed.

| Fixture | Machine | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `amd-laptop` | Ryzen 5 7530U, Radeon iGPU | Real, from `capture.sh` (connector `card1-eDP-1` and render node `renderD128` added by hand from the same machine) |
| `amd-desktop` | Ryzen 5 5600X, RX 6600 | Hand-written |
| `nvidia-desktop` | i5-8400, GTX 1060 6GB | Hand-written |
| `intel-laptop` | i5-8250U, UHD 620 | Hand-written |
| `hybrid-laptop` | i7-9750H, UHD 630 + GTX 1650 Mobile | Hand-written |
| `steam-deck` | Steam Deck LCD | Hand-written |

Hand-written fixtures use real PCI IDs and the real file formats, but only the lines detection reads. Replace them with real captures when you can.

## Capturing a real machine

```sh
data/fixtures/hardware/capture.sh nvidia-desktop
```

It copies only the files listed in the script and runs `vulkaninfo --summary` and `nvidia-smi` if they're installed. Nothing is uploaded. Read through the output before committing it.

```

`data/fixtures/hardware/capture.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# Copies the files and command output rigcheck's hardware detection reads into
# a new fixture directory, so tests can replay this machine.
#
# Usage: ./capture.sh <fixture-name>     e.g. ./capture.sh nvidia-desktop
#
# Nothing is uploaded. Look through the output before committing it.
set -eu

[ $# -eq 1 ] || { echo "usage: $0 <fixture-name>" >&2; exit 1; }
out="$(dirname "$0")/$1"

copy() {
    [ -r "$1" ] || return 0
    mkdir -p "$out$(dirname "$1")"
    cp "$1" "$out$1"
}

copy /proc/cpuinfo
copy /proc/meminfo
copy /proc/sys/kernel/osrelease
copy /etc/os-release
copy /sys/module/nvidia/version

for entry in /sys/class/drm/*; do
    case "$(basename "$entry")" in
    card*-* | renderD*) # connectors and render nodes: detection must skip these
        copy "$entry/device/uevent" ;;
    card*)
        for file in vendor device uevent mem_info_vram_total; do
            copy "$entry/device/$file"
        done ;;
    esac
done

mkdir -p "$out/commands"
if command -v vulkaninfo >/dev/null; then
    vulkaninfo --summary >"$out/commands/vulkaninfo.txt" 2>/dev/null || true
fi
if command -v nvidia-smi >/dev/null; then
    nvidia-smi --query-gpu=pci.device_id,memory.total --format=csv,noheader,nounits \
        >"$out/commands/nvidia-smi.txt" || true
fi

echo "captured into $out"

```

# ProtonDB fixtures

`reports.json`: 20 real reports, verbatim, from ProtonDB's `reports_oct1_2026.tar.gz` dump ([bdefore/protondb-data](https://github.com/bdefore/protondb-data)). ProtonDB's data is licensed under the [ODbL](http://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/).

Picked to exercise the tier rule (ROADMAP §9): every report for Lara Croft GO (540840), Act of War: High Treason (9760), Chompy Chomp Chomp (292570) and Bye Sweet Carole (2428980), plus one report on a native Linux build (3493540), and one Way of the Samurai 3 (427510) report whose `appId` is a number, as about 8% of the dump's are. Tests treat 2026-10-01 as "now".

```

`data/fixtures/requirements/fetch.py`:

```py
"""Builds the parser corpus: raw PC requirement HTML from Steam's store API.

Dev-only. The app and tests never fetch; they read corpus.json.

    python3 data/fixtures/requirements/fetch.py

Re-running re-fetches everything (one request every 1.5 s) and overwrites
corpus.json. Unknown or removed app IDs are skipped.
"""

import json
import pathlib
import time
import urllib.request

USER_AGENT = "rigcheck-dev/0.0 (corpus builder; +https://github.com/Glory42/rigcheck)"

# Varied on purpose: new AAA, old classics, indies, sims, strategy, VR and
# games whose pages are known to be odd.
APP_IDS = [
    10, 70, 220, 240, 400, 440, 500, 550, 570, 620, 730, 2280, 3590, 4000, 4700,
    8930, 12100, 12120, 12210, 21000, 22380, 39210, 47890, 72850, 105600, 218620,
    227300, 230230, 230410, 236390, 236850, 244210, 250900, 252490, 255710, 264710,
    268910, 270880, 271590, 275850, 281990, 289070, 292030, 294100, 322330, 346110,
    359550, 367520, 374320, 377160, 379720, 381210, 391540, 394360, 413150, 427520,
    435150, 444090, 489830, 504230, 524220, 546560, 550650, 570940, 578080, 582010,
    582160, 588650, 594570, 601150, 646570, 739630, 782330, 805550, 812140, 814380,
    848450, 863550, 883710, 892970, 945360, 949230, 952060, 976730, 990080,
    1063730, 1066890, 1085660, 1086940, 1091500, 1097150, 1113560, 1142710, 1144200,
    1145350, 1145360, 1150690, 1151640, 1158310, 1172380, 1172470, 1174180, 1196590,
    1203220, 1222140, 1222670, 1237970, 1238810, 1238840, 1240440, 1245620, 1250410,
    1259420, 1293830, 1325200, 1328670, 1426210, 1446780, 1449850, 1462040, 1517290,
    1551360, 1593500, 1599340, 1623730, 1659040, 1665460, 1716740, 1774580, 1782210,
    1794680, 1817070, 1868140, 1888930, 1938090, 1966720, 2050650, 2208920, 2215430,
    2246340, 2357570, 2379780, 2399830, 2420110, 2440510,
]


def fetch(app_id):
    url = f"https://store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails?appids={app_id}&l=english&cc=us"
    request = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": USER_AGENT})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=30) as response:
        entry = json.load(response)[str(app_id)]
    if not entry.get("success"):
        return None
    data = entry["data"]
    requirements = data.get("pc_requirements")
    if not isinstance(requirements, dict) or not requirements.get("minimum"):
        return None
    return {
        "app_id": app_id,
        "name": data["name"],
        "minimum": requirements.get("minimum"),
        "recommended": requirements.get("recommended"),
    }


def main():
    corpus = []
    for app_id in APP_IDS:
        try:
            game = fetch(app_id)
        except Exception as error:  # keep going; report at the end
            print(f"{app_id}: {error}")
            game = None
        if game:
            corpus.append(game)
            print(f"{app_id}: {game['name']}")
        time.sleep(1.5)
    out = pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name("corpus.json")
    out.write_text(json.dumps(corpus, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    print(f"{len(corpus)} games -> {out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

`packaging/README.md`:

```md
# Packaging

Files that install rigcheck into a Linux desktop. The app ID, `dev.gorkemkaryol.rigcheck`, names all of them: Wayland matches the running window to its `.desktop` file (and so its icon) by this ID, and Flatpak uses it as the app ID.

| File | Installed to |
|---|---|
| `dev.gorkemkaryol.rigcheck.desktop` | `share/applications/` |
| `dev.gorkemkaryol.rigcheck.metainfo.xml` | `share/metainfo/` (AppStream: what software centers show) |
| `assets/brand/icon-{128,256,512}.png` | `share/icons/hicolor/<size>x<size>/apps/dev.gorkemkaryol.rigcheck.png` |

CI validates the first two (`desktop-file-validate`, `appstreamcli validate`).

## Release packages

`.github/workflows/release-app.yml` builds them on every pull request that touches packaging (to catch breakage) and publishes them when a `v*` tag is pushed. The tag must match the version in `Cargo.toml`.

| Package | Built by |
|---|---|
| `rigcheck-<version>-x86_64.AppImage` | `packaging/package.sh` + `appimagetool` |
| `rigcheck-<version>-x86_64-linux.tar.gz` | `packaging/package.sh` |
| `rigcheck_<version>-1_amd64.deb` | `cargo deb` (`[package.metadata.deb]` in `app/Cargo.toml`) |
| `rigcheck-<version>-1.x86_64.rpm` | `cargo generate-rpm` (`[package.metadata.generate-rpm]`) |
| `version.txt` | `packaging/package.sh`; the app's update notice reads it |

Built on Ubuntu 22.04, so the binary runs on any distro with glibc 2.35 or newer. It links only glibc and libgcc; Wayland/X11 and Vulkan are loaded at runtime.

To release: bump `version` in `Cargo.toml` (and the `<releases>` entry in the metainfo), merge, then `git tag v<version> && git push origin v<version>`.

## AUR: `rigcheck-bin`

`aur/PKGBUILD` repackages the release tarball. After a release: bump `pkgver`, run `updpkgsums` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo > .SRCINFO`, then push both files to `ssh://aur@aur.archlinux.org/rigcheck-bin.git` (needs an AUR account with your SSH key).

## Flathub

`flatpak/dev.gorkemkaryol.rigcheck.yml` builds from the release tag, offline. Before submitting, generate the crates it needs:

```sh
# github.com/flatpak/flatpak-builder-tools, cargo/flatpak-cargo-generator.py
python3 flatpak-cargo-generator.py Cargo.lock -o packaging/flatpak/cargo-sources.json
flatpak-builder --user --install --force-clean build-dir packaging/flatpak/dev.gorkemkaryol.rigcheck.yml
```

Then follow Flathub's submission guide (a pull request to `flathub/flathub` with the manifest and `cargo-sources.json`). In the sandbox `vulkaninfo` isn't available, so the Vulkan version and VRAM show as unknown; Steam libraries on other drives need an extra filesystem grant.

```

# Maintainer: Glory42 <https://github.com/Glory42>
#
# rigcheck-bin: the prebuilt binary from a GitHub Release. After a new
# release: bump pkgver, run `updpkgsums` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo > .SRCINFO`.
pkgname=rigcheck-bin
pkgver=0.7.0
pkgrel=1
pkgdesc="Check which Steam games your PC can run on Linux"
arch=('x86_64')
url="https://github.com/Glory42/rigcheck"
license=('MIT')
# The binary links only glibc and libgcc; the windowing and GPU libraries
# are loaded at runtime.
depends=('gcc-libs' 'glibc' 'libxkbcommon')
optdepends=(
  'wayland: Wayland sessions'
  'libxcursor: X11 sessions'
  'libxrandr: X11 sessions'
  'libxi: X11 sessions'
  'vulkan-icd-loader: GPU rendering (falls back to software without it)'
  'vulkan-tools: vulkaninfo, for Vulkan version and VRAM detection'
)
provides=('rigcheck')
conflicts=('rigcheck')
source=("$url/releases/download/v$pkgver/rigcheck-$pkgver-x86_64-linux.tar.gz")
sha256sums=('SKIP')

package() {
  cp -a "rigcheck-$pkgver-x86_64-linux/usr" "$pkgdir/"
}

`packaging/package.sh`:

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Builds the AppImage and the tarball from target/release/rigcheck into dist/.
# The .deb and .rpm come from `cargo deb` and `cargo generate-rpm` (see
# app/Cargo.toml). Usage: packaging/package.sh <version> [path to appimagetool]
set -euo pipefail

version="$1"
appimagetool="${2:-appimagetool}"
id=dev.gorkemkaryol.rigcheck
root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
dist="$root/dist"
rm -rf "$dist" && mkdir -p "$dist"

# The installed layout, shared by the tarball and the AppImage.
stage() {
    local into="$1"
    install -Dm755 "$root/target/release/rigcheck" "$into/usr/bin/rigcheck"
    install -Dm644 "$root/packaging/$id.desktop" "$into/usr/share/applications/$id.desktop"
    install -Dm644 "$root/packaging/$id.metainfo.xml" "$into/usr/share/metainfo/$id.metainfo.xml"
    for size in 128 256 512; do
        install -Dm644 "$root/assets/brand/icon-$size.png" \
            "$into/usr/share/icons/hicolor/${size}x${size}/apps/$id.png"
    done
}

# Tarball, for the AUR package and anyone installing by hand.
tarball="rigcheck-$version-x86_64-linux"
stage "$dist/$tarball"
install -Dm644 "$root/LICENSE" "$dist/$tarball/usr/share/licenses/rigcheck/LICENSE"
tar -C "$dist" -czf "$dist/$tarball.tar.gz" "$tarball"
rm -rf "$dist/$tarball"

# AppImage: the same layout plus what appimagetool wants at the top.
appdir="$dist/rigcheck.AppDir"
stage "$appdir"
cp "$root/packaging/$id.desktop" "$appdir/$id.desktop"
cp "$root/assets/brand/icon-256.png" "$appdir/$id.png"
ln -s usr/bin/rigcheck "$appdir/AppRun"
# No FUSE in containers and CI: let appimagetool unpack itself instead.
APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1 ARCH=x86_64 "$appimagetool" --no-appstream "$appdir" \
    "$dist/rigcheck-$version-x86_64.AppImage"
rm -rf "$appdir"

# What the app's update notice reads (app/src/release.rs).
echo "$version" > "$dist/version.txt"

ls -l "$dist"

```

`pipeline/src/applist.rs`:

```rs
//! Steam's list of every game, from `IStoreService/GetAppList`.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

use crate::Error;

/// A game on Steam, as the app list names it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct App {
    #[serde(rename = "appid")]
    pub app_id: u32,
    pub name: String,
    /// When the store page last changed, as a Unix timestamp.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub last_modified: i64,
}

/// Reads every page. `fetch_page` gets the last app ID seen (0 for the first
/// page) and returns that page's JSON.
pub fn collect(
    mut fetch_page: impl FnMut(u32) -> Result<String, Error>,
) -> Result<Vec<App>, Error> {
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct Page {
        response: Response,
    }
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct Response {
        #[serde(default)]
        apps: Vec<App>,
        #[serde(default)]
        have_more_results: bool,
        #[serde(default)]
        last_appid: u32,
    }

    let mut apps = Vec::new();
    let mut last_appid = 0;
    loop {
        let page: Page = serde_json::from_str(&fetch_page(last_appid)?)?;
        apps.extend(page.response.apps);
        if !page.response.have_more_results {
            return Ok(apps);
        }
        last_appid = page.response.last_appid;
    }
}

```

`pipeline/src/awacy.rs`:

```rs
//! AreWeAntiCheatYet's games.json → anti-cheat status per Steam game.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use rigcheck_core::AntiCheat;
use serde::Deserialize;

use crate::Error;

/// A game's anti-cheat and whether it works on Linux.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct AntiCheatInfo {
    pub status: AntiCheat,
    /// The anti-cheats it uses, e.g. "BattlEye" or "Easy Anti-Cheat".
    pub name: String,
}

/// Status per Steam app ID. Games without a Steam ID are skipped.
pub fn statuses(json: &str) -> Result<HashMap<u32, AntiCheatInfo>, Error> {
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
    struct Game {
        status: String,
        #[serde(default)]
        anticheats: Vec<String>,
        #[serde(default)]
        store_ids: StoreIds,
    }
    #[derive(Deserialize, Default)]
    struct StoreIds {
        steam: Option<String>,
    }

    let games: Vec<Game> = serde_json::from_str(json)?;
    Ok(games
        .into_iter()
        .filter_map(|game| {
            let app_id = game.store_ids.steam?.parse().ok()?;
            let status = match game.status.as_str() {
                "Supported" => AntiCheat::Supported,
                "Running" => AntiCheat::Running,
                "Planned" => AntiCheat::Planned,
                "Broken" => AntiCheat::Broken,
                "Denied" => AntiCheat::Denied,
                _ => return None,
            };
            let name = game.anticheats.join(", ");
            Some((app_id, AntiCheatInfo { status, name }))
        })
        .collect())
}

```

`pipeline/src/blender.rs`:

```rs
//! Filling gaps in the hardware table from Blender Open Data (CC0).
//!
//! Blender's benchmark measures rendering, not games, so hand scores in
//! data/hardware.toml always win. Blender only scores parts the table lacks:
//! each device's median score (sum of samples/minute over the three standard
//! scenes, ≥ 3 runs) is rescaled by the median ratio of our score to
//! Blender's over the 3 same-vendor parts both have whose Blender scores are
//! closest. Nearest anchors beat one ratio per vendor (13% vs 21% median
//! error, leave-one-out over the hand table), because rendering and games
//! scale differently across generations. NVIDIA uses CUDA runs, because
//! OptiX also uses RT cores and overrates RTX cards against GTX ones.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader, Read};

use rigcheck_core::{Catalog, CatalogEntry, Vendor};
use serde::Deserialize;

use crate::Error;

const SCENES: [&str; 3] = ["monster", "junkshop", "classroom"];
const MIN_RUNS: usize = 3;
/// How many nearby parts both scored set a missing part's ratio.
const ANCHORS: usize = 3;

/// Parts the table lacks, with rescaled scores.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct GapScores {
    pub cpus: Vec<CatalogEntry>,
    pub gpus: Vec<CatalogEntry>,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Record {
    schema_version: String,
    data: Vec<Run>,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Run {
    device_info: DeviceInfo,
    scene: Scene,
    stats: Stats,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct DeviceInfo {
    device_type: String,
    compute_devices: Vec<Device>,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Device {
    name: String,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Scene {
    label: String,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
struct Stats {
    samples_per_minute: Option<f64>,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
enum Kind {
    Cpu,
    Gpu,
}

/// Reads a snapshot (one JSON record per line) and scores missing parts.
pub fn gap_scores(snapshot: impl Read, catalog: &Catalog) -> Result<GapScores, Error> {
    let mut runs: HashMap<(Kind, Vendor, String), Vec<f64>> = HashMap::new();
    for line in BufReader::new(snapshot).lines() {
        let Ok(record) = serde_json::from_str::<Record>(&line?) else {
            continue; // other schemas and malformed lines
        };
        if let Some((device, score)) = benchmark(&record) {
            runs.entry(device).or_default().push(score);
        }
    }

    // Median score per device with enough runs.
    let medians: Vec<((Kind, Vendor, String), f64)> = runs
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|(_, scores)| scores.len() >= MIN_RUNS)
        .map(|(device, scores)| (device, median(scores)))
        .collect();

    // Per kind and vendor: our-score / Blender-score over parts both have.
    // (Blender score, our score / Blender score) for parts both have.
    let mut anchors: HashMap<(Kind, Vendor), Vec<(f64, f64)>> = HashMap::new();
    let mut missing = Vec::new();
    for ((kind, vendor, name), score) in medians {
        let matches = match kind {
            Kind::Cpu => catalog.match_cpus(&name),
            Kind::Gpu => catalog.match_gpus(&name),
        };
        match matches.as_slice() {
            [entry] => anchors
                .entry((kind, vendor))
                .or_default()
                .push((score, f64::from(entry.score) / score)),
            [] => missing.push((kind, vendor, name, score)),
            _ => {} // ambiguous name
        }
    }

    let mut gaps = GapScores::default();
    for (kind, vendor, name, score) in missing {
        let Some(known) = anchors.get(&(kind, vendor)).filter(|a| a.len() >= ANCHORS) else {
            continue;
        };
        let mut nearest = known.clone();
        nearest.sort_by(|a, b| (a.0 - score).abs().total_cmp(&(b.0 - score).abs()));
        let ratio = median(nearest.iter().take(ANCHORS).map(|&(_, r)| r).collect());
        let entry = CatalogEntry {
            name,
            vendor,
            score: (score * ratio).round() as u32,
            vram_mb: None,
            aliases: Vec::new(),
            pci: Vec::new(),
        };
        match kind {
            Kind::Cpu => gaps.cpus.push(entry),
            Kind::Gpu => gaps.gpus.push(entry),
        }
    }
    gaps.cpus.sort_by(|a, b| a.name.cmp(&b.name));
    gaps.gpus.sort_by(|a, b| a.name.cmp(&b.name));
    Ok(gaps)
}

/// The device a v4 record benchmarked and its score, if it ran all three
/// scenes on one device through a backend we use.
fn benchmark(record: &Record) -> Option<((Kind, Vendor, String), f64)> {
    if record.schema_version != "v4" {
        return None;
    }
    let first = record.data.first()?;
    let [device] = first.device_info.compute_devices.as_slice() else {
        return None;
    };
    let (kind, vendor) = match first.device_info.device_type.as_str() {
        "CUDA" => (Kind::Gpu, Vendor::Nvidia),
        "HIP" => (Kind::Gpu, Vendor::Amd),
        "ONEAPI" => (Kind::Gpu, Vendor::Intel),
        "CPU" if device.name.contains("AMD") => (Kind::Cpu, Vendor::Amd),
        "CPU" if device.name.contains("Intel") => (Kind::Cpu, Vendor::Intel),
        _ => return None,
    };
    let mut score = 0.0;
    for scene in SCENES {
        let run = record.data.iter().find(|run| run.scene.label == scene)?;
        score += run.stats.samples_per_minute?;
    }
    Some(((kind, vendor, device.name.clone()), score))
}

fn median(mut values: Vec<f64>) -> f64 {
    values.sort_by(f64::total_cmp);
    let mid = values.len() / 2;
    if values.len().is_multiple_of(2) {
        (values[mid - 1] + values[mid]) / 2.0
    } else {
        values[mid]
    }
}

```rs
//! `build`: merging the data sources into the crawled games.db.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use rigcheck_gamedb::GameDb;

use rigcheck_core::Catalog;

use crate::Error;
use crate::applist::App;
use crate::awacy::AntiCheatInfo;
use crate::blender::GapScores;
use crate::pci::PciId;
use crate::protondb::Summary;

/// Everything `build` merges into the crawled games.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct Sources {
    /// Every game on Steam, for name search.
    pub apps: Vec<App>,
    pub protondb: HashMap<u32, Summary>,
    pub anticheat: HashMap<u32, AntiCheatInfo>,
    /// Parts missing from data/hardware.toml, scored from Blender Open Data.
    pub gaps: GapScores,
    pub pci_ids: Vec<PciId>,
}

/// ROADMAP §1.2: ProtonDB's data is ODbL (share-alike), so games.db is too.
const LICENSE: &str = "This database is made available under the Open Database License \
(ODbL 1.0): https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1-0/. Its contents are under the \
Database Contents License: https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/dbcl/1-0/.";

/// Credits for every data source (ROADMAP §9).
const SOURCES: &str = "Steam store data: Valve Corporation (store.steampowered.com). \
ProtonDB reports: ProtonDB (protondb.com), ODbL, via github.com/bdefore/protondb-data; \
tiers computed by rigcheck's own rule. \
Anti-cheat status: AreWeAntiCheatYet (areweanticheatyet.com), MIT, © AreWeAntiCheatYet contributors. \
Steam Deck compatibility: Valve Corporation's Deck compatibility reports. \
Hardware scores: rigcheck's table (github.com/Glory42/rigcheck), gaps from Blender Open Data \
(opendata.blender.org), CC0. GPU PCI IDs: pci.ids (pci-ids.ucw.cz), BSD-3-Clause or GPL-2.0.";

/// Adds missing hardware and GPU PCI IDs and re-matches every game against
/// the grown table; adds every app-list game not crawled yet (by name),
/// ProtonDB tiers and popularity and anti-cheat status; rebuilds the name
/// search; and writes the license and source credits.
pub fn build(db: &GameDb, sources: &Sources) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let Sources {
        apps,
        protondb,
        anticheat,
        gaps,
        pci_ids,
    } = sources;
    db.store_extra_hardware(
        &Catalog::new(gaps.cpus.clone(), gaps.gpus.clone()),
        "blender",
    )?;
    let pci_rows: Vec<(u16, u16, &str)> = pci_ids
        .iter()
        .map(|id| (id.vendor_id, id.device_id, id.name.as_str()))
        .collect();
    db.add_pci_ids(&pci_rows)?;
    db.rematch()?;
    let names: Vec<(u32, &str)> = apps
        .iter()
        .map(|app| (app.app_id, app.name.as_str()))
        .collect();
    db.store_names(&names)?;
    let proton: Vec<_> = protondb
        .iter()
        .map(|(&app_id, summary)| (app_id, summary.tier, summary.reports))
        .collect();
    db.set_protondb(&proton)?;
    let anticheat: Vec<_> = anticheat
        .iter()
        .map(|(&app_id, info)| (app_id, info.status, info.name.clone()))
        .collect();
    db.set_anticheat(&anticheat)?;
    db.rebuild_search()?;
    db.set_meta("license", LICENSE)?;
    db.set_meta("sources", SOURCES)?;
    Ok(())
}

`pipeline/src/crawl.rs`:

```rs
//! Deciding which apps to fetch next (ROADMAP Phase 4, §9).

use std::cmp::Reverse;
use std::collections::HashMap;

use rigcheck_gamedb::GameDb;

use crate::Error;
use crate::applist::App;

/// The next apps to fetch, at most `budget`: those never fetched, whose
/// store page changed since, or stored without their requirement text,
/// popular ones first (by ProtonDB report count),
/// then the most recently changed.
pub fn plan(
    apps: &[App],
    db: &GameDb,
    popularity: &HashMap<u32, u32>,
    budget: usize,
) -> Result<Vec<u32>, Error> {
    let fetched = db.fetched()?;
    let without_text = db.without_requirement_text()?;
    let mut candidates: Vec<&App> = apps
        .iter()
        .filter(|app| {
            without_text.contains(&app.app_id)
                || fetched
                    .get(&app.app_id)
                    .is_none_or(|&at| app.last_modified > at)
        })
        .collect();
    candidates.sort_by_key(|app| {
        let reports = popularity.get(&app.app_id).copied().unwrap_or(0);
        (Reverse(reports), Reverse(app.last_modified))
    });
    Ok(candidates
        .into_iter()
        .take(budget)
        .map(|app| app.app_id)
        .collect())
}

//! Steam Deck compatibility from the store's (unofficial) Deck report.

use serde::Deserialize;

use crate::Error;

/// verified | playable | unsupported | unknown, from a response of
/// `saleaction/ajaxgetdeckappcompatibilityreport`.
pub fn status(json: &str) -> Result<&'static str, Error> {
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct Response {
        results: Option<Results>,
    }
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct Results {
        resolved_category: u8,
    }

    let response: Response = serde_json::from_str(json)?;
    Ok(match response.results.map(|r| r.resolved_category) {
        Some(3) => "verified",
        Some(2) => "playable",
        Some(1) => "unsupported",
        _ => "unknown",
    })
}

`pipeline/src/main.rs`:

```rs
//! rigcheck-pipeline: builds games.db from Steam and its data sources
//! (ROADMAP Phase 4). The logic lives in the library; this is the command line.
//!
//!   rigcheck-pipeline applist <apps.json>
//!       Every game on Steam, from GetAppList. Needs $STEAM_API_KEY.
//!   rigcheck-pipeline crawl <apps.json> <games.db> <budget> [reports.json]
//!       Fetches up to <budget> store pages into games.db (created if
//!       missing): changed or never-fetched ones, most ProtonDB reports first
//!       when ProtonDB's reports_piiremoved.json is given. Run again to continue.
//!   rigcheck-pipeline build <games.db> <apps.json> <reports.json> <awacy-games.json> <pci.ids> <blender.jsonl>
//!       Adds parts missing from the hardware table (Blender Open Data), GPU
//!       PCI IDs, uncrawled games by name, ProtonDB tiers and anti-cheat
//!       status; re-matches hardware; rebuilds name search.
//!   rigcheck-pipeline publish <games.db> <out-dir> <db_version> <built_at> <url> <min_app_version>
//!       Writes <out-dir>/games.db.zst and manifest.json (ROADMAP §7.3).
//!   rigcheck-pipeline validate <games.db>
//!       Fails (exit 1) if games.db shouldn't be published.
//!   rigcheck-pipeline report <games.db>
//!       Hardware names data/hardware.toml doesn't know, most used first.

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::BufReader;
use std::path::Path;
use std::time::{Duration, SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

use rigcheck_core::Catalog;
use rigcheck_gamedb::GameDb;
use rigcheck_gamedb::ingest::{Ingested, ingest};
use rigcheck_net::{Allowlist, Client, RateLimiter, Retry};
use rigcheck_pipeline::Error;
use rigcheck_pipeline::applist::{self, App};
use rigcheck_pipeline::crawl::plan;
use rigcheck_pipeline::validate::{Rules, validate};
use rigcheck_pipeline::{awacy, blender, build, deck, pci, protondb, publish, report};

const HARDWARE: &str = include_str!("../../data/hardware.toml");

fn main() -> Result<(), Error> {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
    let args: Vec<&str> = args.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();
    match args.as_slice() {
        ["applist", out] => fetch_applist(Path::new(out)),
        ["crawl", apps, db, budget] => crawl(Path::new(apps), Path::new(db), budget.parse()?, None),
        ["crawl", apps, db, budget, reports] => crawl(
            Path::new(apps),
            Path::new(db),
            budget.parse()?,
            Some(Path::new(reports)),
        ),
        ["build", db, apps, reports, awacy, pci_ids, blender] => build_db(
            Path::new(db),
            Inputs {
                apps: Path::new(apps),
                reports: Path::new(reports),
                awacy: Path::new(awacy),
                pci_ids: Path::new(pci_ids),
                blender: Path::new(blender),
            },
        ),
        [
            "publish",
            db,
            out,
            db_version,
            built_at,
            url,
            min_app_version,
        ] => {
            let release = publish::Release {
                db_version: db_version.to_string(),
                built_at: built_at.to_string(),
                url: url.to_string(),
                min_app_version: min_app_version.to_string(),
            };
            let manifest = publish::package(Path::new(db), Path::new(out), &release)?;
            println!("{} bytes, sha256 {}", manifest.size_bytes, manifest.sha256);
            Ok(())
        }
        ["validate", db] => validate_db(Path::new(db)),
        ["report", db] => report_db(Path::new(db)),
        _ => Err("usage: see the comment at the top of pipeline/src/main.rs".into()),
    }
}

/// Steam documents ~200 store requests per 5 minutes; stay below it.
fn client() -> Result<Client, Error> {
    Client::new(
        Allowlist::pipeline(),
        RateLimiter::new(150, Duration::from_secs(300)),
        Retry::new(4, Duration::from_secs(30)),
    )
}

fn fetch_applist(out: &Path) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let key = std::env::var("STEAM_API_KEY").map_err(|_| "set STEAM_API_KEY")?;
    let mut client = client()?;
    let apps = applist::collect(|last_appid| {
        let url = format!(
            "https://api.steampowered.com/IStoreService/GetAppList/v1/?key={key}\
             &include_games=true&include_dlc=false&include_software=false\
             &include_videos=false&include_hardware=false&max_results=50000&last_appid={last_appid}"
        );
        client.get_text(&url)
    })?;
    std::fs::write(out, serde_json::to_string(&apps)?)?;
    println!("{} games → {}", apps.len(), out.display());
    Ok(())
}

fn now() -> Result<i64, Error> {
    Ok(SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH)?.as_secs() as i64)
}

/// ProtonDB tiers and report counts for every game it has reports for.
fn protondb_summaries(reports: &Path) -> Result<HashMap<u32, protondb::Summary>, Error> {
    let reports = protondb::read_reports(BufReader::new(File::open(reports)?))?;
    Ok(protondb::summarize(&reports, now()?))
}

/// The data files `build` reads.
struct Inputs<'a> {
    apps: &'a Path,
    reports: &'a Path,
    awacy: &'a Path,
    pci_ids: &'a Path,
    blender: &'a Path,
}

fn build_db(db: &Path, inputs: Inputs) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let db = GameDb::open(db)?;
    let table = db.catalog()?;
    let gaps = blender::gap_scores(BufReader::new(File::open(inputs.blender)?), &table)?;
    // PCI IDs are looked up in the table as it will be, Blender parts included.
    let grown = Catalog::new(
        table.cpus().iter().chain(&gaps.cpus).cloned().collect(),
        table.gpus().iter().chain(&gaps.gpus).cloned().collect(),
    );
    let sources = build::Sources {
        apps: serde_json::from_str(&std::fs::read_to_string(inputs.apps)?)?,
        protondb: protondb_summaries(inputs.reports)?,
        anticheat: awacy::statuses(&std::fs::read_to_string(inputs.awacy)?)?,
        pci_ids: pci::ids(&grown, &std::fs::read_to_string(inputs.pci_ids)?),
        gaps,
    };
    build::build(&db, &sources)?;
    println!(
        "built: {} apps, ProtonDB facts for {}, anti-cheat for {}, {} PCI IDs, \
         Blender scores for {} CPUs and {} GPUs",
        sources.apps.len(),
        sources.protondb.len(),
        sources.anticheat.len(),
        sources.pci_ids.len(),
        sources.gaps.cpus.len(),
        sources.gaps.gpus.len()
    );
    Ok(())
}

fn validate_db(path: &Path) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let rules = Rules {
        top: 100,
        min_parsed_share: 0.9,
        max_bytes: 200 * 1024 * 1024, // uncompressed; ROADMAP §7.4 caps the .zst at 50 MB
    };
    let problems = validate(&GameDb::open(path)?, path, &rules)?;
    for problem in &problems {
        eprintln!("problem: {problem:?}");
    }
    if problems.is_empty() {
        println!("valid");
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(format!("{} problem(s); not publishable", problems.len()).into())
    }
}

fn report_db(path: &Path) -> Result<(), Error> {
    use std::io::Write;
    let db = GameDb::open(path)?;
    let mut out = std::io::stdout().lock();
    for line in report::unmatched(&db, &db.catalog()?)?.iter().take(100) {
        match writeln!(out, "{}\t{}\t{}", line.games, line.kind, line.text) {
            // `report | head` closes the pipe early; that's not an error.
            Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::BrokenPipe => return Ok(()),
            result => result?,
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn crawl(apps: &Path, db_path: &Path, budget: usize, reports: Option<&Path>) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let apps: Vec<App> = serde_json::from_str(&std::fs::read_to_string(apps)?)?;
    let db = if db_path.exists() {
        GameDb::open(db_path)?
    } else {
        let db = GameDb::create(db_path)?;
        db.store_catalog(&Catalog::from_toml(HARDWARE)?)?;
        db
    };
    let catalog = db.catalog()?;
    let popularity: HashMap<u32, u32> = match reports {
        Some(reports) => protondb_summaries(reports)?
            .into_iter()
            .map(|(app_id, summary)| (app_id, summary.reports))
            .collect(),
        None => HashMap::new(),
    };
    let batch = plan(&apps, &db, &popularity, budget)?;
    let mut client = client()?;
    let (mut games, mut other) = (0, 0);
    for app_id in &batch {
        let url = format!(
            "https://store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails?appids={app_id}&l=english&cc=us"
        );
        let fetched_at = now()?;
        match client
            .get_text(&url)
            .and_then(|json| ingest(*app_id, &json))
        {
            Ok(Ingested::Game(mut record)) => {
                record.updated_at = fetched_at;
                // A failed Deck lookup only leaves the status empty.
                let deck_url = format!(
                    "https://store.steampowered.com/saleaction/ajaxgetdeckappcompatibilityreport?nAppID={app_id}&l=english"
                );
                record.deck = client
                    .get_text(&deck_url)
                    .and_then(|json| deck::status(&json))
                    .ok()
                    .map(str::to_owned);
                db.store(&record, &catalog)?;
                games += 1;
            }
            Ok(Ingested::NotAGame { .. } | Ingested::Unavailable) => other += 1,
            Err(error) => {
                // Not recorded, so the next run tries again.
                eprintln!("{app_id}: {error}");
                continue;
            }
        }
        db.record_fetch(*app_id, fetched_at)?;
    }
    println!(
        "fetched {} of {} planned: {games} games, {other} other",
        games + other,
        batch.len()
    );
    Ok(())
}

`pipeline/src/pci.rs`:

```rs
//! PCI IDs for the hardware table's GPUs, from pci.ids (the PCI ID
//! Repository), so detected GPUs can be identified exactly.

use rigcheck_core::Catalog;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PciId {
    pub vendor_id: u16,
    pub device_id: u16,
    /// The hardware table entry it belongs to.
    pub name: String,
}

/// Every pci.ids device whose bracketed name matches exactly one table GPU.
/// IDs shared by several table entries ("Radeon RX 470/480/570/580") are
/// skipped rather than guessed.
pub fn ids(catalog: &Catalog, pci_ids: &str) -> Vec<PciId> {
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    let mut vendor_id = None;
    for line in pci_ids.lines() {
        if line.starts_with('#') || line.trim().is_empty() || line.starts_with("\t\t") {
            continue; // comments and subsystem lines
        }
        let Some(device) = line.strip_prefix('\t') else {
            vendor_id = u16::from_str_radix(&line[..4.min(line.len())], 16).ok();
            continue;
        };
        let (Some(vendor_id), Some((id, name))) = (vendor_id, device.split_once("  ")) else {
            continue;
        };
        let Some(bracketed) = name
            .split_once('[')
            .and_then(|(_, rest)| rest.strip_suffix(']'))
        else {
            continue;
        };
        if let ([entry], Ok(device_id)) = (
            catalog.match_gpus(bracketed).as_slice(),
            u16::from_str_radix(id, 16),
        ) {
            found.push(PciId {
                vendor_id,
                device_id,
                name: entry.name.clone(),
            });
        }
    }
    found
}

```

`pipeline/src/protondb.rs`:

```rs
//! ProtonDB's raw reports (ODbL dump) → a tier and a report count per game.
//! ProtonDB's own tier formula isn't published, so this rule is ours
//! (ROADMAP §9) and the app labels it "ProtonDB reports".

use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::io::Read;

use rigcheck_core::ProtonTier;
use serde::Deserialize;

use crate::Error;

/// One report, with only the fields the rule reads.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct Report {
    app: ReportApp,
    pub timestamp: i64,
    responses: Responses,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
struct ReportApp {
    steam: SteamApp,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
struct SteamApp {
    #[serde(rename = "appId")]
    app_id: AppId,
}

/// Most reports write the ID as a string, some as a number.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
#[serde(untagged)]
enum AppId {
    Text(String),
    Number(u32),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", default)]
struct Responses {
    verdict: Option<String>,
    verdict_oob: Option<String>,
    variant: Option<String>,
    custom_proton_version: Option<String>,
    launch_options: Option<String>,
    audio_faults: Option<String>,
    graphical_faults: Option<String>,
    input_faults: Option<String>,
    performance_faults: Option<String>,
    save_game_faults: Option<String>,
    stability_faults: Option<String>,
    windowing_faults: Option<String>,
    significant_bugs: Option<String>,
}

impl Report {
    pub fn app_id(&self) -> Option<u32> {
        match &self.app.steam.app_id {
            AppId::Text(text) => text.parse().ok(),
            AppId::Number(number) => Some(*number),
        }
    }
}

/// What ProtonDB's reports say about a game.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Summary {
    /// `None` if no report is about running it through Proton.
    pub tier: Option<ProtonTier>,
    /// Every report, native ones included: how much Linux players care.
    pub reports: u32,
}

/// Reads the dump's `reports_piiremoved.json` (a JSON array).
pub fn read_reports(reader: impl Read) -> Result<Vec<Report>, Error> {
    Ok(serde_json::from_reader(reader)?)
}

const YEAR: i64 = 365 * 24 * 60 * 60;

/// A tier and report count for every game with reports, as of `now`.
pub fn summarize(reports: &[Report], now: i64) -> HashMap<u32, Summary> {
    let mut by_app: HashMap<u32, Vec<&Report>> = HashMap::new();
    for report in reports {
        if let Some(app_id) = report.app_id() {
            by_app.entry(app_id).or_default().push(report);
        }
    }
    by_app
        .into_iter()
        .map(|(app_id, reports)| {
            let proton: Vec<&Report> = reports
                .iter()
                .copied()
                .filter(|r| r.responses.variant.as_deref() != Some("native"))
                .collect();
            let recent: Vec<&Report> = proton
                .iter()
                .copied()
                .filter(|r| r.timestamp >= now - YEAR)
                .collect();
            let counted = if recent.len() >= 3 { recent } else { proton };
            let summary = Summary {
                tier: most_common(counted.iter().map(|r| rate(&r.responses))),
                reports: reports.len() as u32,
            };
            (app_id, summary)
        })
        .collect()
}

/// The most common tier; ties go to the worse one.
fn most_common(tiers: impl Iterator<Item = ProtonTier>) -> Option<ProtonTier> {
    let mut counts: HashMap<ProtonTier, usize> = HashMap::new();
    for tier in tiers {
        *counts.entry(tier).or_default() += 1;
    }
    counts
        .into_iter()
        .max_by_key(|&(tier, count)| (count, rank(tier)))
        .map(|(tier, _)| tier)
}

/// Higher is worse, so ties pick the worse tier.
fn rank(tier: ProtonTier) -> u8 {
    match tier {
        ProtonTier::Platinum => 0,
        ProtonTier::Gold => 1,
        ProtonTier::Silver => 2,
        ProtonTier::Bronze => 3,
        ProtonTier::Borked => 4,
    }
}

/// One report's rating (ROADMAP §9).
fn rate(r: &Responses) -> ProtonTier {
    let yes = |answer: &Option<String>| answer.as_deref() == Some("yes");
    if r.verdict.as_deref() == Some("no") {
        return ProtonTier::Borked;
    }
    if yes(&r.stability_faults) || yes(&r.significant_bugs) {
        return ProtonTier::Bronze;
    }
    let faults = [
        &r.audio_faults,
        &r.graphical_faults,
        &r.input_faults,
        &r.performance_faults,
        &r.save_game_faults,
        &r.windowing_faults,
    ];
    if faults.into_iter().any(yes) {
        return ProtonTier::Silver;
    }
    let tweaked = r.verdict_oob.as_deref() == Some("no")
        || r.custom_proton_version
            .as_deref()
            .is_some_and(|v| !v.is_empty())
        || r.launch_options
            .as_deref()
            .is_some_and(|o| !o.trim().is_empty())
        || matches!(r.variant.as_deref(), Some("ge" | "notListed"));
    if tweaked {
        ProtonTier::Gold
    } else {
        ProtonTier::Platinum
    }
}

`pipeline/src/publish.rs`:

```rs
//! Packaging games.db for download: `games.db.zst` and `manifest.json`
//! (ROADMAP §7.3). The app checks the manifest, downloads the file, verifies
//! its SHA-256 and swaps it in.

use std::fs::{self, File};
use std::io::BufReader;
use std::path::Path;

use rigcheck_gamedb::{GameDb, Manifest};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

use crate::Error;

/// What this build is, from the workflow.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Release {
    /// e.g. "2026-11-01.1": date and run number.
    pub db_version: String,
    /// RFC 3339, e.g. "2026-11-01T04:00:00Z".
    pub built_at: String,
    /// Where `games.db.zst` will be downloaded from.
    pub url: String,
    /// The oldest app version that can read this schema.
    pub min_app_version: String,
}

/// Compresses `db` into `out/games.db.zst` and writes `out/manifest.json`.
pub fn package(db: &Path, out: &Path, release: &Release) -> Result<Manifest, Error> {
    let schema_version = GameDb::open(db)?
        .meta("schema_version")?
        .ok_or("games.db has no schema_version")?
        .parse()?;
    fs::create_dir_all(out)?;
    let zst = out.join("games.db.zst");
    // Level 19: a smaller download is worth a slower build.
    zstd::stream::copy_encode(BufReader::new(File::open(db)?), File::create(&zst)?, 19)?;
    let bytes = fs::read(&zst)?;
    let sha256 = Sha256::digest(&bytes)
        .iter()
        .map(|byte| format!("{byte:02x}"))
        .collect();
    let manifest = Manifest {
        schema_version,
        db_version: release.db_version.clone(),
        built_at: release.built_at.clone(),
        url: release.url.clone(),
        sha256,
        size_bytes: bytes.len() as u64,
        min_app_version: release.min_app_version.clone(),
    };
    fs::write(
        out.join("manifest.json"),
        serde_json::to_string_pretty(&manifest)? + "\n",
    )?;
    Ok(manifest)
}

`pipeline/src/report.rs`:

```rs
//! `report`: CPU and GPU names the hardware table doesn't know, by how many
//! games mention them, so data/hardware.toml can grow where it matters.

use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};

use rigcheck_core::Catalog;
use rigcheck_gamedb::GameDb;

use crate::Error;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Unmatched {
    /// "cpu" or "gpu".
    pub kind: &'static str,
    /// As a requirement wrote it, e.g. "Qualcomm Adreno X1".
    pub text: String,
    /// How many games mention it.
    pub games: usize,
}

/// Unknown names, most mentioned first.
pub fn unmatched(db: &GameDb, catalog: &Catalog) -> Result<Vec<Unmatched>, Error> {
    // Each (kind, name) once per game, however many tiers mention it.
    let mut seen: HashSet<(u32, &'static str, String)> = HashSet::new();
    for tier in db.requirement_text()? {
        let cpus = tier
            .cpu
            .map(|text| catalog.unmatched_cpus(&text))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        let gpus = tier
            .gpu
            .map(|text| catalog.unmatched_gpus(&text))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        for name in cpus {
            seen.insert((tier.app_id, "cpu", name));
        }
        for name in gpus {
            seen.insert((tier.app_id, "gpu", name));
        }
    }
    let mut counts: HashMap<(&'static str, String), usize> = HashMap::new();
    for (_, kind, name) in seen {
        *counts.entry((kind, name)).or_default() += 1;
    }
    let mut report: Vec<Unmatched> = counts
        .into_iter()
        .map(|((kind, text), games)| Unmatched { kind, text, games })
        .collect();
    report.sort_by(|a, b| b.games.cmp(&a.games).then_with(|| a.text.cmp(&b.text)));
    Ok(report)
}

`pipeline/src/validate.rs`:

```rs
//! `validate`: checks a built games.db before it's published.

use std::path::Path;

use rigcheck_gamedb::GameDb;

use crate::Error;

/// What a publishable games.db must meet.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct Rules {
    /// How many of the most popular games to check.
    pub top: usize,
    /// The share of those that must have CPU, GPU and RAM parsed. Below 1.0
    /// because some popular games leave a field out on Steam (TF2 lists no GPU).
    pub min_parsed_share: f64,
    /// Size limit for the file (ROADMAP §7.4).
    pub max_bytes: u64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Problem {
    NoGames,
    TooFewParsed { parsed: usize, top: usize },
    TooBig { bytes: u64, max: u64 },
}

/// Everything wrong with the games.db at `path`; empty if it can be published.
pub fn validate(db: &GameDb, path: &Path, rules: &Rules) -> Result<Vec<Problem>, Error> {
    let mut problems = Vec::new();
    let top = db.most_popular(rules.top)?;
    if top.is_empty() {
        return Ok(vec![Problem::NoGames]);
    }
    let parsed = top.iter().filter(|(_, status)| status == "parsed").count();
    if (parsed as f64) < rules.min_parsed_share * top.len() as f64 {
        problems.push(Problem::TooFewParsed {
            parsed,
            top: top.len(),
        });
    }
    let bytes = std::fs::metadata(path)?.len();
    if bytes > rules.max_bytes {
        problems.push(Problem::TooBig {
            bytes,
            max: rules.max_bytes,
        });
    }
    Ok(problems)
}

`pipeline/tests/blender.rs`:

```rs
//! Tests for filling gaps in the hardware table from Blender Open Data.
//!
//! Hand scores in data/hardware.toml win. Blender only scores parts the
//! table lacks, rescaled by the median our-score/Blender-score ratio of the 3
//! same-vendor parts both have whose Blender scores are closest. NVIDIA uses
//! CUDA runs (OptiX overweights RT cores).

use std::fs::File;
use std::io::BufReader;

use rigcheck_core::{Catalog, Vendor};
use rigcheck_pipeline::blender::gap_scores;

#[test]
fn a_gpu_missing_from_the_table_gets_a_rescaled_score() {
    let catalog = Catalog::from_toml(include_str!("../../data/hardware.toml")).unwrap();
    let path = concat!(
        env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
        "/../data/fixtures/blender.jsonl"
    );

    let gaps = gap_scores(BufReader::new(File::open(path).unwrap()), &catalog).unwrap();

    // Medians of 3 CUDA runs: GTX 1650 512.2311, RTX 2060 1137.3496,
    // RTX 3060 1350.2494, RTX 3070 2055.1828. Closest to the RTX 3050's
    // 823.8554: GTX 1650, RTX 2060, RTX 3060, with our/Blender ratios 0.1367,
    // 0.1231, 0.1296 → median 0.1296 → 823.8554 × 175/1350.2494 = 106.8 → 107.
    let [gpu] = gaps.gpus.as_slice() else {
        panic!("expected only the RTX 3050, got {:?}", gaps.gpus);
    };
    assert_eq!(gpu.name, "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050");
    assert_eq!(gpu.vendor, Vendor::Nvidia);
    assert_eq!(gpu.score, 107);
    assert!(gaps.cpus.is_empty());
}

`pipeline/tests/crawl.rs`:

```rs
//! Tests for crawl planning: which apps to fetch next.
//!
//! ROADMAP Phase 4: popular games first, then new releases, then the rest;
//! resumable across runs. §9: never re-crawl a game whose store page hasn't
//! changed.

use std::collections::HashMap;

use rigcheck_core::{Catalog, ParsedTier};
use rigcheck_gamedb::{GameDb, GameRecord};
use rigcheck_pipeline::applist::App;
use rigcheck_pipeline::crawl::plan;
use tempfile::TempDir;

/// An app-list entry whose store page last changed at `last_modified`.
fn app(app_id: u32, last_modified: i64) -> App {
    App {
        app_id,
        name: format!("Game {app_id}"),
        last_modified,
    }
}

#[test]
fn popular_games_come_first_then_the_newest() {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let db = GameDb::create(&dir.path().join("games.db")).unwrap();
    let apps = [
        app(1, 100),
        app(2, 500),
        app(3, 300),
        app(4, 200),
        app(5, 400),
    ];
    // ProtonDB report counts.
    let popularity = HashMap::from([(4, 900), (1, 50)]);

    let next = plan(&apps, &db, &popularity, 4).unwrap();

    assert_eq!(next, [4, 1, 2, 5]);
}

#[test]
fn a_store_page_is_fetched_again_only_after_it_changes() {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let db = GameDb::create(&dir.path().join("games.db")).unwrap();
    let apps = [
        app(1, 100),
        app(2, 500),
        app(3, 300),
        app(4, 200),
        app(5, 400),
    ];
    db.record_fetch(2, 600).unwrap(); // fetched after its last change: skip
    db.record_fetch(3, 250).unwrap(); // changed at 300, after the fetch: again

    let next = plan(&apps, &db, &HashMap::new(), 10).unwrap();

    assert_eq!(next, [5, 3, 4, 1]);
}

#[test]
fn each_run_continues_where_the_last_one_stopped() {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let db = GameDb::create(&dir.path().join("games.db")).unwrap();
    let apps = [
        app(1, 100),
        app(2, 500),
        app(3, 300),
        app(4, 200),
        app(5, 400),
    ];
    let popularity = HashMap::from([(4, 900), (1, 50)]);

    let mut runs = Vec::new();
    for run_at in [1000, 2000, 3000, 4000] {
        let batch = plan(&apps, &db, &popularity, 2).unwrap();
        for &app_id in &batch {
            db.record_fetch(app_id, run_at).unwrap();
        }
        runs.push(batch);
    }

    assert_eq!(runs, [vec![4, 1], vec![2, 5], vec![3], vec![]]);
}

#[test]
fn a_game_stored_without_its_requirement_text_is_fetched_again() {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let db = GameDb::create(&dir.path().join("games.db")).unwrap();
    let tier = || {
        Some(ParsedTier {
            ram_mb: Some(2048),
            ..ParsedTier::default()
        })
    };
    // Crawled before the text was kept.
    let old = GameRecord {
        app_id: 1,
        name: "Old".to_owned(),
        minimum: tier(),
        ..GameRecord::default()
    };
    let new = GameRecord {
        app_id: 2,
        name: "New".to_owned(),
        minimum: tier(),
        minimum_text: Some("Memory: 2 GB RAM".to_owned()),
        ..GameRecord::default()
    };
    for record in [&old, &new] {
        db.store(record, &Catalog::default()).unwrap();
        db.record_fetch(record.app_id, 600).unwrap(); // after the last change
    }

    let next = plan(&[app(1, 100), app(2, 100)], &db, &HashMap::new(), 10).unwrap();

    assert_eq!(next, [1]);
}

`pipeline/tests/protondb.rs`:

```rs
//! Tests for turning ProtonDB's raw reports into a tier per game (ROADMAP §9).
//!
//! Per report: Borked if the verdict is "no"; Bronze with stability faults or
//! significant bugs; Silver with other faults; Gold if it needed tweaks (not
//! working out of the box, custom or GE Proton, launch options); else Platinum.
//! Per game: the most common rating in the last 12 months (all reports if
//! fewer than 3 are that recent), ties going to the worse tier. Reports on
//! native Linux builds don't count toward the tier.

use std::fs::File;
use std::io::BufReader;

use rigcheck_core::ProtonTier;
use rigcheck_pipeline::protondb::{Report, read_reports, summarize};

/// 2026-10-01, the dump's date.
const NOW: i64 = 1_790_812_800;

fn reports() -> Vec<Report> {
    let path = concat!(
        env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
        "/../data/fixtures/protondb/reports.json"
    );
    read_reports(BufReader::new(File::open(path).unwrap())).unwrap()
}

#[test]
fn a_game_gets_its_most_common_recent_rating() {
    // Lara Croft GO, last 12 months: Borked, Silver, Borked, Gold, Platinum.
    let summaries = summarize(&reports(), NOW);

    assert_eq!(summaries[&540840].tier, Some(ProtonTier::Borked));
}

#[test]
fn ties_go_to_the_worse_tier() {
    // Bye Sweet Carole: Platinum, Gold, Platinum, Gold.
    assert_eq!(
        summarize(&reports(), NOW)[&2428980].tier,
        Some(ProtonTier::Gold)
    );
}

#[test]
fn with_fewer_than_3_recent_reports_older_ones_count_too() {
    // Chompy Chomp Chomp: recent Gold and Platinum would tie (→ Gold); with
    // the 2019 Platinum report it's Platinum 2 to 1.
    assert_eq!(
        summarize(&reports(), NOW)[&292570].tier,
        Some(ProtonTier::Platinum)
    );
}

#[test]
fn native_reports_count_for_popularity_but_not_the_tier() {
    let summaries = summarize(&reports(), NOW);

    assert_eq!(summaries[&3493540].tier, None);
    assert_eq!(summaries[&3493540].reports, 1);
    assert_eq!(summaries[&540840].reports, 7);
}

#[test]
fn each_report_is_rated_by_the_rule() {
    let all = reports();
    let cases = [
        // Lara Croft GO
        (1762124894, ProtonTier::Borked),   // verdict "no"
        (1766589519, ProtonTier::Silver),   // input faults
        (1779432570, ProtonTier::Gold),     // an unlisted Proton build
        (1782658133, ProtonTier::Platinum), // official Proton, no faults
        // Act of War: High Treason
        (1753653100, ProtonTier::Bronze), // stability faults
        (1669894058, ProtonTier::Gold),   // GE-Proton
    ];
    for (timestamp, tier) in cases {
        let one: Vec<Report> = all
            .iter()
            .filter(|r| r.timestamp == timestamp)
            .cloned()
            .collect();
        let summary = summarize(&one, NOW).into_values().next().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(summary.tier, Some(tier), "report at {timestamp}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn reports_with_a_numeric_app_id_count_too() {
    // About 8% of the dump writes "appId": 427510 instead of "427510".
    let summaries = summarize(&reports(), NOW);

    assert_eq!(summaries[&427510].reports, 1);
}

`pipeline/tests/publish.rs`:

```rs
//! Tests for packaging games.db for download: zstd compression and
//! manifest.json (ROADMAP §7.3).

use std::process::Command;

use rigcheck_gamedb::GameDb;
use rigcheck_pipeline::publish::{Release, package};
use tempfile::TempDir;

fn release() -> Release {
    Release {
        db_version: "2026-11-01.1".to_owned(),
        built_at: "2026-11-01T04:00:00Z".to_owned(),
        url: "https://github.com/Glory42/rigcheck/releases/download/db-latest/games.db.zst"
            .to_owned(),
        min_app_version: "0.4.0".to_owned(),
    }
}

#[test]
fn the_download_decompresses_to_the_same_database() {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let db_path = dir.path().join("games.db");
    drop(GameDb::create(&db_path).unwrap());
    let out = dir.path().join("out");

    package(&db_path, &out, &release()).unwrap();

    let compressed = std::fs::read(out.join("games.db.zst")).unwrap();
    let restored = zstd::decode_all(compressed.as_slice()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(restored, std::fs::read(&db_path).unwrap());
}

#[test]
fn the_manifest_describes_the_download_exactly() {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let db_path = dir.path().join("games.db");
    drop(GameDb::create(&db_path).unwrap());
    let out = dir.path().join("out");

    let manifest = package(&db_path, &out, &release()).unwrap();

    let zst = out.join("games.db.zst");
    let sha256sum = Command::new("sha256sum").arg(&zst).output().unwrap();
    let expected = String::from_utf8(sha256sum.stdout).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(manifest.sha256, expected.split_whitespace().next().unwrap());
    assert_eq!(manifest.size_bytes, std::fs::metadata(&zst).unwrap().len());
    assert_eq!(manifest.schema_version, 1);
    assert_eq!(manifest.db_version, "2026-11-01.1");
    let written: serde_json::Value =
        serde_json::from_str(&std::fs::read_to_string(out.join("manifest.json")).unwrap()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(written["sha256"], manifest.sha256.as_str());
}

`pipeline/tests/report.rs`:

```rs
//! Tests for the unmatched-hardware report: CPU/GPU names the hardware table
//! doesn't know, by how many games mention them, to grow data/hardware.toml.

use rigcheck_core::{Catalog, ParsedTier};
use rigcheck_gamedb::{GameDb, GameRecord};
use rigcheck_pipeline::report::{Unmatched, unmatched};
use tempfile::TempDir;

fn catalog() -> Catalog {
    Catalog::from_toml(include_str!("../../data/hardware.toml")).unwrap()
}

#[test]
fn lists_unknown_hardware_by_how_many_games_mention_it() {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let db = GameDb::create(&dir.path().join("games.db")).unwrap();
    db.store_catalog(&catalog()).unwrap();
    // Real requirement text: Baldur's Gate 3, a game with the same Adreno,
    // OMORI, and Cyberpunk 2077 (all known).
    let games = [
        (
            1086940,
            None,
            "Nvidia GTX 970 / RX 480 / Intel Arc A380 / Qualcomm Adreno X1 (4GB+ of VRAM)",
        ),
        (2, None, "GeForce GTX 1060 or Qualcomm Adreno X1"),
        (
            1150690,
            Some("Intel N4100 (or similar) or better"),
            "GeForce GTX 1060 6GB",
        ),
        (
            1091500,
            Some("Core i7-6700 or Ryzen 5 1600"),
            "GeForce GTX 1060 6GB or Radeon RX 580 8GB or Arc A380",
        ),
    ];
    for (app_id, cpu, gpu) in games {
        let record = GameRecord {
            app_id,
            name: format!("Game {app_id}"),
            minimum: Some(ParsedTier {
                cpu: cpu.map(str::to_owned),
                gpu: Some(gpu.to_owned()),
                ..ParsedTier::default()
            }),
            ..GameRecord::default()
        };
        db.store(&record, &catalog()).unwrap();
    }

    let report = unmatched(&db, &catalog()).unwrap();

    assert_eq!(
        report,
        [
            Unmatched {
                kind: "gpu",
                text: "Qualcomm Adreno X1".to_owned(),
                games: 2
            },
            Unmatched {
                kind: "cpu",
                text: "Intel N4100".to_owned(),
                games: 1
            },
        ]
    );
}

`pipeline/tests/validate.rs`:

```rs
//! Tests for `validate`: what stops a games.db from being published.

use rigcheck_core::{Catalog, ParsedTier, ProtonTier};
use rigcheck_gamedb::{GameDb, GameRecord};
use rigcheck_pipeline::validate::{Problem, Rules, validate};
use tempfile::TempDir;

fn catalog() -> Catalog {
    Catalog::from_toml(include_str!("../../data/hardware.toml")).unwrap()
}

/// A requirement tier with CPU, GPU and RAM: "parsed".
fn parsed() -> ParsedTier {
    ParsedTier {
        cpu: Some("Core i5-4460".to_owned()),
        gpu: Some("GeForce GTX 970".to_owned()),
        ram_mb: Some(8192),
        ..ParsedTier::default()
    }
}

/// A games.db with `games` as (app ID, popularity, parsed?).
fn database(dir: &TempDir, games: &[(u32, u32, bool)]) -> GameDb {
    let db = GameDb::create(&dir.path().join("games.db")).unwrap();
    db.store_catalog(&catalog()).unwrap();
    let mut popularity = Vec::new();
    for &(app_id, reports, is_parsed) in games {
        let record = GameRecord {
            app_id,
            name: format!("Game {app_id}"),
            minimum: is_parsed.then(parsed),
            ..GameRecord::default()
        };
        db.store(&record, &catalog()).unwrap();
        popularity.push((app_id, Some(ProtonTier::Gold), reports));
    }
    db.set_protondb(&popularity).unwrap();
    db
}

const RULES: Rules = Rules {
    top: 10,
    min_parsed_share: 0.9,
    max_bytes: 50 * 1024 * 1024,
};

#[test]
fn a_database_whose_popular_games_are_parsed_passes() {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    // 9 of the top 10 parsed (90%); an unpopular game unparsed doesn't matter.
    let mut games: Vec<(u32, u32, bool)> = (1..=10).map(|id| (id, 1000 - id, id != 7)).collect();
    games.push((99, 1, false));
    let db = database(&dir, &games);

    assert_eq!(
        validate(&db, &dir.path().join("games.db"), &RULES).unwrap(),
        []
    );
}

#[test]
fn too_few_parsed_popular_games_fail() {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    // 8 of the top 10 parsed.
    let games: Vec<(u32, u32, bool)> = (1..=10).map(|id| (id, 1000 - id, id > 2)).collect();
    let db = database(&dir, &games);

    assert_eq!(
        validate(&db, &dir.path().join("games.db"), &RULES).unwrap(),
        [Problem::TooFewParsed { parsed: 8, top: 10 }]
    );
}

#[test]
fn a_database_over_the_size_limit_fails() {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let games: Vec<(u32, u32, bool)> = (1..=10).map(|id| (id, 1000 - id, true)).collect();
    let db = database(&dir, &games);
    let path = dir.path().join("games.db");
    let bytes = std::fs::metadata(&path).unwrap().len();
    let rules = Rules {
        max_bytes: bytes - 1,
        ..RULES
    };

    assert_eq!(
        validate(&db, &path, &rules).unwrap(),
        [Problem::TooBig {
            bytes,
            max: bytes - 1
        }]
    );
}

#[test]
fn an_empty_database_fails() {
    let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
    let db = database(&dir, &[]);

    assert_eq!(
        validate(&db, &dir.path().join("games.db"), &RULES).unwrap(),
        [Problem::NoGames]
    );
}
